**Components**

-   **Profile header:** User greeting, conversion status, last activity.

-   **Diagnostic card:** Score, disclaimer, answered/unanswered, time.

-   **Charts:** Specialty/difficulty breakdown (accessible with text
    alternatives).

-   **Confidence matrix:** 2x2 grid with footnote.

-   **Diagnostic weaknesses list:** Sortable, clickable (links to
    UKMLA-012 with canonical ID).

-   **Progress/mastery summaries:** Revision progress (if available),
    mastery counts.

-   **Recommendations slot:** UKMLA-012 integration point.

**Interactions**

-   Clicking diagnostic weakness topic → redirects to UKMLA-012 with
    canonical presentation_id or condition_id.

-   Scrolling dashboard → lazy-loads metrics (optional performance
    optimisation).

-   Anonymous user → sees diagnostic summary only (no revision
    progress/mastery/recommendations).

**5. Business Logic**

**Data Aggregation**

-   **Source of truth:** Use canonical data from UKMLA-008 (diagnostic
    sessions), UKMLA-009 (diagnostic results), UKMLA-010 (conversion
    status), UKMLA-007 (mastery), UKMLA-015/016 (revision progress).

-   **Do not recalculate diagnostic score or specialty breakdowns** ---
    fetch pre-computed data from UKMLA-009.

-   **Do not calculate/classify/alter mastery** --- read current mastery
    states from UKMLA-007 and perform only read-only counting/grouping
    for display.

-   **Calculate read-only derived aggregations:**

    -   Revision progress: Count questions answered, CPSA stations
        completed, weakness topics addressed (from ongoing practice, if
        available).

    -   Mastery summary: Count presentations/conditions
        mastered/learning (from UKMLA-007, read-only).

-   **Do not generate personalised recommendations** --- that is
    UKMLA-012\'s responsibility.

**Cache Management**

-   **Cache dashboard metrics** in dashboard_metrics table for fast
    retrieval (authenticated users only).

-   **Cache invalidation:**

    -   Use TTL + event-driven invalidation (not TTL alone).

    -   Invalidate cache when underlying canonical source changes (e.g.
        new diagnostic completed, mastery state changed).

    -   Check source_updated_at to determine if cache is stale relative
        to canonical source.

-   **Lazy-loading:** Optionally fetch specific metrics on-demand (e.g.
    /metrics/diagnostic_weaknesses).

**Anonymous vs Authenticated**

-   **Anonymous users:**

    -   See diagnostic summary only (no revision
        progress/mastery/recommendations).

    -   Diagnostic data read directly from UKMLA-009 (no
        dashboard_metrics cache).

    -   No candidate_profiles row.

    -   Conversion status shown (if applicable).

-   **Authenticated users:**

    -   See full dashboard (diagnostic, revision progress, mastery,
        recommendations slot).

    -   Use candidate_profiles and dashboard_metrics for cached data.

    -   Conversion status shown (if applicable).

**Diagnostic Weaknesses vs Current Weaknesses**

-   **Diagnostic weaknesses:** Derived from UKMLA-009 diagnostic results
    (snapshot at time of diagnostic).

-   **Current weaknesses:** Will be derived from ongoing practice
    (UKMLA-015/016, mastery system) in future iterations.

-   **011 displays diagnostic weaknesses** (from 009) --- clearly
    distinguished from future current weaknesses.

**6. Edge Cases**

**Error Handling**

-   **No diagnostic session:** Show message \"No diagnostic completed
    yet. Start your first diagnostic to see your performance.\"

-   **Dashboard metrics not yet computed:** Show loading state with
    message \"Loading your dashboard\...\" (should be rare if metrics
    cached).

-   **Network failure:** Retry logic (3 attempts), then show error
    \"Unable to load dashboard. Please try again.\"

-   **Cache stale relative to source:** Recalculate metrics on-demand
    (check source_updated_at).

**Empty States**

-   **No revision progress (not yet integrated):** Show \"Revision
    progress tracking coming soon.\"

-   **No mastery data (not yet integrated):** Show \"Mastery tracking
    coming soon.\"

**Data Integrity**

-   **Dashboard mismatch:** If dashboard_metrics doesn\'t match
    canonical data (e.g. due to bug), log error and show message
    \"Dashboard temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.\"

-   **Stale cache:** If cache expired or source_updated_at \>
    last_calculated_at, recalculate metrics on-demand.

**7. Permissions/Security**

**Access Control**

-   **Authentication required:** User must be authenticated (or
    anonymous session with valid diagnostic session).

-   **Authorization:** User can only access their own profile/dashboard.

-   **Read-only:** Dashboard data cannot be modified (no update/delete
    endpoints).

**Data Protection**

-   **PII:** User data encrypted at rest (per platform security
    architecture).

-   **Session management:** Follows UKMLA-000 (no separate dashboard
    token mechanism).

-   **Audit log:** Record dashboard access for governance (optional, if
    required).

**8. Analytics/Events**

**Tracking Events**

-   dashboard_viewed: {user_id, timestamp}

-   diagnostic_summary_clicked: {user_id, session_id, timestamp}

-   weakness_topic_clicked: {user_id, presentation_id, accuracy,
    timestamp}

-   recommendation_clicked: {user_id, action_type, target, timestamp}
    (when UKMLA-012 integrated)

**Metrics**

-   Dashboard view rate.

-   Time spent on dashboard.

-   Weakness topic click-through rate.

-   Recommendation click-through rate (when UKMLA-012 integrated).

**9. Acceptance Criteria**

-   **Given** an authenticated user with completed diagnostic, **when**
    they view dashboard, **then** diagnostic summary is displayed using
    canonical UKMLA-009 data.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they view dashboard,
    **then** specialty/difficulty breakdowns are displayed using
    canonical UKMLA-009 data.

-   **Given** an authenticated user with confidence ratings, **when**
    they view dashboard, **then** confidence calibration is displayed
    with threshold footnote (1--3 = uncertain, 4--5 = confident;
    self-reported, not validated).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they view dashboard,
    **then** diagnostic_weaknesses are displayed (lowest-accuracy
    GMC/content mapped entities from diagnostic).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they view dashboard,
    **then** revision_progress is displayed with status: \"available\"
    or status: \"not_available\" (if UKMLA-015/016 not yet integrated).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they view dashboard,
    **then** mastery_summary is displayed (read-only aggregation of
    UKMLA-007 mastery states).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they view dashboard,
    **then** recommendations_slot is displayed with status:
    \"unavailable\" (until UKMLA-012 integrated).

-   **Given** an anonymous user with completed diagnostic, **when** they
    view dashboard, **then** diagnostic summary is displayed (no
    revision progress/mastery/recommendations).

-   **Given** an anonymous user, **when** they view dashboard, **then**
    conversion status is displayed (if applicable).

-   **Given** a user with no diagnostic session, **when** they view
    dashboard, **then** message shown (\"No diagnostic completed yet\").

-   **Given** a user with stale cache, **when** they view dashboard,
    **then** metrics recalculated on-demand (check source_updated_at).

-   **Given** a dashboard mismatch, **when** user views dashboard,
    **then** error logged and message shown (\"Dashboard temporarily
    unavailable\").

-   **Given** a diagnostic weakness topic clicked, **when** user clicks,
    **then** redirected to UKMLA-012 with canonical presentation_id or
    condition_id.

-   **Given** a dashboard view, **when** user views, **then** analytics
    event tracked (dashboard_viewed).

-   **Given** an anonymous user, **when** they view dashboard, **then**
    no candidate_profiles row is created/used.

-   **Given** an anonymous user, **when** they view dashboard, **then**
    no dashboard_metrics cache is used (diagnostic read directly from
    UKMLA-009).

-   **Given** a cache invalidation event, **when** underlying canonical
    source changes, **then** cache invalidated (event-driven, not TTL
    alone).

-   **Given** a GET /candidate/profile request, **when** it is
    processed, **then** last_activity_at is not updated as side effect
    (derived asynchronously from canonical activity records).

**10. Dependencies**

-   **UKMLA-000:** Authentication and user identity (required for access
    control).

-   **UKMLA-008:** Diagnostic Engine (upstream --- provides diagnostic
    session data).

-   **UKMLA-009:** Diagnostic Results Page (upstream --- provides
    canonical diagnostic results).

-   **UKMLA-010:** Diagnostic Conversion Flow (upstream --- provides
    conversion status).

-   **UKMLA-007:** Mastery Calculation Engine (upstream --- provides
    mastery states).

-   **UKMLA-012:** Recommendation Engine (downstream --- generates
    personalised next steps).

-   **UKMLA-015/016:** Revision practice/Weakness Loop (upstream ---
    provides revision progress, if available).

**12. Clinical/Governance Requirements**

**Clinical Content**

-   **No clinical content** in dashboard (purely aggregations of
    diagnostic/revision data).

**Governance**

-   **Read-only:** Dashboard data cannot be modified (no update/delete
    endpoints).

-   **Audit trail:** Dashboard access logged (if required for
    governance).

-   **Cache management:** Dashboard metrics cached for performance
    (TTL + event-driven invalidation), but always rebuildable from
    canonical data.

-   **Clinical content rules vs engineering rules:**

    -   ✅ Engineering implements: dashboard aggregation, cache
        management, access control.

    -   ❌ Engineering does not invent/alter: clinical answers, scoring
        rules, mastery thresholds.

    -   ✅ Governed content: Diagnostic results, mastery thresholds
        (require clinical/educational approval).

    -   ✅ Engineering responsibility: Implement governed rules
        correctly, with proper versioning and audit.

**Disclaimer**

-   Diagnostic score is a snapshot of performance on this diagnostic
    assessment, not a prediction of UKMLA result.

-   Dashboard aggregations are behavioural telemetry, not validated
    measures of candidate ability.

-   Confidence calibration is a self-reported indicator, not a validated
    psychometric measure.

**UKMLA-012 --- Recommendation Engine (\"What should I do today?\")
(Full Engineering Specification)**

**1. User Story**

**As an** AMaC candidate (authenticated),\
**I want to** receive personalised, actionable recommendations on what
to study or practise next,\
**so that** I can focus my revision time efficiently on the areas that
will most improve my performance.

**2. Data/Schema**

**Tables**

**recommendations** (personalised recommendations generated for
candidate)

-   id (PK, UUID)

-   user_id (FK to users.id, indexed, not null)

-   recommendation_type (enum: weakness_focus, specialty_practice,
    difficulty_practice, confidence_calibration, mastery_progress,
    revision_plan, not null)

-   priority_score (decimal, not null, e.g. 0.0--1.0) --- higher score =
    higher priority.

-   subject_type (enum: presentation, condition, specialty, difficulty,
    not null) --- canonical entity type for recommendation focus.

-   subject_id (UUID, nullable) --- canonical entity ID (e.g.
    presentation_id, condition_id).

-   action_type (enum: start_revision, review_explanations,
    practise_timing, focus_clinical_reasoning, retest_weakness, not
    null) --- recommended action.

-   reason_json (JSON, not null) --- structured explanation for
    recommendation (e.g. {\"diagnostic_accuracy\": 0.45,
    \"question_count\": 11, \"source\": \"diagnostic_weakness\"}).

-   metadata_json (JSON, nullable) --- additional context (e.g.
    {\"specialty\": \"Cardiology\", \"difficulty\": \"Hard\"}).

-   expires_at (timestamp, nullable) --- recommendation expiry (e.g. 7
    days).

-   is_active (boolean, default true) --- whether recommendation is
    still relevant.

-   created_at (timestamp, not null)

-   updated_at (timestamp, not null)

-   Index: (user_id, is_active, priority_score DESC)

-   Index: (user_id, recommendation_type)

**recommendation_events** (audit trail for recommendation interactions)

-   id (PK, UUID)

-   recommendation_id (FK to recommendations.id, indexed, not null)

-   event_type (enum: recommendation_generated,
    recommendation_displayed, recommendation_clicked,
    recommendation_dismissed, recommendation_completed, not null)

-   metadata_json (JSON, nullable) --- e.g. {action_type:
    \"start_revision\", subject_type: \"presentation\"}

-   timestamp (timestamp, not null)

-   created_at (timestamp, not null)

-   Index: (recommendation_id, event_type, timestamp)

**Migrations**

-   Create recommendations table with above schema (personalised
    recommendations with priority scoring, canonical subject entities).

-   Create recommendation_events table for audit trail.

-   Add foreign key constraints for user_id, recommendation_id.

-   Add indexes for performance (user_id lookup, priority sorting, event
    tracking).

**3. API/Backend**

**Endpoints**

**GET /api/v1/recommendations/next**

-   **Request:** {} (user authenticated)

-   **Response:**

-   {

-   \"recommendations\": \[

-   {

-   \"id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"recommendation_type\": \"weakness_focus\",

-   \"priority_score\": 0.92,

-   \"subject_type\": \"presentation\",

-   \"subject_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"action_type\": \"start_revision\",

-   \"title\": \"Focus on Chest pain\",

-   \"reason\": \"Low accuracy (45%) across 11 diagnostic questions\",

-   \"reason_json\": {

-   \"diagnostic_accuracy\": 0.45,

-   \"question_count\": 11,

-   \"source\": \"diagnostic_weakness\"

-   },

-   \"metadata_json\": {

-   \"specialty\": \"Cardiology\"

-   },

-   \"expires_at\": \"2026-10-14T14:00:00Z\",

-   \"is_active\": true

-   },

-   {

-   \"id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"recommendation_type\": \"difficulty_practice\",

-   \"priority_score\": 0.78,

-   \"subject_type\": \"difficulty\",

-   \"subject_id\": null,

-   \"action_type\": \"review_explanations\",

-   \"title\": \"Review hard questions\",

-   \"reason\": \"5/9 correct on hard difficulty questions\",

-   \"reason_json\": {

-   \"difficulty_accuracy\": 0.56,

-   \"question_count\": 9,

-   \"source\": \"diagnostic_difficulty\"

-   },

-   \"metadata_json\": {

-   \"difficulty\": \"Hard\"

-   },

-   \"expires_at\": \"2026-10-14T14:00:00Z\",

-   \"is_active\": true

-   }

-   \]

}

-   **Business logic:**

    -   Validate user is authenticated.

    -   **Fetch diagnostic findings** from UKMLA-009
        (diagnostic_weaknesses, specialty_breakdown,
        difficulty_breakdown, confidence_calibration).

    -   **Fetch mastery states** from UKMLA-007
        (presentations/conditions mastered/learning).

    -   **Fetch revision progress** from UKMLA-015/016 (questions
        answered, CPSA stations completed, weakness topics addressed).

    -   **Generate recommendations:**

        -   **Weakness focus:** Lowest-accuracy diagnostic weaknesses
            (e.g. Chest pain 45% accuracy).

        -   **Specialty practice:** Lowest-accuracy specialties from
            diagnostic.

        -   **Difficulty practice:** Lowest-accuracy difficulty levels
            from diagnostic.

        -   **Confidence calibration:** High incorrect+confident count →
            focus on clinical reasoning.

        -   **Mastery progress:** Presentations/conditions in
            \"learning\" state → practise to achieve mastery.

        -   **Revision plan:** Combine diagnostic findings, mastery
            states, revision progress into prioritised plan.

    -   **Calculate priority scores:**

        -   Based on accuracy (lower = higher priority), question count
            (higher = more evidence), mastery state (learning = higher
            priority), time since last practice (older = higher
            priority).

        -   Normalise to 0.0--1.0 scale.

    -   **Store recommendations** in recommendations table.

    -   Return top N recommendations (e.g. 3--5) sorted by
        priority_score DESC.

**POST /api/v1/recommendations/{recommendation_id}/interact**

-   **Request:**

-   {

-   \"event_type\": \"recommendation_clicked\",

-   \"metadata_json\": {\"action_type\": \"start_revision\"}

}

-   **Response:**

-   {

-   \"recommendation_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"event_type\": \"recommendation_clicked\",

-   \"timestamp\": \"2026-10-07T14:00:00Z\"

}

-   **Business logic:**

    -   Validate recommendation exists and belongs to authenticated
        user.

    -   Log recommendation_events record.

    -   Return event confirmation.

**GET /api/v1/recommendations/why/{recommendation_id}**

-   **Request:** {} (user authenticated)

-   **Response:**

-   {

-   \"recommendation_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"why_json\": {

-   \"diagnostic_accuracy\": 0.45,

-   \"question_count\": 11,

-   \"source\": \"diagnostic_weakness\",

-   \"presentation_name\": \"Chest pain\",

-   \"specialty\": \"Cardiology\",

-   \"explanation\": \"You scored 45% accuracy on Chest pain questions
    in your diagnostic assessment (5/11 correct). This is below your
    overall diagnostic score of 69%. Focusing on this topic will help
    improve your clinical reasoning and knowledge in Cardiology.\"

-   }

}

-   **Business logic:**

    -   Validate recommendation exists and belongs to authenticated
        user.

    -   Fetch reason_json, metadata_json from recommendations.

    -   Generate human-readable explanation from structured data.

    -   Return \"why\" explanation for transparency.

**Validation**

-   User must be authenticated.

-   User can only access their own recommendations.

-   Recommendations are read-only (no update/delete endpoints, only
    interaction events).

-   Priority scores must be in range 0.0--1.0.

-   subject_type/subject_id must be valid canonical entities
    (presentation, condition, specialty, difficulty).

**4. Frontend/UI**

**Screens**

**Recommendations Slot (in UKMLA-011 Dashboard)**

-   Display:

    -   \"Your next step\" header.

    -   List of recommendations (sorted by priority):

        -   **Focus on Chest pain** (priority: 92%)

            -   Reason: \"Low accuracy (45%) across 11 diagnostic
                questions\"

            -   Action button: \"Start revision\"

            -   \"Why this?\" link → shows detailed explanation.

        -   **Review hard questions** (priority: 78%)

            -   Reason: \"5/9 correct on hard difficulty questions\"

            -   Action button: \"Review explanations\"

            -   \"Why this?\" link.

    -   \"Dismiss\" button for each recommendation (optional, if product
        allows dismissal).

-   State: Loading (fetching recommendations), Ready (recommendations
    displayed), Unavailable (no recommendations yet).

**\"Why this?\" Modal**

-   Display:

    -   \"Why are you seeing this recommendation?\"

    -   Detailed explanation:

        -   \"You scored 45% accuracy on Chest pain questions in your
            diagnostic assessment (5/11 correct). This is below your
            overall diagnostic score of 69%. Focusing on this topic will
            help improve your clinical reasoning and knowledge in
            Cardiology.\"

    -   \"Close\" button.

-   State: Loading (fetching explanation), Ready (explanation
    displayed).

**Components**

-   **Recommendation card:** Title, reason, priority score, action
    button, \"Why this?\" link.

-   **\"Why this?\" modal:** Detailed explanation from why_json.

-   **Dismiss button:** Optional (if product allows dismissal).

**Interactions**

-   Clicking action button → redirects to appropriate practice mode
    (UKMLA-015 Learning Mode, UKMLA-016 Weakness Loop, etc.) with
    subject_type/subject_id as focus.

-   Clicking \"Why this?\" → opens modal with detailed explanation.

-   Clicking dismiss → hides recommendation (optional, logs
    recommendation_dismissed event).

**5. Business Logic**

**Recommendation Generation**

-   **Source of truth:** Use canonical data from UKMLA-009 (diagnostic
    findings), UKMLA-007 (mastery states), UKMLA-015/016 (revision
    progress).

-   **Do not recalculate diagnostic findings or mastery states** ---
    fetch from canonical sources.

-   **Generate recommendations based on:**

    -   **Diagnostic weaknesses:** Lowest-accuracy
        presentations/conditions from diagnostic.

    -   **Specialty breakdown:** Lowest-accuracy specialties.

    -   **Difficulty breakdown:** Lowest-accuracy difficulty levels.

    -   **Confidence calibration:** High incorrect+confident count →
        clinical reasoning focus.

    -   **Mastery states:** Presentations/conditions in \"learning\"
        state → practise to achieve mastery.

    -   **Revision progress:** Topics not practised recently →
        prioritise for revision.

-   **Calculate priority scores:**

    -   Accuracy weight: Lower accuracy = higher priority (e.g. 45%
        accuracy → 0.92 priority).

    -   Question count weight: Higher question count = more evidence =
        higher priority.

    -   Mastery state weight: \"Learning\" state = higher priority than
        \"mastered\".

    -   Recency weight: Older last practice = higher priority.

    -   Normalise to 0.0--1.0 scale.

-   **Store recommendations** in recommendations table with
    priority_score, reason_json, metadata_json.

**Recommendation Types**

-   **weakness_focus:** Focus on lowest-accuracy diagnostic weakness
    (presentation/condition).

-   **specialty_practice:** Focus on lowest-accuracy specialty.

-   **difficulty_practice:** Focus on lowest-accuracy difficulty level.

-   **confidence_calibration:** High incorrect+confident → focus on
    clinical reasoning.

-   **mastery_progress:** Practise topics in \"learning\" mastery state.

-   **revision_plan:** Combined prioritised plan from all sources.

**Action Types**

-   **start_revision:** Start targeted revision on topic (links to
    UKMLA-015 Learning Mode).

-   **review_explanations:** Review explanations for incorrect questions
    (links to UKMLA-015 Learning Mode).

-   **practise_timing:** Focus on timing practice (links to UKMLA-015
    Exam Mode).

-   **focus_clinical_reasoning:** Focus on clinical reasoning (links to
    UKMLA-016 Weakness Loop).

-   **retest_weakness:** Retest previously weak topic (links to
    UKMLA-016 Weakness Loop).

**Recommendation Expiry**

-   Recommendations expire after configurable duration (e.g. 7 days).

-   Expired recommendations marked is_active = false.

-   New recommendations generated on next dashboard load.

**6. Edge Cases**

**Error Handling**

-   **No diagnostic findings:** Show message \"Complete a diagnostic
    assessment to receive personalised recommendations.\"

-   **No mastery data:** Show message \"Complete more questions to
    receive mastery-based recommendations.\"

-   **Network failure:** Retry logic (3 attempts), then show error
    \"Unable to load recommendations. Please try again.\"

**Empty States**

-   **No recommendations yet:** Show message \"Recommendations will
    appear here once you have completed a diagnostic assessment.\"

**Data Integrity**

-   **Recommendation mismatch:** If recommendations doesn\'t match
    canonical data (e.g. due to bug), log error and regenerate
    recommendations.

-   **Stale recommendations:** If recommendations expired, regenerate on
    next dashboard load.

**7. Permissions/Security**

**Access Control**

-   **Authentication required:** User must be authenticated.

-   **Authorization:** User can only access their own recommendations.

-   **Read-only:** Recommendations cannot be modified (only interaction
    events logged).

**Data Protection**

-   **PII:** User data encrypted at rest (per platform security
    architecture).

-   **Session management:** Follows UKMLA-000 (no separate
    recommendation token mechanism).

-   **Audit log:** All recommendation interactions logged for
    governance.

**8. Analytics/Events**

**Tracking Events**

-   recommendation_generated: {user_id, recommendation_type,
    priority_score, timestamp}

-   recommendation_displayed: {user_id, recommendation_id, timestamp}

-   recommendation_clicked: {user_id, recommendation_id, action_type,
    timestamp}

-   recommendation_dismissed: {user_id, recommendation_id, timestamp}

-   recommendation_completed: {user_id, recommendation_id, timestamp}

**Metrics**

-   Recommendation click-through rate.

-   Recommendation completion rate.

-   Average priority score of clicked recommendations.

-   Time from recommendation displayed to clicked.

-   Dismissal rate.

**9. Acceptance Criteria**

-   **Given** an authenticated user with diagnostic findings, **when**
    they request recommendations, **then** recommendations are generated
    based on diagnostic weaknesses, specialty/difficulty breakdowns,
    confidence calibration.

-   **Given** an authenticated user with mastery states, **when** they
    request recommendations, **then** recommendations include
    mastery-progress recommendations (topics in \"learning\" state).

-   **Given** an authenticated user with revision progress, **when**
    they request recommendations, **then** recommendations account for
    recency (topics not practised recently prioritised).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they request
    recommendations, **then** recommendations are sorted by
    priority_score DESC.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they click recommendation
    action button, **then** they are redirected to appropriate practice
    mode (UKMLA-015/016) with subject_type/subject_id as focus.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they click \"Why this?\",
    **then** detailed explanation is displayed from why_json.

-   **Given** an authenticated user with no diagnostic findings,
    **when** they request recommendations, **then** message shown
    (\"Complete a diagnostic assessment to receive personalised
    recommendations\").

-   **Given** an authenticated user with expired recommendations,
    **when** they request recommendations, **then** new recommendations
    are generated.

-   **Given** a recommendation interaction, **when** it occurs, **then**
    recommendation_events record is logged.

-   **Given** a recommendation, **when** it is generated, **then**
    priority_score is in range 0.0--1.0.

-   **Given** a recommendation, **when** it is generated, **then**
    subject_type/subject_id are valid canonical entities.

-   **Given** a user, **when** they request recommendations, **then**
    only their own recommendations are returned (authorization).

**12. Clinical/Governance Requirements**

**Clinical Content**

-   **No clinical content** in recommendations (purely aggregations of
    diagnostic/mastery/revision data).

**Governance**

-   **Read-only:** Recommendations cannot be modified (only interaction
    events logged).

-   **Audit trail:** All recommendation interactions logged for
    governance.

-   **Clinical content rules vs engineering rules:**

    -   ✅ Engineering implements: recommendation generation, priority
        scoring, interaction tracking.

    -   ❌ Engineering does not invent/alter: clinical answers,
        diagnostic findings, mastery thresholds.

    -   ✅ Governed content: Diagnostic findings, mastery thresholds
        (require clinical/educational approval).

    -   ✅ Engineering responsibility: Implement governed rules
        correctly, with proper versioning and audit.

**Disclaimer**

-   Recommendations are personalised suggestions based on diagnostic
    performance, mastery states and revision progress.

-   Recommendations are not validated measures of candidate ability or
    guaranteed to improve performance.

-   Candidates should use recommendations as guidance, not prescriptive
    rules.
