**Status: AMEND --- not frozen yet**

These are **implementation-level corrections, not a change to the
architecture**.

Once you incorporate those changes, I would expect:

**UKMLA-014 --- GMC Content Map Coverage Engine & Candidate Coverage
View**\
**FINAL ENGINEERING SPECIFICATION --- FROZEN / APPROVED**

And then we can move cleanly to **UKMLA-015 --- Learning Mode vs Exam
Mode (AKT)**.

Yes. I have **triple-checked it against the current GMC MLA/PLAB
position and NICE acute pancreatitis guidance**, rather than relying on
the general clinical assessment I gave previously.

**PLAB-NEW-155 --- AMEND**

**Overall:** The station is clinically sound and worth keeping, but I
would make **a few targeted amendments before publishing it on AMaC**.

Importantly, I would **not** make the extensive changes I suggested in
my previous response. On re-checking the actual NICE recommendations,
several parts of your original station are already exactly right.

**1. Title --- AMEND**

\"The Upper Abdominal Pain\"

This is unnatural English.

Use:

**\"Acute Upper Abdominal Pain\"**

or, if you want the diagnosis less obvious:

**\"Severe Epigastric Pain\"**

I prefer **Acute Upper Abdominal Pain**.

**2. Exam --- CORRECT**

\"exam\": \[\"UKMLA CPSA\", \"PLAB 2\"\]

This is actually reasonable.

The GMC confirms that **PLAB 2 meets the MLA CPSA requirements**, and
PLAB 2 itself is an 8-minute CPSA. ([General Medical
Council](https://www.gmc-uk.org/education/medical-licensing-assessment/plab-and-the-mla?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

So I would **not remove either label**.

For AMaC wording, however, I would describe it as a **PLAB 2 / UKMLA
CPSA-style station**, rather than suggesting it is an official GMC
station.

**3. Station type --- CORRECT**

\"Acute abdominal assessment / investigation interpretation\"

Good.

This fits the actual PLAB 2 domains particularly well: data
gathering/assessment, investigations leading to diagnosis and clinical
management. ([General Medical
Council](https://www.gmc-uk.org/registration-and-licensing/join-our-registers/plab/plab-2-guide/how-will-you-be-tested?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

**4. Duration --- CORRECT**

\"durationMinutes\": 8

Exactly appropriate for a PLAB 2-style station. GMC states that PLAB 2
scenarios are **8 minutes each**. ([General Medical
Council](https://www.gmc-uk.org/registration-and-licensing/join-our-registers/plab/plab-2-guide/what-is-the-plab-2-exam?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

**5. Candidate task --- AMEND SLIGHTLY**

Current:

\"Assess the patient, identify the likely diagnosis and explain your
immediate management.\"

This is acceptable, but I would make the severity component explicit
because it is one of the important clinical objectives.

**Better:**

**\"Assess the patient, identify the likely diagnosis, assess the
severity and explain your immediate management.\"**

That is a meaningful improvement without making the task unnecessarily
complicated.

**6. Initial information --- CORRECT**

Severe upper abdominal pain\
Radiation through to the back\
Vomiting

Good classic acute pancreatitis presentation.

NICE specifically describes sudden-onset abdominal pain,
nausea/vomiting, epigastric tenderness and tachycardia as typical
features.
([NICE](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng104/chapter/Recommendations))

**7. History --- CORRECT, with one useful addition**

Your history is good:

-   onset/progression

-   site/character

-   radiation

-   vomiting

-   fever/rigors

-   previous episodes

-   gallstones

-   alcohol

-   medications

-   previous pancreatic disease

-   cardiovascular symptoms

-   bowel/urinary symptoms

I would **keep it**.

One thing I would add:

**Previous gallbladder disease / biliary colic**

That makes the gallstone aetiology investigation more clinically
natural.

Your instruction:

\"Do not assume alcohol is the cause simply because the patient drinks
alcohol.\"

is particularly good.

In fact, this directly mirrors NICE:

**\"Do not assume that a person\'s acute pancreatitis is alcohol-related
just because they drink alcohol.\"**
([NICE](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng104/chapter/Recommendations))

**Verdict: CORRECT with minor addition.**

**8. Examination finding --- CORRECT**

\"The patient is tachycardic and uncomfortable. There is epigastric
tenderness without obvious peritonism.\"

Good.

It gives the candidate enough to recognise pancreatitis while avoiding
an unrealistically dramatic examination.

**9. Lipase --- CORRECT, but I would improve the examiner finding**

Your current:

\"Serum lipase is substantially raised.\"

is clinically acceptable.

And your key issue correctly says that lipase can be raised in other
conditions. NICE explicitly states this.
([NICE](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng104/chapter/Recommendations))

However, for an educational station, I\'d make the result more
interpretable:

**\"Serum lipase is more than three times the upper limit of normal.\"**

That teaches the candidate something useful without requiring them to
memorise a particular numerical value.

**Verdict: AMEND slightly.**

**10. Key issue --- CORRECT**

This is one of the strongest parts:

\"The presentation is consistent with acute pancreatitis. The candidate
should recognise the diagnosis while still assessing severity and
considering alternative causes\...\"

Exactly right.

And:

\"A raised lipase or amylase supports the diagnosis but can occur in
other conditions, so the result must be interpreted in clinical
context.\"

Also correct and supported by NICE.
([NICE](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng104/chapter/Recommendations))

**Keep.**

**11. Diagnosis explanation --- CORRECT**

Your proposed wording is good:

\"I\'m concerned that you have acute pancreatitis\...\"

It appropriately says:

-   likely diagnosis

-   evidence

-   need to establish cause

-   need to assess severity

That\'s exactly the sort of patient-centred explanation that fits the
GMC\'s current MLA emphasis on **safe practice, managing uncertainty and
person-centred care**. ([General Medical
Council](https://www.gmc-uk.org/education/medical-licensing-assessment/mla-content-map?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

**Keep.**

**12. Cause --- CORRECT**

Your list:

-   gallstones

-   alcohol

-   medicines

-   previous pancreatitis

-   metabolic/less common causes

is good.

NICE specifically identifies metabolic causes, prescription drugs,
microlithiasis, hereditary causes, autoimmune pancreatitis and
pancreatic/ampullary tumours among other possible causes when gallstones
and alcohol have been excluded.
([NICE](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng104/chapter/Recommendations))

Your station doesn\'t need to force candidates to list every rare cause.

**Keep.**

**13. Immediate management --- AMEND**

This is the **main area I would strengthen**.

Current:

Hospital management with appropriate clinical assessment and monitoring\
Analgesia and antiemetic treatment\
Appropriate fluid management\
Blood tests and investigation of cause\
Nutritional management\...

This is broadly right, but I\'d make the first item more explicit:

**\"ABCDE assessment, appropriate monitoring and assessment for organ
dysfunction/severity.\"**

Then:

**\"Appropriate IV fluid management with regular reassessment.\"**

NICE directs clinicians to its IV-fluid guidance for fluid resuscitation
in acute pancreatitis.
([NICE](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng104/chapter/Recommendations))

I would **not** specify a fixed fluid volume or aggressive fluid regimen
in this station.

Your original decision not to embed fluid volumes is therefore **good**.

**14. Nutrition --- CORRECT**

This is where I want to correct something from my previous answer:
**your original wording is already excellent.**

You wrote:

\"food should not routinely be withheld unless there is a clear reason
such as vomiting\"

That is essentially NICE\'s recommendation:

People with acute pancreatitis should **not be made nil-by-mouth and
should not have food withheld unless there is a clear reason, such as
vomiting.**
([NICE](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng104/chapter/Recommendations))

So:

**KEEP THIS EXACTLY AS A CORE AMaC TEACHING POINT.**

The curveball is also excellent.

**15. Curveball --- nil by mouth --- CORRECT**

Excellent.

It tests a genuinely outdated misconception without making the station
artificially difficult.

**Keep.**

**16. Curveball --- alcohol --- CORRECT**

Also excellent.

The expected response is appropriately non-judgemental.

It also reinforces an explicit NICE recommendation not to assume alcohol
is the cause simply because the patient drinks.
([NICE](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng104/chapter/Recommendations))

**Keep.**

**17. Safety-critical --- CORRECT**

Your list is strong:

-   recognise potentially serious illness

-   assess physiological state

-   don\'t anchor on alcohol

-   don\'t interpret lipase in isolation

-   investigate cause

-   don\'t routinely prescribe prophylactic antibiotics

The final point is directly supported by NICE:

**Do not offer prophylactic antimicrobials to people with acute
pancreatitis.**
([NICE](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng104/chapter/Recommendations))

**Keep all six.**

**18. Severity assessment --- AMEND**

This is the biggest substantive gap.

You mention:

\"Assessment of severity\"

and:

\"assess severity\"

but there isn\'t enough in the station to tell the candidate **how**.

I would add to candidateShouldEstablish:

**\"Assess physiological severity, including haemodynamic status,
respiratory status, mental state and evidence of organ dysfunction.\"**

You don\'t need to turn this into a Glasgow-Imrie/BISAP scoring
exercise.

For this type of station, the important thing is that the candidate
recognises that pancreatitis is not simply:

**pain + high lipase = diagnosis + discharge.**

NICE defines severe acute pancreatitis by **persistent organ failure**,
while moderately severe disease involves transient organ failure and/or
local/systemic complications.
([NICE](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng104/chapter/Recommendations))

**19. Differential diagnosis --- AMEND**

This is another place where I would make a modest improvement.

Your station says the candidate should consider alternative causes, but
doesn\'t identify them.

For **severe upper abdominal pain radiating to the back**, I would
expect the candidate to remain alert to important alternatives such as:

-   perforated peptic ulcer

-   acute biliary disease

-   acute coronary syndrome

-   aortic pathology

-   other acute abdominal pathology

You don\'t need to make candidates recite a differential. But the
examiner guidance can make clear that **anchoring on pancreatitis is
undesirable**, particularly before assessment of the whole patient.

This also fits the GMC\'s emphasis on managing uncertainty. ([General
Medical
Council](https://www.gmc-uk.org/education/medical-licensing-assessment/mla-content-map?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

**20. Sources --- AMEND**

Your:

\"sources\": \[\"NICE guideline on acute pancreatitis\"\]

is too vague for your production database.

I\'d change it to something like:

**\"NICE NG104 --- Pancreatitis: diagnosis and management\"**

The current NICE recommendations page identifies NG104 and contains the
relevant recommendations on diagnosis, aetiology, antibiotics, fluids
and nutrition.
([NICE](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng104/chapter/Recommendations))

One important point: **NICE NG104 was last updated in December 2020**,
so I would not describe it on AMaC as a newly updated guideline.
([NICE](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng104/chapter/Recommendations))

**21. Release notes --- AMEND**

Your current:

\"Distinct from upper GI bleeding, pyelonephritis, ascites, appendicitis
and obstructive jaundice stations.\"

I\'d change this.

The more useful neighbouring differential stations are:

**\"Distinct from upper GI bleeding, perforated peptic ulcer, acute
biliary disease, acute coronary syndrome and other causes of severe
upper abdominal pain.\"**

\"Ascites\" isn\'t really a particularly useful competing diagnosis for
this presentation.

**Final AMaC verdict**

**PLAB-NEW-155 --- AMEND**

**Keep**

-   Acute pancreatitis as the diagnosis

-   8-minute format

-   epigastric pain radiating to back

-   vomiting

-   tachycardia/epigastric tenderness

-   lipase interpretation

-   gallstone + alcohol assessment

-   **don\'t assume alcohol**

-   **don\'t routinely use prophylactic antibiotics**

-   **don\'t routinely make patients nil-by-mouth**

-   non-judgemental alcohol communication

-   AMaC principle

**Amend**

1.  **Title**

2.  Slightly improve candidate task

3.  Make lipase **\>3× ULN**

4.  Strengthen **severity/organ dysfunction assessment**

5.  Add a small amount of differential guidance

6.  Make immediate management more explicitly ABCDE/monitoring-focused

7.  Improve source citation

8.  Replace the release-note differential list

**My revised score**

**Clinical accuracy: 9/10**\
**Current-practice alignment: 9/10**\
**PLAB 2 / CPSA suitability: 9/10**\
**Educational value: 9/10**

**Overall: 9/10 after minor amendments.**

So I **would not reject this question**. It is a good AMaC station that
needs **polishing rather than rebuilding**.

And after checking the current GMC position, one thing is particularly
reassuring for your database: **PLAB 2 is explicitly a CPSA, lasts 8
minutes per scenario, and is now compliant with the MLA requirements;
PLAB 2 questions/stations are based on the MLA content map.** ([General
Medical
Council](https://www.gmc-uk.org/education/medical-licensing-assessment/plab-and-the-mla?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

**UKMLA-014 --- GMC Content Map Coverage Engine & Candidate Coverage
View (Revised Engineering Specification)**

**1. User Story**

**As an** AMaC candidate (authenticated),\
**I want to** see how much of the current GMC MLA Content Map I have
covered across presentations, conditions and capabilities,\
**so that** I can identify gaps in my revision and understand which
areas of the blueprint I have not yet meaningfully attempted.

**2. Data/Schema**

**Tables**

**gmc_coverage_snapshots** (candidate\'s coverage snapshot of GMC
Content Map)

-   id (PK, UUID)

-   user_id (FK to users.id, indexed, not null)

-   gmc_map_version (string, not null, e.g. \"v2024.1\") --- version of
    GMC MLA Content Map at snapshot time.

-   coverage_config_version (string, not null, e.g. \"v1.0\") ---
    version of coverage configuration (evidence threshold, eligible
    attempt rules) at snapshot time.

-   mastery_model_version (string, nullable) --- version of mastery
    model used for snapshot (from UKMLA-007).

-   presentations_total (integer, not null) --- total presentations in
    GMC map.

-   presentations_covered (integer, not null) --- presentations with
    attempt_count \>= evidence_threshold.

-   presentations_partial (integer, not null) --- presentations with 1
    \<= attempt_count \< evidence_threshold.

-   presentations_not_attempted (integer, not null) --- presentations
    with attempt_count = 0.

-   conditions_total (integer, not null) --- total conditions in GMC
    map.

-   conditions_covered (integer, not null) --- conditions with
    attempt_count \>= evidence_threshold.

-   conditions_partial (integer, not null) --- conditions with 1 \<=
    attempt_count \< evidence_threshold.

-   conditions_not_attempted (integer, not null) --- conditions with
    attempt_count = 0.

-   capabilities_total (integer, not null) --- total capabilities in GMC
    map.

-   capabilities_covered (integer, not null) --- capabilities with
    attempt_count \>= evidence_threshold.

-   capabilities_partial (integer, not null) --- capabilities with 1 \<=
    attempt_count \< evidence_threshold.

-   capabilities_not_attempted (integer, not null) --- capabilities with
    attempt_count = 0.

-   snapshot_created_at (timestamp, not null) --- when snapshot was
    generated.

-   created_at (timestamp, not null)

-   Index: (user_id, snapshot_created_at DESC)

-   Index: (user_id, gmc_map_version)

-   Index: (coverage_config_version)

**gmc_coverage_details** (detailed coverage breakdown by entity type)

-   id (PK, UUID)

-   snapshot_id (FK to gmc_coverage_snapshots.id, indexed, not null)

-   entity_type (enum: presentation, condition, capability, not null)

-   entity_id (UUID, not null) --- canonical entity ID from
    UKMLA-001/003.

-   entity_name (string, not null) --- e.g. \"Chest pain\", \"Acute
    coronary syndrome\", \"Managing uncertainty\".

-   coverage_status (enum: covered, partial, not_attempted, not null)
    --- whether candidate has attempted related questions/stations.

-   attempt_count (integer, not null, default 0) --- number of eligible
    attempted questions/stations mapped to this entity.

-   last_attempted_at (timestamp, nullable) --- timestamp of most recent
    eligible attempt.

-   mastery_state (string, nullable) --- mastery state from
    authoritative mastery system at snapshot time (e.g. \"secure\",
    \"learning\", \"not_demonstrated\", \"not_available\").

-   mastery_state_source (string, nullable) --- authoritative system
    used (e.g. \"UKMLA-007\", \"UKMLA-027\", null if not available).

-   created_at (timestamp, not null)

-   Index: (snapshot_id, entity_type, entity_id)

-   Index: (snapshot_id, coverage_status)

-   **Unique constraint:** UNIQUE(snapshot_id, entity_type, entity_id)
    --- guarantees one detail row per canonical entity within a
    snapshot.

**coverage_config** (versioned configuration for coverage calculation)

-   id (PK, UUID)

-   version (string, unique, not null, e.g. \"v1.0\")

-   effective_from (timestamp, not null)

-   effective_to (timestamp, nullable)

-   configuration_json (JSON, not null) --- e.g.
    {\"evidence_threshold\": 5, \"eligible_attempt_types\":
    \[\"learning\", \"exam\", \"repeat\", \"retest\"\],
    \"excluded_attempt_types\": \[\"diagnostic\", \"abandoned\"\]}

-   approved_by (FK to users.id, not null) --- **must reference user
    with required AMaC product/educational governance permission**
    (authorisation enforced at application/service layer).

-   approved_at (timestamp, not null)

-   change_reason (text, nullable)

-   Index: (version)

-   Index: (effective_from, effective_to)

**Migrations**

-   Create gmc_coverage_snapshots table with above schema (including
    coverage_config_version, mastery_model_version).

-   Create gmc_coverage_details table for detailed breakdown by
    presentation/condition/capability (including mastery_state,
    mastery_state_source, unique constraint).

-   Create coverage_config table for versioned configuration.

-   Add foreign key constraints for user_id, snapshot_id, approved_by.

-   Add unique index on (snapshot_id, entity_type, entity_id) for data
    integrity.

-   Add indexes for performance (user_id lookup, snapshot retrieval,
    entity filtering, config version queries).

**3. API/Backend**

**Endpoints**

**GET /api/v1/gmc-coverage/summary**

-   **Request:** {} (user authenticated)

-   **Response:**

-   {

-   \"gmc_map_version\": \"v2024.1\",

-   \"coverage_config_version\": \"v1.0\",

-   \"mastery_model_version\": \"v1.0\",

-   \"presentations\": {

-   \"total\": 120,

-   \"partial\": 20,

-   \"not_attempted\": 15

-   },

-   \"conditions\": {

-   \"not_attempted\": 25

-   },

-   \"capabilities\": {

-   \"covered\": 7,

-   \"partial\": 1,

-   \"not_attempted\": 0

-   },

-   \"snapshot_created_at\": \"2026-10-07T14:00:00Z\"

}

-   **Business logic:**

    -   Validate user is authenticated.

    -   Fetch most recent gmc_coverage_snapshots for user.

    -   Return aggregate coverage statistics (read-only from snapshot).

    -   **Do not calculate coverage on-the-fly** --- use pre-generated
        snapshot (performance).

**GET /api/v1/gmc-coverage/details**

-   **Request:** {entity_type: \"presentation\"} (optional filter, user
    authenticated)

-   **Response:**

-   {

-   \"entity_type\": \"presentation\",

-   \"gmc_map_version\": \"v2024.1\",

-   \"coverage_config_version\": \"v1.0\",

-   \"mastery_model_version\": \"v1.0\",

-   \"entities\": \[

-   {

-   \"last_attempted_at\": \"2026-10-06T10:00:00Z\",

-   \"mastery_state\": \"secure\",

-   \"mastery_state_source\": \"UKMLA-007\"

-   },

-   {

-   \"entity_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"entity_name\": \"Breathlessness\",

-   \"coverage_status\": \"covered\",

-   \"attempt_count\": 18,

-   \"last_attempted_at\": \"2026-10-05T14:00:00Z\",

-   \"mastery_state\": \"learning\",

-   \"mastery_state_source\": \"UKMLA-007\"

-   },

-   {

-   \"entity_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"entity_name\": \"Abdominal pain\",

-   \"coverage_status\": \"partial\",

-   \"attempt_count\": 3,

-   \"last_attempted_at\": \"2026-10-04T09:00:00Z\",

-   \"mastery_state\": \"learning\",

-   },

-   {

-   \"attempt_count\": 2,

-   \"last_attempted_at\": \"2026-10-03T11:00:00Z\",

-   },

-   {

-   \"entity_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"entity_name\": \"Confusion\",

-   \"coverage_status\": \"covered\",

-   \"attempt_count\": 15,

-   \"last_attempted_at\": \"2026-10-02T16:00:00Z\",

-   \"mastery_state\": \"secure\",

-   \"mastery_state_source\": \"UKMLA-007\"

-   },

-   {

-   \"entity_name\": \"Managing uncertainty\",

-   \"mastery_state_source\": null

-   }

-   \],

-   \"snapshot_created_at\": \"2026-10-07T14:00:00Z\"

}

-   **Business logic:**

    -   Validate user is authenticated.

    -   Fetch most recent gmc_coverage_snapshots for user.

    -   Fetch gmc_coverage_details for requested entity_type
        (presentation/condition/capability) --- **read-only from
        snapshot**.

    -   **Mastery state:** Snapshot contains mastery state at generation
        time (fetched from authoritative system during snapshot
        generation, not live from 007).

    -   **Capability mastery:** If no authoritative mastery model exists
        for capability entity type, mastery_state = \"not_available\",
        mastery_state_source = null.

    -   Return detailed breakdown sorted by entity_name.

    -   **Coverage status definitions:**

        -   covered: attempt_count \>= evidence_threshold (from
            coverage_config).

        -   partial: 1 \<= attempt_count \< evidence_threshold.

        -   not_attempted: attempt_count = 0.

**POST /api/v1/gmc-coverage/refresh**

-   **Request:** {} (user authenticated)

-   **Response:**

-   {

-   \"snapshot_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"gmc_map_version\": \"v2024.1\",

-   \"coverage_config_version\": \"v1.0\",

-   \"mastery_model_version\": \"v1.0\",

-   \"snapshot_created_at\": \"2026-10-07T15:00:00Z\",

-   \"refreshed\": true

}

-   **Business logic:**

    -   Validate user is authenticated.

    -   **Trigger coverage recalculation:**

        -   Fetch canonical GMC mappings from UKMLA-001/003.

        -   Fetch active coverage_config (evidence threshold, eligible
            attempt rules).

        -   Fetch candidate\'s eligible question/station attempts (per
            coverage_config).

        -   Calculate coverage status for each
            presentation/condition/capability.

        -   Fetch mastery states from UKMLA-007 (for
            presentations/conditions only; capabilities =
            \"not_available\").

        -   Create new gmc_coverage_snapshots record with
            gmc_map_version, coverage_config_version,
            mastery_model_version.

        -   Create new gmc_coverage_details records (one per entity,
            with mastery state snapshot).

    -   Return new snapshot ID, versions and timestamp.

    -   **Rate limit:** Maximum one refresh per N minutes (configurable,
        e.g. 5 minutes).

**Coverage Calculation Service (internal service)**

**Triggered by:**

-   Explicit refresh (POST /api/v1/gmc-coverage/refresh).

-   Scheduled refresh (e.g. daily).

-   Significant attempt milestone (e.g. every 50 new eligible attempts).

**Business logic:**

-   **Fetch canonical GMC mappings** from UKMLA-001/003 (presentations,
    conditions, capabilities).

-   **Fetch active coverage_config** --- evidence threshold, eligible
    attempt types.

-   **Fetch candidate\'s eligible question/station attempts** --- per
    coverage_config.eligible_attempt_types.

-   **Calculate coverage status:**

    -   For each presentation/condition/capability:

        -   Count eligible attempted questions/stations mapped to
            entity.

        -   covered: attempt_count \>= evidence_threshold.

        -   partial: 1 \<= attempt_count \< evidence_threshold.

        -   not_attempted: attempt_count = 0.

-   **Fetch mastery states:**

    -   **Presentations/conditions:** Fetch from UKMLA-007
        (authoritative mastery system).

    -   **Capabilities:** Set mastery_state = \"not_available\",
        mastery_state_source = null (no authoritative mastery model
        yet).

-   **Create snapshot:**

    -   Aggregate statistics (total, covered, partial, not_attempted for
        each entity type).

    -   Detailed breakdown (entity-level coverage status, attempt count,
        mastery state, mastery source).

    -   Include gmc_map_version, coverage_config_version,
        mastery_model_version.

-   **Store snapshot** in gmc_coverage_snapshots and
    gmc_coverage_details.

-   **Idempotency:** Concurrent refresh requests should not create
    duplicate snapshots (use database-level protection or
    application-level locking).

**Validation**

-   User must be authenticated.

-   User can only access their own coverage data.

-   entity_type must be presentation/condition/capability.

-   gmc_map_version must correspond to valid GMC MLA Content Map
    version.

-   coverage_config_version must correspond to valid, approved
    coverage_config version that was effective at time of snapshot
    generation.

-   Coverage status must be covered/partial/not_attempted (based on
    attempt_count vs evidence_threshold from coverage_config).

-   Mastery state fetched from authoritative system during snapshot
    generation (not calculated by 014).

-   For capabilities, mastery_state = \"not_available\",
    mastery_state_source = null (until authoritative mastery model
    exists).

-   entity_id must reference existing active canonical AMaC entity of
    correct type (validated at application/service layer).

**4. Frontend/UI**

**Screens**

**GMC Coverage Dashboard (in UKMLA-011 or dedicated page)**

-   Display:

    -   \"Your GMC MLA Content Map Coverage\" header.

    -   Overall coverage summary:

        -   **Presentations:** 85/120 covered (71%), 20 partial, 15 not
            attempted.

        -   **Conditions:** 140/200 covered (70%), 35 partial, 25 not
            attempted.

        -   **Capabilities:** 7/8 covered (88%), 1 partial, 0 not
            attempted.

    -   **Do not display single \"readiness\" percentage** --- coverage
        is structural measure, not pass prediction.

    -   Coverage config version display (e.g. \"Coverage rules: v1.0\").

    -   \"Refresh coverage\" button (rate-limited).

    -   Entity type tabs (Presentations / Conditions / Capabilities).

    -   Detailed table for selected entity type:

        -   Entity name

        -   Coverage status (covered/partial/not_attempted)

        -   Attempt count

        -   Last attempted date

        -   Mastery state (from snapshot, \"Not available\" for
            capabilities)

    -   Filter/sort options (by coverage status, mastery state, attempt
        count).

-   State: Loading (fetching coverage), Ready (coverage displayed),
    Refreshing (recalculating).

**GMC Coverage Card (widget in UKMLA-011 Dashboard)**

-   Display:

    -   \"GMC Coverage\" header.

    -   Summary statistics:

        -   Presentations: 85/120 covered

        -   Conditions: 140/200 covered

        -   Capabilities: 7/8 covered

    -   \"View full coverage\" link → GMC Coverage Dashboard.

-   State: Loading (fetching summary), Ready (summary displayed).

**Components**

-   **Coverage summary card:** Overall statistics for
    presentations/conditions/capabilities.

-   **Coverage table:** Detailed breakdown by entity (name, coverage
    status, attempt count, mastery state).

-   **Coverage status indicator:** Visual indicator (e.g. green =
    covered, amber = partial, grey = not_attempted).

-   **Mastery state indicator:** Visual indicator (e.g. green = secure,
    amber = learning, grey = not_demonstrated, muted = not_available).

-   **Refresh button:** Triggers coverage recalculation (rate-limited).

-   **Coverage config version badge:** Displays active coverage rules
    version.

**Interactions**

-   Clicking \"Refresh coverage\" → triggers POST
    /api/v1/gmc-coverage/refresh.

-   Clicking entity type tab → filters detailed table.

-   Sorting/filtering table → reorders coverage details.

-   Clicking \"View full coverage\" → navigates to GMC Coverage
    Dashboard.

**5. Business Logic**

**Coverage Calculation**

-   **Source of truth:** Use canonical GMC mappings from UKMLA-001/003
    (presentations, conditions, capabilities).

-   **Do not calculate mastery** --- fetch mastery states from
    authoritative system during snapshot generation.

-   **Coverage status definitions:**

    -   not_attempted: attempt_count = 0 (no eligible attempts).

    -   partial: 1 \<= attempt_count \< evidence_threshold (below
        meaningful coverage).

    -   covered: attempt_count \>= evidence_threshold (meaningfully
        attempted).

-   **Evidence threshold:** Configurable via coverage_config (e.g. 5
    attempts) --- defines when entity is considered \"covered\".

-   **Attempt count:** Number of eligible attempted questions/stations
    mapped to entity (per coverage_config.eligible_attempt_types).

**Coverage vs Mastery Distinction**

-   **Coverage (014):** \"Has the candidate meaningfully attempted
    questions/stations mapped to this entity?\"

-   **Mastery (007):** \"Has the candidate demonstrated mastery of this
    entity?\"

-   **Example:**

    -   Chest pain: Covered (25 attempts) + Secure (mastery from 007).

    -   Breathlessness: Covered (18 attempts) + Learning (mastery from
        007).

    -   PE: Partial (3 attempts) + Not demonstrated (mastery from 007).

    -   Managing uncertainty: Covered (12 attempts) + Not available (no
        authoritative mastery model yet).

-   **014 does not infer mastery from coverage** --- mastery fetched
    from authoritative system during snapshot generation.

-   **Capabilities:** Mastery state = \"not_available\" until
    authoritative mastery model exists (e.g. UKMLA-027 for CPSA).

**Coverage Refresh**

-   **Explicit refresh:** Candidate clicks \"Refresh coverage\" →
    triggers recalculation.

-   **Scheduled refresh:** Daily scheduled job recalculates coverage for
    active users.

-   **Milestone refresh:** Every N new eligible attempts (e.g. 50)
    triggers recalculation.

-   **Rate limit:** Maximum one explicit refresh per N minutes (e.g. 5
    minutes).

-   **Idempotency:** Concurrent refresh requests should not create
    duplicate snapshots.

**Coverage Versioning**

-   **GMC map version:** Snapshot includes gmc_map_version (e.g.
    \"v2024.1\").

-   **Coverage config version:** Snapshot includes
    coverage_config_version (e.g. \"v1.0\") --- evidence threshold,
    eligible attempt rules.

-   **Mastery model version:** Snapshot includes mastery_model_version
    (e.g. \"v1.0\") --- mastery model used for snapshot.

-   **Version changes:** If GMC map or coverage config updates, new
    snapshots use new versions.

-   **Historical snapshots:** Previous snapshots retained for
    audit/historical comparison (reproducible with version info).

**Eligible Attempt Rules**

-   **Configurable via coverage_config:**

    -   eligible_attempt_types: \[\"learning\", \"exam\", \"repeat\",
        \"retest\"\]

    -   excluded_attempt_types: \[\"diagnostic\", \"abandoned\"\]

-   **Examples:**

    -   Learning attempt → included.

    -   Exam-mode attempt → included.

    -   Repeat attempt → included.

    -   Retest → included.

    -   Diagnostic attempt → excluded (unless configured otherwise).

    -   Abandoned attempt → excluded.

    -   Unanswered question → excluded.

-   **Versioned:** Changes to eligible attempt rules require new
    coverage_config_version (historical snapshots remain reproducible).

**6. Edge Cases**

**Error Handling**

-   **No attempts yet:** Show \"You haven\'t attempted any
    questions/stations yet. Coverage will appear here once you start
    practising.\"

-   **GMC mapping unavailable:** Show error \"GMC Content Map data is
    temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.\"

-   **Mastery data unavailable:** Show mastery state as \"Unknown\" (do
    not block coverage display).

-   **Network failure:** Retry logic (3 attempts), then show error
    \"Unable to load coverage. Please try again.\"

**Empty States**

-   **No coverage data:** Show message \"Your coverage will appear here
    once you start attempting questions/stations.\"

**Data Integrity**

-   **GMC mapping mismatch:** If entity mapping changes (e.g.
    presentation renamed), log error and use most recent mapping.

-   **Stale coverage:** If coverage older than N days, show \"Coverage
    last updated X days ago. Click refresh to update.\"

-   **Duplicate snapshot prevention:** Concurrent refresh requests
    should not create duplicate snapshots (idempotency).

**7. Permissions/Security**

**Access Control**

-   **Authentication required:** User must be authenticated.

-   **Authorization:** User can only access their own coverage data.

-   **Read-only:** Coverage data is read-only (refresh triggers
    recalculation, not manual edit).

**Data Protection**

-   **PII:** User data encrypted at rest (per platform security
    architecture).

-   **Session management:** Follows UKMLA-000 (no separate coverage
    token mechanism).

-   **Audit log:** Coverage refresh events logged for governance.

**8. Analytics/Events**

**Tracking Events**

-   coverage_viewed: {user_id, entity_type, timestamp}

-   coverage_refreshed: {user_id, gmc_map_version,
    coverage_config_version, timestamp}

**Metrics**

-   Coverage refresh rate.

-   Average coverage percentage (presentations/conditions/capabilities).

-   Time from signup to first coverage (first attempt).

-   Coverage progression over time (longitudinal tracking).

**9. Acceptance Criteria**

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they request coverage
    summary, **then** aggregate statistics are returned
    (presentations/conditions/capabilities
    covered/partial/not_attempted).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they request coverage
    details, **then** detailed breakdown is returned by entity type
    (presentation/condition/capability).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they request coverage
    details, **then** mastery states are from snapshot (fetched from
    authoritative system during snapshot generation, not live from 007).

-   **Given** an authenticated user with capabilities, **when** they
    request coverage details, **then** mastery_state =
    \"not_available\", mastery_state_source = null (no authoritative
    mastery model yet).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they refresh coverage,
    **then** new snapshot is generated with gmc_map_version,
    coverage_config_version, mastery_model_version.

-   **Given** an authenticated user with no attempts, **when** they
    request coverage, **then** message shown (\"You haven\'t attempted
    any questions/stations yet\").

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they view coverage,
    **then** coverage status is displayed as
    covered/partial/not_attempted (based on attempt_count vs
    evidence_threshold).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they view coverage,
    **then** mastery state is displayed (from snapshot, \"Not
    available\" for capabilities).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they refresh coverage,
    **then** rate limit enforced (max one refresh per N minutes).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they view coverage,
    **then** GMC map version and coverage config version are displayed.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they view coverage,
    **then** coverage is distinguished from mastery (no single
    \"readiness\" percentage).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** coverage is calculated,
    **then** canonical GMC mappings from UKMLA-001/003 are used.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** coverage is calculated,
    **then** evidence threshold is applied from coverage_config (e.g. 5
    attempts = covered).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** coverage is calculated,
    **then** eligible attempt rules are applied from coverage_config.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** coverage is refreshed,
    **then** snapshot is stored with gmc_map_version,
    coverage_config_version, mastery_model_version, snapshot_created_at.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they view coverage,
    **then** only their own coverage data is returned (authorization).

-   **Given** concurrent refresh requests, **when** they occur, **then**
    only one snapshot is created (idempotency).

-   **Given** a coverage_config approval, **when** it is created,
    **then** approved_by references user with required AMaC
    product/educational governance permission (authorisation enforced at
    application/service layer).

**10. Dependencies**

-   **UKMLA-000:** Authentication and user identity (required for access
    control).

-   **UKMLA-001/003:** GMC Content Map + canonical mappings (upstream
    --- provides presentations/conditions/capabilities).

-   **UKMLA-007:** Mastery Calculation Engine (upstream --- provides
    mastery states for presentations/conditions).

-   **UKMLA-011:** Candidate Profile Dashboard (downstream --- displays
    coverage card/dashboard).

**12. Clinical/Governance Requirements**

**Clinical Content**

-   **No clinical content** in coverage calculations (purely structural
    measure of eligible attempted questions/stations).

**Governance**

-   **Read-only:** Coverage data is read-only (refresh triggers
    recalculation, not manual edit).

-   **Audit trail:** Coverage refresh events logged for governance.

-   **GMC map versioning:** Coverage snapshots include gmc_map_version
    for traceability.

-   **Coverage config versioning:** Coverage snapshots include
    coverage_config_version for traceability (evidence threshold,
    eligible attempt rules).

-   **Mastery model versioning:** Coverage snapshots include
    mastery_model_version for traceability.

-   **Coverage vs mastery:** 014 explicitly distinguishes coverage
    (meaningfully attempted) from mastery (demonstrated) --- mastery
    fetched from authoritative system during snapshot generation.

-   **coverage_config approval:** Changes to coverage rules, evidence
    threshold, eligible attempt types require versioning and approval
    through the AMaC product/educational governance process. Changes
    must not silently alter previously generated snapshots.

**Disclaimer**

-   Coverage shows how much of the GMC MLA Content Map you have
    meaningfully attempted, based on AMaC\'s configured coverage
    evidence rules.

-   Coverage does not indicate mastery, competence, or exam readiness.

-   Candidates should use coverage to identify gaps in revision, not as
    a pass prediction.

-   Mastery states are from authoritative mastery systems (e.g.
    UKMLA-007 for presentations/conditions) and represent demonstrated
    competence, not coverage.

-   Capability mastery is not yet available (no authoritative mastery
    model exists yet).

This revision resolves the outstanding issues from the previous version.

**What is now correctly locked**

-   **Coverage threshold:** consistently defined as 0 = not_attempted,
    1..threshold-1 = partial, \>= threshold = covered.

    authoritative capability mastery system exists. 014 does not invent
    one.

-   **Snapshot consistency:** API reads use the stored snapshot rather
    than mixing historical coverage with live mastery.

    from UKMLA-001/003.

-   **Polymorphic entity IDs:** correctly treated as

    cannot silently rewrite historical snapshots.

-   **Refresh:** explicit, scheduled and milestone refreshes are clearly
    separated, with rate limiting and idempotency.

-   **Scope:** 014 remains a **coverage engine**, not another mastery

-   **Language:** the disclaimer correctly avoids implying competence,
    readiness or pass probability.

**Implementation Notes (Developer Guidance)**

**Concurrent Refresh Protection**

-   The specification requires idempotency for concurrent refresh
    requests. Implementation should use real database-level locking or
    idempotency mechanisms:

-   **Recommended pattern:**

\-- Application-level lock (e.g. PostgreSQL pg_advisory_lock)

SELECT pg_advisory_lock(:user_id);

\-- Check if recent snapshot exists (within rate limit window)

SELECT id, snapshot_created_at

FROM gmc_coverage_snapshots

WHERE user_id = :user_id

ORDER BY snapshot_created_at DESC

LIMIT 1;

\-- If refresh needed, proceed with atomic snapshot creation

BEGIN;

\-- Create snapshot

INSERT INTO gmc_coverage_snapshots (\...)

VALUES (\...)

RETURNING id;

\-- Create details (one per entity)

INSERT INTO gmc_coverage_details (\...)

VALUES (\...);

COMMIT;

\-- Release lock

SELECT pg_advisory_unlock(:user_id);

-   **Alternative:** Use unique constraint on (user_id,
    snapshot_created_at) with appropriate time bucketing to prevent
    duplicate snapshots within rate limit window.

**UKMLA-015 --- Learning Mode vs Exam Mode (AKT) (Full Engineering
Specification)**

**1. User Story**

**As an** AMaC candidate (authenticated),\
**I want to** choose between a learning-focused practice experience
(with explanations, hints, and educational feedback) and an exam-focused
practice experience (timed, no hints, exam-style interaction),\
**so that** I can adapt my practice mode to match my current revision
goals (learning new material vs simulating exam conditions).

**2. Data/Schema**

**Tables**

**practice_sessions** (candidate\'s practice session attempts)

-   id (PK, UUID)

-   user_id (FK to users.id, indexed, not null)

-   session_type (enum: learning, exam, not null) --- mode selected by
    candidate.

-   session_status (enum: in_progress, completed, abandoned, not null,
    default \"in_progress\")

-   question_count (integer, not null) --- number of questions in
    session (configurable, e.g. 20, 40, 60).

-   time_limit_seconds (integer, nullable) --- time limit for exam mode
    (e.g. 3600 for 60 minutes), NULL for learning mode (no time limit).

-   started_at (timestamp, not null)

-   completed_at (timestamp, nullable)

-   abandoned_at (timestamp, nullable)

-   created_at (timestamp, not null)

-   Index: (user_id, session_status, started_at DESC)

-   Index: (user_id, session_type)

**practice_session_questions** (questions within a practice session)

-   id (PK, UUID)

-   session_id (FK to practice_sessions.id, indexed, not null)

-   question_id (FK to questions.id, indexed, not null) --- canonical
    question from question bank.

-   question_order (integer, not null) --- order of question within
    session (1, 2, 3\...).

-   attempt_status (enum: not_attempted, in_progress, answered, not
    null, default \"not_attempted\")

-   selected_answer_id (FK to question_answers.id, nullable) ---
    candidate\'s selected answer.

-   is_correct (boolean, nullable) --- whether selected answer is
    correct (NULL if not yet answered).

-   time_spent_seconds (integer, nullable) --- time spent on this
    question (NULL if not yet answered).

-   answered_at (timestamp, nullable)

-   created_at (timestamp, not null)

-   Index: (session_id, question_order)

-   Index: (session_id, attempt_status)

-   Unique constraint: UNIQUE(session_id, question_id) --- same question
    cannot appear twice in same session.

**practice_session_config** (versioned configuration for practice
sessions)

-   id (PK, UUID)

-   version (string, unique, not null, e.g. \"v1.0\")

-   effective_from (timestamp, not null)

-   effective_to (timestamp, nullable)

-   configuration_json (JSON, not null) --- e.g. {\"learning_mode\":
    {\"default_question_count\": 20, \"show_explanations_immediately\":
    true, \"show_hints\": true, \"allow_answer_change\": true},
    \"exam_mode\": {\"default_question_count\": 60,
    \"time_limit_seconds\": 3600, \"show_explanations_immediately\":
    false, \"show_hints\": false, \"allow_answer_change\": false}}

-   approved_by (FK to users.id, not null) --- **must reference user
    with required AMaC product/educational governance permission**
    (authorisation enforced at application/service layer).

-   approved_at (timestamp, not null)

-   change_reason (text, nullable)

-   Index: (version)

-   Index: (effective_from, effective_to)

**Migrations**

-   Create practice_sessions table with above schema.

-   Create practice_session_questions table for questions within
    session.

-   Create practice_session_config table for versioned configuration.

-   Add foreign key constraints for user_id, session_id, question_id,
    selected_answer_id, approved_by.

-   Add unique index on (session_id, question_id) to prevent duplicate
    questions in same session.

-   Add indexes for performance (user_id lookup, session retrieval,
    question order).

**3. API/Backend**

**Endpoints**

**POST /api/v1/practice-sessions/start**

-   **Request:**

-   {

-   \"session_type\": \"learning\",

-   \"question_count\": 20

}

-   **Response:**

-   {

-   \"session\": {

-   \"id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"session_type\": \"learning\",

-   \"session_status\": \"in_progress\",

-   \"question_count\": 20,

-   \"time_limit_seconds\": null,

-   \"started_at\": \"2026-10-07T14:00:00Z\",

-   \"completed_at\": null,

-   \"abandoned_at\": null,

-   \"created_at\": \"2026-10-07T14:00:00Z\"

-   },

-   \"questions\": \[

-   {

-   \"question_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"question_order\": 1,

-   \"attempt_status\": \"not_attempted\"

-   },

-   {

-   \"question_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"question_order\": 2,

-   \"attempt_status\": \"not_attempted\"

-   }

-   \]

}

-   **Business logic:**

    -   Validate user is authenticated.

    -   Validate session_type (learning/exam).

    -   Validate question_count (per practice_session_config for
        selected mode).

    -   **Select questions:**

        -   Random selection from question bank (or based on candidate
            focus from UKMLA-013, if provided).

        -   Ensure no duplicate questions in same session.

        -   Ensure questions are active/approved.

    -   Create practice_sessions record.

    -   Create practice_session_questions records (one per selected
        question).

    -   Return session and question list (without question content ---
        content fetched via GET
        /api/v1/practice-sessions/{session_id}/questions/{question_id}).

**GET /api/v1/practice-sessions/{session_id}**

-   **Request:** {} (user authenticated)

-   **Response:**

-   {

-   \"session\": {

-   \"id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"session_type\": \"learning\",

-   \"session_status\": \"in_progress\",

-   \"question_count\": 20,

-   \"time_limit_seconds\": null,

-   \"started_at\": \"2026-10-07T14:00:00Z\",

-   \"completed_at\": null,

-   \"abandoned_at\": null,

-   \"created_at\": \"2026-10-07T14:00:00Z\"

-   },

-   \"progress\": {

-   \"answered_count\": 5,

-   \"not_attempted_count\": 15,

-   \"correct_count\": 4,

-   \"incorrect_count\": 1

-   }

}

-   **Business logic:**

    -   Validate user is authenticated.

    -   Validate session exists and belongs to authenticated user.

    -   Return session details and progress summary.

**GET /api/v1/practice-sessions/{session_id}/questions/{question_id}**

-   **Request:** {} (user authenticated)

-   **Response (Learning Mode):**

-   {

-   \"question\": {

-   \"question_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"question_order\": 1,

-   \"attempt_status\": \"not_attempted\",

-   \"stem\": \"A 55-year-old man presents with chest pain\...\",

-   \"options\": \[

-   {\"id\": \"uuid\", \"text\": \"Acute coronary syndrome\"},

-   {\"id\": \"uuid\", \"text\": \"Pulmonary embolism\"},

-   {\"id\": \"uuid\", \"text\": \"Pneumonia\"},

-   {\"id\": \"uuid\", \"text\": \"Gastro-oesophageal reflux\"}

-   \],

-   \"learning_mode_features\": {

-   \"show_hints\": true,

-   \"hints\": \[\"Think about the cardiovascular system\...\"\],

-   \"show_explanations_immediately\": true,

-   \"allow_answer_change\": true

-   }

-   },

-   \"selected_answer_id\": null,

-   \"is_correct\": null,

-   \"time_spent_seconds\": 0

}

-   **Response (Exam Mode):**

-   {

-   \"question\": {

-   \"question_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"question_order\": 1,

-   \"attempt_status\": \"not_attempted\",

-   \"stem\": \"A 55-year-old man presents with chest pain\...\",

-   \"options\": \[

-   {\"id\": \"uuid\", \"text\": \"Acute coronary syndrome\"},

-   {\"id\": \"uuid\", \"text\": \"Pulmonary embolism\"},

-   {\"id\": \"uuid\", \"text\": \"Pneumonia\"},

-   {\"id\": \"uuid\", \"text\": \"Gastro-oesophageal reflux\"}

-   \],

-   \"exam_mode_features\": {

-   \"show_hints\": false,

-   \"hints\": null,

-   \"show_explanations_immediately\": false,

-   \"allow_answer_change\": false

-   }

-   },

-   \"selected_answer_id\": null,

-   \"is_correct\": null,

-   \"time_spent_seconds\": 0,

-   \"time_remaining_seconds\": 3600

}

-   **Business logic:**

    -   Validate user is authenticated.

    -   Validate session exists and belongs to authenticated user.

    -   Validate question is part of session.

    -   **Learning mode features:**

        -   Show hints (if configured).

        -   Show explanations immediately after answering (if
            configured).

        -   Allow answer change (if configured).

    -   **Exam mode features:**

        -   No hints.

        -   No explanations until session completed.

        -   No answer change (once submitted, locked).

        -   Show time remaining.

    -   Return question content with mode-specific features.

**POST
/api/v1/practice-sessions/{session_id}/questions/{question_id}/answer**

-   **Request:**

-   {

-   \"selected_answer_id\": \"uuid\"

}

-   **Response (Learning Mode):**

-   {

-   \"question_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"selected_answer_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"is_correct\": true,

-   \"explanation\": \"Acute coronary syndrome is the most likely
    diagnosis\...\",

-   \"gmc_mappings\": \[\"Cardiovascular\", \"Chest pain\"\],

-   \"references\": \[\"NICE CG95\", \"ESC Guidelines 2023\"\],

-   \"time_spent_seconds\": 45

}

-   **Response (Exam Mode):**

-   {

-   \"question_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"selected_answer_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"is_correct\": null, --- NULL until session completed

-   \"explanation\": null, --- NULL until session completed

-   \"time_spent_seconds\": 45,

-   \"answer_locked\": true --- cannot change answer in exam mode

}

-   **Business logic:**

    -   Validate user is authenticated.

    -   Validate session exists and belongs to authenticated user.

    -   Validate question is part of session.

    -   Validate selected_answer_id is valid for question.

    -   **Learning mode:**

        -   Record selected answer.

        -   Immediately calculate is_correct.

        -   Return explanation, GMC mappings, references.

        -   Allow answer change (if configured).

    -   **Exam mode:**

        -   Record selected answer.

        -   Do NOT calculate is_correct yet (NULL until session
            completed).

        -   Do NOT return explanation (NULL until session completed).

        -   Lock answer (cannot change, answer_locked: true).

    -   Update practice_session_questions record (selected_answer_id,
        attempt_status, time_spent_seconds, answered_at).

    -   Log attempt event for mastery calculation (UKMLA-007).

**POST /api/v1/practice-sessions/{session_id}/complete**

-   **Request:** {} (user authenticated)

-   **Response:**

-   {

-   \"session\": {

-   \"id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"session_type\": \"exam\",

-   \"session_status\": \"completed\",

-   \"question_count\": 60,

-   \"time_limit_seconds\": 3600,

-   \"started_at\": \"2026-10-07T14:00:00Z\",

-   \"completed_at\": \"2026-10-07T15:00:00Z\",

-   \"abandoned_at\": null,

-   \"created_at\": \"2026-10-07T14:00:00Z\"

-   },

-   \"results\": {

-   \"correct_count\": 45,

-   \"incorrect_count\": 15,

-   \"percentage\": 75,

-   \"time_taken_seconds\": 3600

-   },

-   \"questions\": \[

-   {

-   \"question_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"question_order\": 1,

-   \"selected_answer_id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"is_correct\": true,

-   \"explanation\": \"\...\",

-   \"gmc_mappings\": \[\"\...\"\],

-   \"references\": \[\"\...\"\]

-   }

-   \]

}

-   **Business logic:**

    -   Validate user is authenticated.

    -   Validate session exists and belongs to authenticated user.

    -   Validate session is in_progress (not already
        completed/abandoned).

    -   Update session status to completed.

    -   Calculate results (correct_count, incorrect_count, percentage).

    -   **Exam mode:** Now reveal is_correct, explanations, GMC
        mappings, references for all questions.

    -   Return session results with full question review.

    -   Log session completion event for analytics.

**POST /api/v1/practice-sessions/{session_id}/abandon**

-   **Request:** {} (user authenticated)

-   **Response:**

-   {

-   \"session\": {

-   \"id\": \"uuid\",

-   \"session_type\": \"exam\",

-   \"session_status\": \"abandoned\",

-   \"question_count\": 60,

-   \"time_limit_seconds\": 3600,

-   \"started_at\": \"2026-10-07T14:00:00Z\",

-   \"completed_at\": null,

-   \"abandoned_at\": \"2026-10-07T14:30:00Z\",

-   \"created_at\": \"2026-10-07T14:00:00Z\"

-   }

}

-   **Business logic:**

    -   Validate user is authenticated.

    -   Validate session exists and belongs to authenticated user.

    -   Update session status to abandoned.

    -   Log session abandonment event for analytics.

    -   Return session details.

**Validation**

-   User must be authenticated.

-   User can only access/modify their own sessions.

-   session_type must be learning/exam.

-   question_count must be per practice_session_config for selected
    mode.

-   selected_answer_id must be valid for question.

-   Exam mode: answer cannot be changed once submitted
    (allow_answer_change: false).

-   Exam mode: explanations not revealed until session completed.

**Screens**

        -   \"Learning Mode\" title.

        -   Features:

            -   Show hints.

            -   Change answers anytime.

            -   No time limit.

        -   Question count selector (20, 40, 60).

        -   \"Start Learning\" button.

    -   Exam Mode card:

        -   \"Exam Mode\" title.

        -   Description: \"Simulate exam conditions with timed, no-hint
            practice.\"

        -   Features:

            -   No explanations until end.

            -   No hints.

            -   Cannot change answers.

            -   Time limit (60 minutes for 60 questions).

        -   Question count selector (60, 120).

        -   \"Start Exam\" button.

-   State: Ready (mode selection displayed).

**Practice Session (Learning Mode)**

-   Display:

    -   Question stem.

    -   Answer options (radio buttons).

    -   Hints button (shows hint if available).

    -   Submit button.

    -   Progress indicator (e.g. \"Question 5 of 20\").

    -   Time spent on question.

-   After answering:

    -   Show correct/incorrect indicator.

    -   Show explanation.

    -   Show GMC mappings.

    -   Show references.

    -   \"Next question\" button.

    -   Allow answer change (if configured).

-   State: Loading (fetching question), Ready (question displayed),
    Answered (explanation shown).

**Practice Session (Exam Mode)**

-   Display:

    -   Question stem.

    -   Answer options (radio buttons).

    -   Submit button.

    -   Progress indicator (e.g. \"Question 5 of 60\").

    -   Time remaining.

    -   Time spent on question.

-   After answering:

    -   No correct/incorrect indicator.

    -   No explanation.

    -   Answer locked (cannot change).

    -   \"Next question\" button.

-   Session completion:

    -   Show results (percentage, correct/incorrect count).

    -   Show full question review (all questions with explanations).

-   State: Loading (fetching question), Ready (question displayed),
    Answered (locked, no explanation), Completed (results shown).

**Session Results**

-   Display:

    -   \"Session Results\" header.

    -   Percentage score.

    -   Correct/incorrect count.

**Components**

-   **Mode selection card:** Learning/Exam mode features, question count
    selector, start button.

-   **Question display:** Stem, options, submit button, progress
    indicator.

-   **Learning mode features:** Hints button, explanation display, GMC
    mappings, references.

-   **Exam mode features:** Time remaining, answer lock indicator.

-   **Results display:** Percentage, correct/incorrect count, question
    review.

**Interactions**

-   Selecting mode → starts practice session.

-   Answering question (learning) → shows explanation immediately.

-   Answering question (exam) → locks answer, no explanation until
    session completed.

-   Completing session (exam) → reveals all explanations and results.

-   Abandoning session → session marked abandoned, no results shown.

**5. Business Logic**

**Mode Differences**

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Feature**    **Learning Mode**           **Exam Mode**
  -------------- --------------------------- ------------------------------
  Explanations   Immediately after answering After session completed

  Hints          Show (if available)         Hide

  Answer change  Allow (if configured)       Disallow (locked after submit)

  Time limit     None                        Configurable (e.g. 3600s for
                                             60 questions)

  Progress       Correct/incorrect shown     Correct/incorrect hidden until
  feedback       immediately                 completion

  GMC mappings   Shown with explanation      Shown after session completed

  References     Shown with explanation      Shown after session completed
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Question Selection**

-   **Random selection:** Questions randomly selected from question
    bank.

-   **Candidate focus (optional):** If UKMLA-013 override provided,
    prioritise questions matching candidate\'s focus
    (specialty/presentation/condition/difficulty).

-   **No duplicates:** Same question cannot appear twice in same session
    (unique constraint on session_id, question_id).

-   **Active/approved questions only:** Inactive or unapproved questions
    excluded.

**Attempt Logging**

-   **All attempts logged:** For mastery calculation (UKMLA-007).

-   **Attempt metadata:** session_type, question_id, selected_answer_id,
    is_correct, time_spent_seconds.

-   **Eligible for coverage:** Learning and exam attempts both eligible
    for UKMLA-014 coverage (per coverage_config).

**Session Completion**

-   **Learning mode:** Session completed when all questions answered (or
    candidate abandons).

-   **Exam mode:** Session completed when all questions answered OR time
    limit expires.

-   **Results calculation:** correct_count, incorrect_count, percentage.

-   **Explanation reveal (exam mode):** All explanations, GMC mappings,
    references revealed after completion.

**Session Abandonment**

-   **Candidate can abandon:** Anytime during session.

-   **Session marked abandoned:** abandoned_at set, session_status =
    \"abandoned\".

-   **No results shown:** Incomplete session, no percentage calculated.

-   **Attempts still logged:** For coverage/mastery (partial session
    still counts as attempts).

**6. Edge Cases**

**Error Handling**

-   **Session not found:** Show error \"Session not found or does not
    belong to you.\"

-   **Question not in session:** Show error \"This question is not part
    of your session.\"

-   **Invalid answer:** Show error \"Please select a valid answer.\"

-   **Session already completed:** Show error \"This session has already
    been completed.\"

-   **Time limit expired (exam mode):** Automatically complete session,
    calculate results.

-   **Network failure:** Retry logic (3 attempts), then show error
    \"Unable to load question. Please try again.\"

**Empty States**

-   **No questions available:** Show error \"No questions available for
    practice. Please try again later.\"

**Data Integrity**

-   **Duplicate question prevention:** Unique constraint on (session_id,
    question_id).

-   **Answer lock (exam mode):** Once submitted, answer cannot be
    changed (enforced at API layer).

-   **Time limit enforcement (exam mode):** Session automatically
    completed when time expires.

**7. Permissions/Security**

**Access Control**

-   **Authentication required:** User must be authenticated.

-   **Authorization:** User can only access/modify their own sessions.

-   **Read/write:** Sessions are user-controlled (start, answer,
    complete, abandon).

**Data Protection**

-   **PII:** User data encrypted at rest (per platform security
    architecture).

-   **Session management:** Follows UKMLA-000 (no separate session token
    mechanism).

-   **Audit log:** All session interactions logged for governance
    (start, answer, complete, abandon).

**8. Analytics/Events**

**Tracking Events**

-   practice_session_started: {user_id, session_type, question_count,
    timestamp}

-   practice_question_answered: {user_id, session_id, question_id,
    session_type, is_correct, time_spent_seconds, timestamp}

-   practice_session_completed: {user_id, session_id, session_type,
    correct_count, incorrect_count, percentage, time_taken_seconds,
    timestamp}

-   practice_session_abandoned: {user_id, session_id, session_type,
    questions_answered, timestamp}

**Metrics**

-   Session start rate (learning vs exam).

-   Average session percentage (learning vs exam).

-   Time spent per question (learning vs exam).

-   Session completion rate.

-   Session abandonment rate.

-   Question difficulty vs performance (learning vs exam).

**9. Acceptance Criteria**

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they start a learning
    session, **then** session is created with learning mode features
    (hints, immediate explanations, allow answer change).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they start an exam
    session, **then** session is created with exam mode features (no
    hints, no explanations until completion, no answer change, time
    limit).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they answer a question in
    learning mode, **then** explanation, GMC mappings, references are
    shown immediately.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they answer a question in
    exam mode, **then** answer is locked, no explanation shown until
    session completed.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they complete an exam
    session, **then** results are calculated and all explanations
    revealed.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they abandon a session,
    **then** session marked abandoned, no results shown.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they view session
    progress, **then** correct/incorrect count shown (learning mode) or
    hidden (exam mode until completion).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they answer a question,
    **then** attempt logged for mastery calculation (UKMLA-007).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they answer a question,
    **then** attempt counted for coverage (UKMLA-014) per
    coverage_config.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they start a session,
    **then** no duplicate questions in same session (unique constraint).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they answer a question in
    exam mode, **then** answer cannot be changed (locked).

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** time limit expires (exam
    mode), **then** session automatically completed, results calculated.

-   **Given** an authenticated user, **when** they request session,
    **then** only their own session is returned (authorization).

-   **Given** a practice_session_config approval, **when** it is
    created, **then** approved_by references user with required AMaC
    product/educational governance permission (authorisation enforced at
    application/service layer).

**10. Dependencies**

-   **UKMLA-000:** Authentication and user identity (required for access
    control).

-   **UKMLA-007:** Mastery Calculation Engine (downstream --- consumes
    attempt data for mastery calculation).

-   **UKMLA-014:** GMC Coverage Engine (downstream --- consumes attempt
    data for coverage calculation).

-   **Question Bank:** Canonical questions, answers, explanations, GMC
    mappings (upstream --- provides question content).

**12. Clinical/Governance Requirements**

**Clinical Content**

-   **No clinical content invented by 015** --- question content,
    explanations, GMC mappings from canonical question bank.

**Governance**

-   **Read/write:** Sessions are user-controlled (start, answer,
    complete, abandon).

-   **Audit trail:** All session interactions logged for governance.

-   **practice_session_config versioning:** Changes to mode features,
    question counts, time limits require versioning and approval through
    the AMaC product/educational governance process. Changes must not
    silently alter active sessions.

**Disclaimer**

-   Learning mode is for educational practice with explanations and
    feedback.

-   Exam mode simulates exam conditions but does not guarantee exam
    performance.

-   Session results are for self-assessment, not validated measures of
    competence.

Complete**

**UKMLA-015 --- AMEND / NOT YET FROZEN**

This is a strong specification and the overall architecture is right.
However, I would **not freeze it yet** because there are several
important issues around the canonical attempt system, reproducibility,
timing, and what "Exam Mode" is supposed to simulate.

The biggest one is that **015 must not accidentally become a second
attempt system**.

**1. 🔴 Canonical question attempts must be explicit**

The specification currently says:

"Log attempt event for mastery calculation (UKMLA-007)."

That is too vague given the frozen architecture.

We already have the canonical attempt architecture behind **UKMLA-005 /
UKMLA-007**, and 014 consumes eligible attempts. 015 should **write to
the canonical attempt system**, not create an independent
practice-attempt concept.

Add something like:

**Canonical attempt recording**

-   Every submitted practice question creates/updates the canonical
    question_attempts record defined by the existing attempt
    architecture.

-   practice_session_questions is session-level presentation/state only
    and is not the authoritative source for mastery, coverage or attempt
    history.

-   attempt_category (first, repeat, retest) is determined by the
    canonical attempt-classification system, not by session_type.

-   session_type (learning or exam) is stored as contextual metadata and
    must not be used as a substitute for attempt_category.

-   UKMLA-007 consumes canonical attempts for mastery.

-   UKMLA-014 consumes canonical attempts according to its versioned
    eligibility rules.

This is **critical**.

For example:

**Learning + first exposure** ≠ automatically "learning attempt".

**Exam + previously seen question** ≠ automatically "first attempt".

Attempt category is about the candidate\'s history/context, whereas mode
is about the current practice experience.

**2. 🔴 Answer changes need an attempt-event model**

There is currently a potential ambiguity:

Learning Mode → candidate can change answer → every answer submission is
logged as an attempt.

That could artificially inflate attempts and distort both mastery and
coverage.

You need to distinguish:

-   answer interaction/change events

-   the actual canonical question attempt

I recommend:

In Learning Mode, answer changes are recorded as interaction events. The
canonical question attempt represents the candidate\'s final submitted
answer for that question exposure/session, unless the existing attempt
architecture explicitly defines another model.

This prevents:

**A → B → C → D**

from becoming four clinical attempts.

Add a lightweight practice_question_events table **or** use the existing
canonical attempt-event infrastructure if 005 already provides it.

**3. 🔴 Add the canonical attempt-system dependency**

Your dependencies currently list:

-   000

-   007

-   014

-   Question Bank

But 015 should explicitly depend on the existing attempt architecture.

Add:

**UKMLA-005:** Canonical question-attempt recording and attempt
categorisation.

And clarify:

**015 creates practice-session context → canonical attempt system
records the attempt → 007 consumes it → 014 consumes it according to
coverage rules.**

That gives you a clean chain.

**4. 🔴 Snapshot content/config versions into the session**

This is currently missing.

You have a versioned practice_session_config, but practice_sessions
itself doesn\'t store the configuration version.

Add:

practice_config_version

to practice_sessions.

Otherwise a session started under v1.0 could potentially be interpreted
using v1.1 after the configuration changes.

Also add question-content provenance to practice_session_questions:

question_content_version

question_gmc_map_version

This is important because AMaC\'s clinical content and GMC mappings are
versioned.

The session should therefore preserve exactly what the candidate
practised.

**5. 🔴 Exam timer must be server-authoritative**

The current specification says:

"Time limit expires → automatically complete session."

But it needs to explicitly say **the client timer is display-only**.

Add:

-   Server calculates expiry from started_at + time_limit_seconds.

-   Client countdown is presentation only and cannot determine whether a
    session has expired.

-   Answer submission after expiry is rejected or handled according to
    the server-defined expiry rule.

-   Timeout completion is idempotent.

-   Manual completion and timeout completion cannot produce two result
    sets.

This is particularly important for Exam Mode.

Also consider a last_activity_at / heartbeat only if needed for session
recovery; don\'t use it to determine the exam deadline.

**6. 🔴 Exam Mode answer-lock needs reconsideration**

I would change this before freezing.

Your specification currently makes:

**Exam Mode → answer cannot be changed once submitted.**

That is a product choice, but it is **not something I would present as
an accurate simulation of the real AKT without qualification**.

The GMC describes the AKT as a single-best-answer assessment, but the
exact delivery arrangements differ between assessment providers. The
current GMC material confirms that the MLA content map is the framework
for the AKT, while delivery requirements are not simply equivalent to
one AMaC interface. ([GMC
UK](https://www.gmc-uk.org/education/medical-licensing-assessment/mla-content-map?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

For example, PLAB 1 is currently a 180-question, three-hour written SBA
examination. ([GMC
UK](https://www.gmc-uk.org/registration-and-licensing/join-our-registers/plab/plab-1-guide/what-is-the-plab-1-exam?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

So I recommend changing the architecture to:

**Exam Mode answer change:** configurable by practice_session_config.

Then AMaC can support:

-   allow_answer_change = true for a more realistic exam simulation

-   potentially false for a deliberately stricter training mode

But don\'t hard-code "cannot change answers" as though it were a GMC
requirement.

More importantly, **do not call 60 questions / 60 minutes "UKMLA exam
conditions."** Call it an AMaC exam simulation unless the configuration
has been deliberately constructed to reproduce a specified assessment
format.

**7. 🟠 Don\'t hard-code 60 questions / 60 minutes as the implied UKMLA
format**

The current UI says:

"Time limit (60 minutes for 60 questions)."

That\'s fine as an **AMaC practice configuration**, but it shouldn\'t
imply that this is the actual UKMLA format.

The GMC\'s current material shows that delivery arrangements can differ
between assessment providers; for example, the current PLAB 1 format is
180 questions in three hours. ([GMC
UK](https://www.gmc-uk.org/registration-and-licensing/join-our-registers/plab/plab-1-guide/what-is-the-plab-1-exam?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Change the wording to something like:

"Example AMaC exam simulation: 60 questions / 60 minutes."

And let practice_session_config define any officially modelled
simulation separately.

**8. 🟠 Add unanswered questions to exam results**

Your result currently has:

correct_count

incorrect_count

percentage

But an exam session can contain unanswered questions.

Add:

answered_count

unanswered_count

and define:

incorrect_count = answered_count - correct_count

or explicitly define all three independently.

The actual AKT scoring model also treats unanswered items differently
from correct answers, so your internal result model should not obscure
unanswered responses. ([GMC
UK](https://www.gmc-uk.org/-/media/documents/plab---mla-akt-compliance-report-and-decision-report_pdf-107168046.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

**9. 🟠 practice_session_questions.is_correct should be explicitly a
projection**

You currently store:

is_correct

selected_answer_id

That\'s reasonable for fast session retrieval, **provided it is not
another source of truth**.

Add:

practice_session_questions is a session-level projection/cache of the
canonical attempt state. Canonical attempt records remain authoritative
for mastery, coverage and longitudinal analytics.

Same principle as 014.

**10. 🟠 Exam completion needs an explicit server transaction**

The current flow is broadly correct but should state that completion is
atomic.

When completing:

validate session

→ acquire session lock

→ verify still in_progress

→ verify deadline

→ finalise unanswered questions

→ calculate results from canonical/session answers

→ mark completed

→ persist completion event

→ trigger downstream processing

This prevents two browser tabs from both completing the same exam.

It also prevents:

-   manual completion + timeout simultaneously

-   double completion

-   duplicate analytics

-   duplicate downstream attempt processing.

**11. 🟡 Abandoned sessions need clearer attempt semantics**

You currently say:

"Attempts still logged: For coverage/mastery (partial session still
counts as attempts)."

This is potentially correct, but it must defer to the canonical attempt
and 014\'s coverage_config.

Don\'t make 015 decide that an abandoned question is automatically
eligible.

Change to:

Submitted questions in an abandoned session are recorded through the
canonical attempt system. Whether they contribute to mastery or coverage
is determined by UKMLA-007 and UKMLA-014\'s respective rules.

That keeps ownership clean.

**12. 🟡 Add session configuration snapshot**

I\'d also add these fields:

practice_config_version

mode_configuration_snapshot_json

The second one is optional, but useful.

For example, if v1.0 said:

{

\"allow_answer_change\": false,

\"show_hints\": false,

\"time_limit_seconds\": 3600

}

and v1.1 later changes the rules, an existing session must continue
using the configuration under which it started.

This is especially important for an in-progress exam.

**The architecture I would freeze**

After those amendments, the flow becomes:
