The fundamental distinction is:

**012 decides what matters.**

**019 decides what is due.**

**023 decides what clinical performance evidence shows.**

**021 decides how performance has changed.**

**024 decides how today is organised.**

**027 explains where the candidate is in the overall journey and
connects those capabilities into one coherent experience.**

That is the correct architectural role for 027.

**My verdict**

**The original draft: AMEND --- do not freeze.**

**The revised version above: APPROVE / FREEZE as v1.0 FINAL**, subject
only to your confirmation.

The most important architectural improvement is the removal of the
**composite readiness score**. That one change prevents 027 from
becoming an accidental "super-engine" sitting above 007, 021 and 023. It
also makes the product claim much safer: AMaC can show a candidate
**where they are, what evidence supports that position, what stage they
are in, and what happens next**, without pretending it has a validated
probability of passing.

The current GMC framework also supports the separation of the knowledge
and clinical-performance tracks: the MLA has AKT and CPSA components,
and PLAB 1/2 correspond to those respective requirements.
([GMC](https://www.gmc-uk.org/education/medical-licensing-assessment/mla-content-map?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

**I would therefore freeze 027 after this amendment.**

**UKMLA-028 --- Content Authoring, Editorial Workflow & Quality
Assurance Platform**

**Version:** v1.0 DRAFT --- FOR REVIEW\
**Date:** Thursday, October 08, 2026\
**Phase:** D\
**Priority:** VERY HIGH

**Executive Decision**

UKMLA-028 is the next major AMaC capability.

Its purpose is to provide the **unified editorial production layer**
through which AMaC safely creates, clinically reviews, versions,
approves, publishes, updates and retires the content that powers its
preparation systems.

The core product question is:

**\"How does AMaC safely create, clinically review, version, approve,
publish, update and retire the content that powers its preparation
systems?\"**

This is fundamentally different from existing systems:

**003**: canonical GMC/MLA content mapping (consumed by 028 during
authoring)

**005**: question attempts and outcomes (runtime authority, not
authoring)

**020**: mock examination composition and scoring (runtime authority,
not authoring)

**023**: CPSA/clinical-performance assessment (runtime authority, not
station authoring)

**025**: standalone learning content (published content authority, not
authoring workflow)

**026**: interactive clinical reasoning tutor (runtime authority, not
scenario authoring)

**028 is the editorial factory, not the runtime content authority.**

**1. Core Product Question**

**003 asks:**

\"How is knowledge mapped to GMC/MLA frameworks?\"

**005 asks:**

\"What were the question attempts and outcomes?\"

**020 asks:**

\"How did the candidate perform on the mock examination?\"

**023 asks:**

\"Can the candidate demonstrate clinical performance?\"

**025 asks:**

\"Where does the candidate go to learn and understand this?\"

**026 asks:**

\"How should the candidate reason through this clinical problem?\"

**028 asks:**

**\"How does AMaC safely create, review, version, approve, publish and
maintain the content that powers these systems?\"**

This is an **editorial production** capability, not a runtime learning
or assessment system.

**2. Strategic Objective**

028 should transform AMaC from a system that consumes content into a
system that **safely produces content at scale with full clinical
governance**.

The intended workflow:

Author creates draft

↓

Clinical reviewer assigned

↓

Clinical review completed

↓

Editorial QA completed

↓

Approval granted

↓

Publication scheduled

↓

Content published

↓

Runtime systems consume published content

↓

GMC map changes

↓

Affected content identified

↓

Editorial review triggered

↓

Amend/version

↓

Re-approve

↓

Republish

The key differentiator is therefore not simply:

\"AMaC has questions.\"

It is:

**\"AMaC can safely produce, clinically review, version and maintain
questions, stations, learning content and reasoning scenarios with full
audit trail and provenance.\"**

**3. Critical Ownership Principle**

**028 owns editorial production workflow.**

It does **not** own runtime content meaning, assessment logic, mastery
calculation, recommendations, or learning orchestration.

The frozen ownership model is:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **System**   **Authority**
  ------------ ----------------------------------------------------------------
  000          Authentication / identity

  **003**      **GMC/MLA canonical content mapping (consumed by 028 during
               authoring)**

  005          Canonical question attempts and question-level outcomes (runtime
               authority)

  007          Knowledge mastery

  008--010     Diagnostic lifecycle

  011          Dashboard presentation

  012          Recommendations

  013          Manual override for recommendations

  014          Content-map coverage

  015          AKT learning/exam mode

  016          Immediate weakness-loop practice

  017          Homepage / conversion

  018          Commercial entitlement

  019          Knowledge review scheduling

  **020**      **Mock examination lifecycle and scoring (runtime authority,
               consumes 028-published questions)**

  021          Longitudinal analytics

  022          Communication

  **023**      **CPSA/clinical-performance assessment (runtime authority,
               consumes 028-published stations)**

  024          Daily study plan / command centre

  **025**      **Standalone clinical learning content (published content
               authority, consumes 028-published learning content)**

  026          Interactive clinical reasoning tutor (runtime authority,
               consumes 028-published scenarios)

  027          Unified UKMLA/PLAB readiness journey

  **028**      **Content authoring, editorial workflow & quality assurance
               (editorial factory)**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

**4. Non-Negotiable Boundary**

**028 is the editorial production layer. It may create, review, version,
approve, publish and retire content, but it may not own the runtime
meaning, assessment logic, mastery calculation, recommendations,
learning orchestration or performance assessment performed by downstream
systems.**

028 produces:

Draft questions (for 005 runtime)

Draft stations (for 023 runtime)

Draft learning content (for 025 runtime)

Draft reasoning scenarios (for 026 runtime)

Editorial workflow state

Clinical review records

Version history

Publication records

Retirement records

Change history

Content provenance

Quality assurance records

028 does **not** produce:

Question attempts or outcomes (005 owns this)

Mock composition or scoring (020 owns this)

Clinical-performance assessment (023 owns this)

Learning content runtime meaning (025 owns this)

Interactive tutoring (026 owns this)

Mastery state (007 owns this)

Recommendations (012 owns this)

Review scheduling (019 owns this)

Daily plans (024 owns this)

Journey state (027 owns this)

**5. 028 Is Not a Runtime Content Authority**

This is a central design rule.

**028 decides:**

\"This question is ready for publication after clinical review.\"

**005 decides:**

\"This is how candidates performed on this question.\"

**028 decides:**

\"This station is clinically accurate and ready for use.\"

**023 decides:**

\"This is how the candidate performed on this station.\"

**028 decides:**

\"This learning content is approved and published.\"

**025 decides:**

\"This is how the learning content is presented and consumed.\"

**028 decides:**

\"This reasoning scenario is clinically sound.\"

**026 decides:**

\"This is how the tutoring interaction proceeds.\"

028 must not independently calculate:

Question performance (005 owns this)

Mock scoring (020 owns this)

Clinical-performance assessment (023 owns this)

Learning content runtime meaning (025 owns this)

Interactive tutoring logic (026 owns this)

Mastery state (007 owns this)

Recommendations (012 owns this)

Review scheduling (019 owns this)

Daily plans (024 owns this)

Journey state (027 owns this)

028 supports four content families with unified workflow infrastructure:

**7. Data Model**

**7.1 Content Definitions**

content_definitions

**Frozen principle:**

content_definitions is the editorial factory\'s master record for
content under production. It is not the runtime content database.

Fields:

id (PK, UUID)

content_type (enum: AKT_QUESTION, CPSA_STATION, LEARNING_CONTENT,
REASONING_SCENARIO)

content_family (enum: AKT, CPSA, LEARNING, REASONING)

title (string --- working title for editorial use)

description (text, nullable)

status (enum: DRAFT, IN_REVIEW, IN_QA, APPROVED, PUBLISHED, RETIRED,
SUPERSEDED)

current_version_id (FK to content_versions.id, nullable)

author_id (FK to users.id --- editorial author)

clinical_reviewer_id (FK to users.id, nullable --- assigned clinical
reviewer)

content_mapping_version (string --- GMC/MLA map version at time of
authoring)

created_at (timestamp)

updated_at (timestamp)

**Constraint:**

INDEX(content_type, status)

**Frozen principle:**

028 owns the editorial workflow. Published content is consumed by
runtime systems (005, 020, 023, 025, 026).

**7.2 Content Versions**

content_versions

**Frozen principle:**

content_versions captures immutable published snapshots. Each version is

Fields:

id (PK, UUID)

content_definition_id (FK to content_definitions.id, indexed)

version_number (integer)

version_label (string, nullable --- e.g. \"v2.1\", \"Hotfix 2026-10\")

content_body_json (JSON --- versioned content payload, schema varies by
content_type)

content_schema_version (string --- schema version for this content type)

clinical_review_status (enum: PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, APPROVED, REJECTED,
CONDITIONAL)

clinical_reviewer_id (FK to users.id, nullable)

clinical_review_date (timestamp, nullable)

clinical_review_comments (text, nullable)

editorial_qa_status (enum: PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, PASSED, FAILED,
CONDITIONAL)

editorial_qa_reviewer_id (FK to users.id, nullable)

editorial_qa_date (timestamp, nullable)

editorial_qa_comments (text, nullable)

approval_status (enum: PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED, CONDITIONAL)

approver_id (FK to users.id, nullable --- final approver)

approval_date (timestamp, nullable)

approval_comments (text, nullable)

publication_status (enum: UNPUBLISHED, SCHEDULED, PUBLISHED, RETIRED,
SUPERSEDED)

published_at (timestamp, nullable)

retired_at (timestamp, nullable)

superseded_by_version_id (FK to content_versions.id, nullable)

change_summary (text --- author\'s summary of changes in this version)

gmc_map_version_at_publication (string --- GMC/MLA map version when
published)

created_at (timestamp)

updated_at (timestamp)

**Constraint:**

UNIQUE(content_definition_id, version_number)

**Frozen principle:**

Published versions are immutable. Changes create new versions.

**8. Editorial Workflow**

**8.1 Authoring Workflow**

Author creates draft (content_definitions, content_versions)

↓

Clinical reviewer assigned (clinical_review_records)

↓

Clinical review completed (clinical_review_records updated)

↓

Editorial QA performed (editorial_qa_records)

↓

QA passed (editorial_qa_records updated)

↓

Approval granted (content_versions.approval_status = APPROVED)

↓

Publication scheduled (content_publication_records)

↓

Content published (content_publication_records.published_at)

↓

Runtime systems consume published content (005, 020, 023, 025, 026)

**Frozen principle:**

028 owns the editorial workflow. Runtime systems own content consumption
and meaning.

**8.2 Clinical Review Workflow**

Clinical reviewer assigned

↓

Reviewer accesses draft content

↓

Reviewer checks clinical accuracy

↓

Reviewer checks guideline references

↓

Reviewer checks safety concerns

↓

Reviewer submits review (clinical_review_records)

↓

Review status: APPROVED, REJECTED, or CONDITIONAL

↓

If CONDITIONAL: author revises, new version created

↓

If APPROVED: content proceeds to editorial QA

**Frozen principle:**

Clinical review is captured in 028. Clinical accuracy at runtime is the
responsibility of downstream systems.

**8.3 Editorial QA Workflow**

QA reviewer assigned

↓

Reviewer runs structured QA checklist

↓

Duplicate check performed

↓

Completeness check performed

↓

Schema validation performed

↓

Mapping validation performed (003)

↓

Accessibility check performed (for learning content)

↓

QA status: PASSED, FAILED, or CONDITIONAL

↓

If CONDITIONAL: author revises, new version created

↓

If PASSED: content proceeds to approval

**Frozen principle:**

Editorial QA is captured in 028. Runtime content validation is the
responsibility of downstream systems.

**8.4 Approval Workflow**

Approver accesses approved content

↓

Approver reviews clinical review record

↓

Approver reviews QA record

↓

Approver grants approval (content_versions.approval_status = APPROVED)

↓

Publication scheduled (content_publication_records)

↓

Content published at scheduled time

**Frozen principle:**

Approval is captured in 028. Runtime content authority remains with
downstream systems.

**8.5 Publication Workflow**

Publication scheduled

↓

At scheduled time:

↓

Content marked PUBLISHED (content_publication_records)

↓

Runtime systems notified (event: content.published)

↓

Runtime systems consume published content

**Frozen principle:**

028 publishes content. Runtime systems consume and interpret content.

**8.6 Retirement Workflow**

Retirement decision made (author, clinical reviewer, or automated)

↓

Retirement reason recorded

↓

Content marked RETIRED (content_publication_records)

↓

Runtime systems notified (event: content.retired)

↓

Runtime systems handle retired content (e.g. hide from new candidates,
retain for historical records)

**Frozen principle:**

028 retires content. Runtime systems decide how to handle retired
content.

**8.7 Supersession Workflow**

New version created (content_versions)

↓

New version approved and published

↓

Previous version marked SUPERSEDED (content_publication_records)

↓

superseded_by_version_id set

↓

Runtime systems notified (event: content.superseded)

↓

Runtime systems migrate to new version

**Frozen principle:**

028 supersedes content. Runtime systems migrate to new versions.

**9. GMC/MLA Map Change Handling**

The GMC\'s MLA content map is live and under revision. 028 must handle
map changes
systematically.\[[ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws](https://ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws.com/web/direct-files/attachments/140542714/2a57c912-dd24-400d-b34c-28ef2ec8ff5c/UKMLA-IMPROVEMENT-PROJECT.docx)\]

**9.1 Map Change Detection**

GMC releases new MLA content map version

↓

028 detects map change (manual or automated)

↓

gmc_map_impact_records created

↓

Affected content identified (gmc_map_affected_content)

↓

Impact assessment performed

↓

Review triggered for affected content

**Frozen principle:**

003 owns canonical GMC/MLA mapping. 028 tracks content affected by map
changes.

**9.2 Impact Assessment**

For each affected content item:

↓

Determine impact type:

\- MAPPING_CHANGED (canonical target changed)

\- CONTENT_OUTDATED (content no longer aligned)

\- GUIDELINE_CHANGED (underlying guideline updated)

\- SAFETY_CONCERN (safety issue identified)

↓

Set review_required flag

↓

Assign reviewer

↓

Review completed: gmc_map_affected_content.review_status = COMPLETED

**Frozen principle:**

028 tracks impact. 003 owns canonical mapping.

**9.3 Content Revision Trigger**

Review identifies required changes

↓

New version created (content_versions)

↓

Clinical review performed

↓

Editorial QA performed

↓

Approval granted

↓

Publication scheduled

↓

New version published

↓

Previous version superseded

**Frozen principle:**

028 manages revision workflow. Runtime systems consume revised content.

**10. Content APIs**

**10.1 Create Content Definition**

POST /api/v1/content/definitions

Request:

{

\"content_type\": \"AKT_QUESTION\",

\"content_family\": \"AKT\",

\"title\": \"Heart Failure Diagnosis\",

\"description\": \"AKT question on heart failure diagnosis\",

\"author_id\": \"uuid\"

}

Response:

{

\"content_definition\": {

\"id\": \"uuid\",

\"content_type\": \"AKT_QUESTION\",

\"status\": \"DRAFT\",

\"created_at\": \"2026-10-08T08:00:00Z\"

}

}

**10.2 Create Content Version**

POST /api/v1/content/definitions/{definition_id}/versions

Request:

{

\"version_number\": 1,

\"content_body_json\": {

\"stem\": \"A 72-year-old presents with\...\",

\"options\": \[\...\],

\"answer\": \"B\",

\"rationale\": \"\...\",

\"teaching_points\": \[\...\],

\"difficulty\": \"intermediate\",

\"clinical_references\": \[\...\],

\"content_map_ids\": \[\"uuid-1\", \"uuid-2\"\]

},

\"change_summary\": \"Initial version\"

}

**10.3 Submit Clinical Review**

POST /api/v1/content/versions/{version_id}/clinical-review

Request:

{

\"reviewer_id\": \"uuid\",

\"review_comments\": \"Clinically accurate, minor wording suggestion\",

\"clinical_accuracy_rating\": \"ACCURATE\",

\"guideline_references_checked\": \[\"NICE CG108\", \"ESC 2021\"\],

\"safety_concerns\": null,

\"recommended_changes\": \"Consider clarifying option C wording\"

}

**10.4 Submit Editorial QA**

POST /api/v1/content/versions/{version_id}/editorial-qa

Request:

{

\"qa_reviewer_id\": \"uuid\",

\"qa_checklist_json\": {\...},

\"duplicate_check_passed\": true,

\"completeness_check_passed\": true,

\"schema_validation_passed\": true,

\"mapping_validation_passed\": true,

\"issues_found\": null,

\"recommended_changes\": null

}

**10.5 Approve Content**

POST /api/v1/content/versions/{version_id}/approve

Request:

{

\"approver_id\": \"uuid\",

\"approval_comments\": \"Approved for publication\"

}

**10.6 Publish Content**

POST /api/v1/content/versions/{version_id}/publish

Request:

{

\"publication_channel\": \"AKT_QUESTION_BANK\",

\"runtime_system_id\": \"005\",

\"scheduled_at\": \"2026-10-10T00:00:00Z\"

}

**10.7 Retire Content**

POST /api/v1/content/versions/{version_id}/retire

Request:

{

\"retired_by_id\": \"uuid\",

\"retirement_reason\": \"Guideline updated, content outdated\"

}

**10.8 Get Content Change History**

GET /api/v1/content/definitions/{definition_id}/history

Returns chronological change history for editorial audit.

**11. Content Validation**

**11.1 Schema Validation**

Each content type has a structured schema:

AKT_QUESTION: stem, options, answer, rationale, teaching_points,
difficulty, references, mapping

CPSA_STATION: instructions, scenario, actor_brief, examiner_material,
expected_actions, rubric, safety_criteria, references, mapping

LEARNING_CONTENT: title, objectives, sections, resources, references,
mapping

REASONING_SCENARIO: context, starting_information, reasoning_objective,
expected_steps, acceptable_variants, misconceptions, references, mapping

028 validates content against schema before publication.

**Frozen principle:**

028 validates content structure. Runtime systems validate content
meaning.

**11.2 Duplicate Detection**

028 checks for duplicate content:

Textual similarity (stem, title, scenario)

Canonical mapping overlap

Clinical concept overlap

**Frozen principle:**

028 detects duplicates. Runtime systems decide whether to accept similar
content.

**11.3 Completeness Check**

028 checks for editorial completeness:

All required fields present

Clinical references provided

Mapping provided (003)

Teaching points provided (for questions)

Safety criteria provided (for stations)

**Frozen principle:**

028 checks completeness. Runtime systems may have additional
requirements.

**11.4 Mapping Validation**

028 validates mapping against 003:

Canonical content_map_ids exist in 003

Mapping is appropriate for content type

Mapping version is recorded

**Frozen principle:**

003 owns canonical mapping. 028 validates mapping references.

AI cannot publish content

Shall I proceed to review and refine this draft, or would you like to
stress-test specific boundaries?

I have reviewed the draft against the **frozen 000--027 architecture**,
including the current GMC position. My verdict is:

**UKMLA-028 is the correct next capability, but the draft should NOT be
frozen as written.**

There is **one major architectural correction** and several important
secondary amendments.

The good news is that the **concept, strategic direction, four
pipelines, clinical governance, GMC-map handling and unified workflow
are all correct**.

The major issue is that the draft has accidentally turned 028 into the
**owner of content records themselves**, whereas 023, 025 and 026
already own their respective content definitions/versions. That would
create duplicate CMS/content authorities.

The GMC confirms that the MLA content map is a live document, provides
the framework for both AKT and CPSA, and the current version applies to
MLA assessments from September 2026; it also notes a September 2026
terminology/content update from PCOS to PMOS.
([GMC](https://www.gmc-uk.org/education/medical-licensing-assessment/mla-content-map?utm_source=chatgpt.com))
This makes the governance capability in 028 particularly important.

**Verdict**

**Status should become:**

**UKMLA-028 --- AMENDED / APPROVED / FROZEN / v1.0 FINAL**

---but only after the amendments below.

**1. THE MAJOR PROBLEM: 028 OWNS TOO MUCH**

Your draft says:

\"content_definitions is the editorial factory\'s master record for
content under production.\"

This conflicts with the frozen architecture.

**025 already owns**

learning_content_definitions\
learning_content_versions\
learning_content_sections

Therefore 028 cannot also own generic content_definitions representing
those same resources.

**023 already owns**

cpsa_station_definitions\
cpsa_station_versions\
cpsa_rubrics

Therefore 028 cannot become the authoritative owner of station
definitions/versions.

**026 already owns**

reasoning_scenarios\
reasoning_scenario_versions

Therefore 028 cannot become the authoritative owner of reasoning
scenarios.

And the question content service already conceptually owns question
content, while 005 owns **attempts/outcomes**, not question authoring or
question content itself.

So this:

028

↓

content_definitions

↓

runtime systems

should **not** be the architecture.

It would create:

028 content definition

\+

023 station definition

028 content definition

\+

025 learning definition

028 content definition

\+

026 scenario definition

That is precisely the duplication we have been trying to prevent across
000--027.

**2. THE CORRECT ARCHITECTURE**

The clean architecture is:

UKMLA-028

Editorial Production Layer

│

┌──────────┼───────────┐

│ │ │

↓ ↓ ↓

Editorial Review/QA Publication

workflow workflow release

│

↓

┌─────┴──────┬──────────┬───────────┐

↓ ↓ ↓ ↓

Question 023 025 026

content stations learning reasoning

owner owner owner owner

In other words:

**028 owns the production workflow around content. The domain systems
own the content itself.**

This is the single most important amendment.

**3. REPLACE THE CENTRAL OWNERSHIP PRINCIPLE**

I recommend replacing your current wording with:

**028 owns AMaC\'s unified editorial production workflow and governance
layer. It does not become the canonical owner of domain content. Domain
systems remain authoritative for their own content definitions, schemas,
versions and runtime meaning. 028 provides the common authoring
workflow, review, QA, approval, release, provenance, audit and
publication orchestration around those domain-owned content artifacts.**

This is much safer.

Importantly, **do not remove the four pipelines**.

They are correct.

But their ownership becomes:

                    workflow                         service

  stations          workflow

                    workflow

  scenarios         workflow

So 028 becomes the **common editorial operating system**, rather than a
fifth content database.

I would rename it:

**editorial_release_records**

because 028 is recording a **release decision**, not becoming the
canonical runtime publication database.

Fields could include:

id

editorial_work_item_id

domain_content_id

domain_content_version_id

release_status

scheduled_at

released_at

released_by_id

target_domain

release_reference

supersedes_domain_version_id

retirement_request

created_at

updated_at

The downstream system then confirms:

content.release.completed

or equivalent.

This gives you a clean two-phase release:

028 authorises release

↓

domain owner activates

**11. PUBLICATION MUST BE TRANSACTIONAL AND IDEMPOTENT**

This is missing from the draft at sufficient depth.

You need to protect against:

double publication

two publishers clicking simultaneously

scheduled publication racing with retirement

publication racing with a new version

failed downstream activation

downstream activation succeeding but response being lost

duplicate release events.

Therefore:

**Every release operation must have an idempotency key and immutable
release identifier.**

The workflow should not reach:

PUBLISHED

until the relevant domain system confirms successful activation.

Alternatively, 028 can have:

RELEASE_AUTHORISED

RELEASE_REQUESTED

RELEASE_CONFIRMED

RELEASE_FAILED

I strongly prefer this.

**12. THE WORKFLOW STATE MACHINE SHOULD BE IMPROVED**

Your current:

DRAFT

→ IN_REVIEW

→ IN_QA

→ APPROVED

→ PUBLISHED

is too coarse.

I recommend:

DRAFT

↓

READY_FOR_CLINICAL_REVIEW

↓

CLINICAL_REVIEW

↓

CLINICAL_REVIEW_PASSED

↓

READY_FOR_QA

↓

EDITORIAL_QA

↓

QA_PASSED

↓

READY_FOR_APPROVAL

↓

APPROVED

↓

RELEASE_SCHEDULED

↓

RELEASE_REQUESTED

↓

RELEASE_CONFIRMED

↓

SUPERSEDED / RETIRED

Failure paths:

CLINICAL_REVIEW_FAILED

QA_FAILED

APPROVAL_REJECTED

RELEASE_FAILED

with return-to-draft/revision behaviour.

This gives engineering a real state machine rather than relying on
loosely related status fields.

**13. SEPARATION OF DUTIES SHOULD BE MANDATORY**

This is an important missing governance protection.

For clinical content, I recommend:

**An author cannot approve their own content.**

And ideally:

**The final approver should not be the sole clinical reviewer for
high-risk clinical content.**

At minimum:

Author

≠

Clinical reviewer

and:

Author

≠

Approver

for published clinical content.

For safety-critical stations/questions, configurable dual review should
be possible.

**14. CLINICAL REVIEW SHOULD BE CONTENT-TYPE SPECIFIC**

Your current workflow is good, but one universal review process isn\'t
enough.

For example:

**AKT question**

Clinical reviewer checks:

factual accuracy

answer correctness

distractor plausibility

guideline alignment

ambiguity

clinical safety.

**CPSA station**

Reviewer additionally checks:

scenario realism

task clarity

actor instructions

safety-critical criteria

acceptable performance variants

scoring/rubric coherence.

**Learning content**

Reviewer checks:

factual accuracy

current guidance

clinical completeness

references

outdated terminology.

**Reasoning scenario**

Reviewer checks:

starting facts

expected reasoning

acceptable alternative reasoning

safety-critical reasoning

misconception model

clinical references.

Therefore 028 should have:

**a common workflow with content-family-specific validation and review
checklists.**

That is better than four separate CMSs.

**15. GMC MAP HANDLING IS CORRECT IN PRINCIPLE --- BUT THE SOURCE OF THE
EVENT MUST BE 003**

Your draft says:

"028 detects map change."

I would amend this.

**003 owns the canonical map.**

Therefore:

003

↓

gmc_map.version_published

↓

028

↓

impact assessment

028 should not independently become another GMC-map monitoring
authority.

It can receive:

map_version_created

map_version_activated

map_nodes_added

map_nodes_changed

map_nodes_retired

map_relationships_changed

from 003.

Then 028 performs editorial impact analysis.

This preserves the boundary.

**16. YOUR MAP IMPACT MODEL NEEDS MORE DETAIL**

The current:

MAPPING_CHANGED

CONTENT_OUTDATED

GUIDELINE_CHANGED

SAFETY_CONCERN

is useful but incomplete.

I would add:

TARGET_ADDED

TARGET_RENAMED

TARGET_MOVED

TARGET_RETIRED

TARGET_RELATIONSHIP_CHANGED

CONTENT_NO_LONGER_ALIGNED

CONTENT_REQUIRES_REVIEW

CLINICAL_GUIDANCE_CHANGED

And importantly:

**A mapping change does not automatically mean the content is clinically
wrong.**

It should generate:

IMPACT_DETECTED

then:

EDITORIAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED

and only the reviewer determines whether revision is necessary.

**17. GUIDELINE CHANGE HANDLING SHOULD ALSO BE EVENT-DRIVEN**

The draft focuses heavily on GMC-map changes.

But clinically outdated content may occur without a GMC map change.

For example:

new NICE guidance

new BNF version

new resuscitation guidance

new national safety guidance

Therefore 028 should support:

external clinical-reference update

↓

affected content identification

↓

editorial review

↓

version/review workflow

However, don\'t make 028 a general external guideline monitoring engine
in v1.

It should support **reference-change ingestion**, with actual source
monitoring configurable later.

**18. AI ASSISTANCE SHOULD BE MOVED EARLIER**

Your Phase 3 says AI-assisted authoring is later.

That\'s fine as a product rollout.

But architecturally, **AI provenance should be built into v1 schemas
now**, even if AI generation is initially disabled.

For example:

ai_assistance_used

ai_provider

ai_model

ai_model_version

ai_workflow_version

ai_generation_id

ai_generated_at

human_review_required

Why?

Because retrofitting provenance after hundreds or thousands of
AI-assisted items have been produced is painful.

So:

**AI capability can be Phase 3; AI provenance architecture should be
v1.**

**19. DUPLICATE DETECTION SHOULD NOT BE PHASE 4**

Same issue.

You currently have:

Phase 4 --- Duplicate detection

but duplicate detection is already an explicit publication-quality
requirement in your workflow.

I would make **basic duplicate detection v1**.

It doesn\'t need sophisticated semantic AI.

V1 can detect:

exact duplicate

near-identical stem

identical scenario title

same domain + high textual similarity

same content target + highly similar content.

Advanced semantic similarity can remain later.

**20. SCHEMA VALIDATION SHOULD BE CORE V1**

Likewise:

Schema validation

should not wait until Phase 4.

Without it, the whole idea of a unified editorial platform is weakened.

Make these v1:

schema validation

required-field validation

mapping validation

basic duplicate detection

completeness checks

publication eligibility checks.

Advanced QA can come later.

**21. CONTENT-SPECIFIC SCHEMAS ARE ESSENTIAL**

Your four schemas are good.

But instead of storing them generically as:

content_body_json

I recommend:

domain-specific structured payload

\+

schema_version

with explicit validation adapters:

AKTQuestionValidator

CPSAStationValidator

LearningContentValidator

ReasoningScenarioValidator

This gives you:

common workflow

│

↓ ↓ ↓ ↓

AKT CPSA LC Reasoning

validator\...

rather than one enormous generic schema.

You need a structured issue model rather than relying on:

Add:

**23. ONE MORE IMPORTANT ADDITION: CONTENT DEPENDENCIES**

Because 025/026/023 content may reference other content, 028 should

For example:

↓

**24. RETIREMENT NEEDS A SAFETY OVERRIDE**

Your retirement workflow currently says:

author, clinical reviewer, or automated

I would change this.

**Automated systems should never directly retire clinical content.**

They may:

flag content for urgent review.

But actual retirement requires authorised human action.

Particularly for:

SAFETY_CONCERN

CLINICAL_HARM

SERIOUSLY_OUTDATED

you want:

FLAGGED

↓

URGENT_REVIEW

↓

TEMPORARY_WITHDRAWAL

↓

CLINICAL_DECISION

↓

RETIRED / RESTORED

A future emergency withdrawal mechanism would be very valuable.

**25. ADD WITHDRAWN AS A DISTINCT STATE**

This is different from retirement.

**RETIRED**

Normal planned removal.

**WITHDRAWN**

Urgent temporary removal because of:

clinical safety issue

serious factual error

inappropriate question

broken station

regulatory/content concern.

Historical records remain intact.

This is especially important for medical educational content.

**26. HISTORICAL ATTEMPTS MUST NEVER CHANGE**

This needs an explicit frozen principle.

Suppose:

Question v1

→ candidate answers it

→ later question v1 is withdrawn

→ question v2 replaces it

The historical attempt must still reference:

question_id

question_version_id = v1

and remain immutable.

Same for:

020 mock results

023 station results

026 tutor sessions

025 content consumption

021 analytics.

So add:

**Content retirement, withdrawal or supersession must never mutate
historical candidate records that reference an earlier version.**

**27. THE GMC/PLAB CLAIMS ARE CORRECT, WITH ONE NUANCE**

Your use of the GMC framework is directionally correct.

The GMC currently states that the MLA content map provides the framework
for AKT and CPSA, and that PLAB questions and stations are based on it.
([GMC](https://www.gmc-uk.org/education/medical-licensing-assessment/mla-content-map?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

The GMC also currently states that PLAB 1 meets the MLA AKT requirements
and PLAB 2 meets the MLA CPSA requirements.
([GMC](https://www.gmc-uk.org/education/medical-licensing-assessment/plab-and-the-mla?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

And PLAB 2 currently consists of 16 scenarios of eight minutes each.
([GMC](https://www.gmc-uk.org/registration-and-licensing/join-our-registers/plab/plab-2-guide/what-is-the-plab-2-exam?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

However, **028 should not encode those exam structures as universal
editorial rules**.

The existing 020/023 architecture already correctly treats assessment
configuration as versioned.

So 028 should simply support:

exam_scope

assessment_scope

content_family

and let 020/023 determine runtime applicability.

**28. YOUR publication_channel NEEDS REWORK**

This:

AKT_QUESTION_BANK

CPSA_STATION_BANK

LEARNING_LIBRARY

REASONING_SCENARIO_BANK

MOCK_BANK

creates another problem:

**020 does not own a question bank.**

It consumes eligible questions.

Therefore MOCK_BANK should be removed.

A question can be:

published for question-bank consumption

and 020 subsequently selects eligible published questions.

The same question can potentially be eligible for:

ordinary AKT practice

mock exams

weakness loops

diagnostic use.

028 shouldn\'t determine those runtime usages.

**29. 028 SHOULD NOT HAVE runtime_system_id AS A PRIMARY CONCEPT**

This:

runtime_system_id = \"005\", \"023\", \"025\", \"026\", \"020\"

is too coarse.

Because one content artifact may be consumed by several systems.

For example:

Question

├── 005 attempts

├── 016 weakness loop

├── 020 mock

├── 007 mastery

└── 021 analytics

So use:

domain_owner

for the canonical content owner, and let downstream consumers discover
the published artifact through their own eligibility logic.

For a question:

domain_owner = QUESTION_CONTENT

not:

runtime_system_id = 005

UKMLA-028 --- APPROVED / FROZEN / v1.0 FINAL.**

**UKMLA-028 --- Content Authoring, Editorial Workflow & Quality
Assurance Platform**

**Version:** v1.0 FINAL --- FROZEN / ENGINEERING READY\
**Date:** Thursday, October 08, 2026\
**Phase:** D\
**Priority:** VERY HIGH\
**Status:** APPROVED

**Executive Decision**

UKMLA-028 is the next major AMaC capability.

Its purpose is to provide the **unified editorial production workflow
and governance layer** through which AMaC safely creates, clinically
reviews, versions, approves, releases and maintains the content that
powers its preparation systems.

The core product question is:

**\"How does AMaC safely produce and govern the content that powers its
preparation systems?\"**

**Critical architectural principle:**

**028 owns the editorial workflow and governance layer. Domain systems
retain ownership of their own content definitions, schemas, versions and
runtime meaning.**

This is fundamentally different from existing systems:

**003**: canonical GMC/MLA content mapping (source of map change events)

**Question Content Service**: question content definitions and schemas

**005**: canonical question attempts and question-level outcomes

**020**: mock examination composition and scoring

**023**: CPSA station definitions and clinical-performance assessment

**025**: standalone learning content definitions and runtime

**026**: reasoning scenario definitions and interactive tutoring

**028 is the editorial factory, not the domain content authority.**

**1. Core Product Question**

**003 asks:**

\"How is knowledge mapped to GMC/MLA frameworks?\"

**Question Content Service asks:**

\"What is the canonical question content?\"

**005 asks:**

\"What were the question attempts and outcomes?\"

**020 asks:**

\"How did the candidate perform on the mock examination?\"

**023 asks:**

\"Can the candidate demonstrate clinical performance?\"

**025 asks:**

\"Where does the candidate go to learn and understand this?\"

**026 asks:**

\"How should the candidate reason through this clinical problem?\"

**028 asks:**

**\"How does AMaC safely produce, review, version, approve, release and
maintain the content that powers these systems?\"**

This is an **editorial production and governance** capability, not a
runtime learning, assessment or content authority.

**2. Strategic Objective**

028 should transform AMaC from a system that consumes content into a
system that **safely produces content at scale with full clinical
governance**.

The intended workflow:

Author creates editorial work item

↓

Clinical reviewer assigned

↓

Clinical review completed

↓

Editorial QA completed

↓

Approval granted

↓

Release authorised

↓

Domain system activates published version

↓

Runtime systems consume published content

↓

003 GMC map changes

↓

028 receives map change event

↓

Affected content identified

↓

Editorial review triggered

↓

Amend/version

↓

Re-approve

↓

Re-release

The key differentiator is therefore not simply:

\"AMaC has questions.\"

It is:

**\"AMaC can safely produce, clinically review, version and maintain
questions, stations, learning content and reasoning scenarios with full
audit trail and provenance.\"**

**3. Critical Ownership Principle**

**028 owns editorial production workflow and governance.**

It does **not** own domain content definitions, runtime content meaning,
assessment logic, mastery calculation, recommendations, learning
orchestration or performance assessment.

The frozen ownership model is:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **System**       **Authority**
  ---------------- ------------------------------------------------------
  000              Authentication / identity

  **003**          **GMC/MLA canonical content mapping (source of map
                   change events)**

  Question Content Question content definitions and schemas
  Service          

  005              Canonical question attempts and question-level
                   outcomes

  007              Knowledge mastery

  008--010         Diagnostic lifecycle

  011              Dashboard presentation

  012              Recommendations

  013              Manual override for recommendations

  014              Content-map coverage

  015              AKT learning/exam mode

  016              Immediate weakness-loop practice

  017              Homepage / conversion

  018              Commercial entitlement

  019              Knowledge review scheduling

  **020**          **Mock examination lifecycle and scoring (consumes
                   published questions)**

  021              Longitudinal analytics

  022              Communication

  **023**          **CPSA/clinical-performance assessment (owns station
                   definitions and runtime)**

  024              Daily study plan / command centre

  **025**          **Standalone clinical learning content (owns learning
                   definitions and runtime)**

  026              Interactive clinical reasoning tutor (owns reasoning
                   scenario definitions and runtime)

  027              Unified UKMLA/PLAB readiness journey

  **028**          **Content authoring, editorial workflow & quality
                   assurance (editorial factory)**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**4. Non-Negotiable Boundary**

**028 is the editorial production workflow and governance layer. It may
author, review, version, approve, release and retire editorial work
items, but it may not own the domain content definitions, runtime
meaning, assessment logic, mastery calculation, recommendations,
learning orchestration or performance assessment performed by domain
systems.**

028 produces:

Editorial work items (references to domain content)

Editorial revisions (workflow state, not domain content bodies)

Editorial workflow state

Clinical review records

Editorial QA records

Approval records

Release orchestration records

Editorial issue records

Editorial dependency records

Change history

Content provenance

Quality assurance records

028 does **not** produce:

Domain content definitions (Question Content Service, 023, 025, 026 own
these)

Domain content versions (domain systems own these)

Domain content bodies (domain systems own these)

Question attempts or outcomes (005 owns this)

Mock composition or scoring (020 owns this)

Clinical-performance assessment (023 owns this)

Learning content runtime meaning (025 owns this)

Interactive tutoring (026 owns this)

Mastery state (007 owns this)

Recommendations (012 owns this)

Review scheduling (019 owns this)

Daily plans (024 owns this)

Journey state (027 owns this)

**5. 028 Is Not a Domain Content Authority**

This is a central design rule.

**028 decides:**

\"This editorial work item has passed clinical review and QA.\"

**Domain systems decide:**

\"This is the actual content body and runtime behaviour.\"

**028 decides:**

\"This work item is approved for release.\"

**Domain systems decide:**

\"This content version is now active in the runtime domain.\"

**028 decides:**

\"This work item should be withdrawn due to safety concern.\"

**Domain systems decide:**

\"This content version is withdrawn from runtime use.\"

028 must not independently calculate:

Domain content schemas (domain systems own these)

Domain content bodies (domain systems own these)

Question performance (005 owns this)

Mock scoring (020 owns this)

Clinical-performance assessment (023 owns this)

Learning content runtime meaning (025 owns this)

Interactive tutoring logic (026 owns this)

Mastery state (007 owns this)

Recommendations (012 owns this)

Review scheduling (019 owns this)

Daily plans (024 owns this)

Journey state (027 owns this)

Editorial QA workflow

Approval workflow

Release orchestration

Audit trail

Provenance

**Domain system owns:**

Reasoning scenario definition

Reasoning scenario version

Expected reasoning steps

Runtime tutoring logic

**7. Data Model**

**7.1 Editorial Work Items**

editorial_work_items

editorial_work_items is 028\'s master record for editorial workflow. It
references domain content; it does not own domain content.

**8. Editorial Workflow State Machine**

**8.1 Authoring Workflow**

Author creates editorial work item (DRAFT)

↓

Author submits for clinical review (READY_FOR_CLINICAL_REVIEW)

↓

Clinical reviewer assigned

↓

Clinical review in progress (CLINICAL_REVIEW)

↓

Clinical review completed (CLINICAL_REVIEW_PASSED or
CLINICAL_REVIEW_FAILED)

↓

If PASSED: READY_FOR_QA

↓

Editorial QA in progress (EDITORIAL_QA)

↓

Editorial QA completed (QA_PASSED or QA_FAILED)

↓

If PASSED: READY_FOR_APPROVAL

↓

Approval in progress (APPROVED or APPROVAL_REJECTED)

↓

If APPROVED: RELEASE_SCHEDULED

↓

Release requested (RELEASE_REQUESTED)

↓

Domain system confirms activation (RELEASE_CONFIRMED)

↓

Workflow complete

**Frozen principle:**

028 owns editorial workflow. Domain systems own content activation.

**8.2 Clinical Review Workflow**

Clinical reviewer assigned

↓

Reviewer accesses editorial work item

↓

Reviewer checks clinical accuracy (content-family-specific checklist)

↓

Reviewer checks guideline references

↓

Reviewer checks safety concerns

↓

Reviewer submits review (clinical_review_records)

↓

Review status: APPROVED, REJECTED, or CONDITIONAL

↓

If CONDITIONAL: author revises, new editorial revision created

↓

If APPROVED: workflow proceeds to editorial QA

**Frozen principle:**

Clinical review is captured in 028. Clinical accuracy at runtime is the
responsibility of domain systems.

**8.3 Editorial QA Workflow**

QA reviewer assigned

↓

Reviewer runs structured QA checklist (content-family-specific)

↓

Duplicate check performed (v1: exact, near-identical)

↓

Completeness check performed (v1: required fields, references, mapping)

↓

Schema validation performed (v1: domain-specific schema validators)

↓

Mapping validation performed (003 canonical targets)

↓

Accessibility check performed (for learning content)

↓

QA status: PASSED, FAILED, or CONDITIONAL

↓

If CONDITIONAL: author revises, new editorial revision created

↓

If PASSED: workflow proceeds to approval

**Frozen principle:**

Editorial QA is captured in 028. Runtime content validation is the
responsibility of domain systems.

**8.4 Approval Workflow**

Approver accesses editorial work item

↓

Approver reviews clinical review record

↓

Approver reviews QA record

↓

Approver verifies separation of duties (author ≠ approver)

↓

Approver grants approval (approval_records)

↓

Release authorised (RELEASE_AUTHORISED)

**Frozen principle:**

Approval is captured in 028. Domain systems own content activation.

**8.5 Release Orchestration Workflow (Two-Phase)**

Release authorised (RELEASE_AUTHORISED)

↓

Release scheduled (RELEASE_SCHEDULED)

↓

At scheduled time: release requested (RELEASE_REQUESTED)

↓

Domain system receives release request (idempotent, release_reference)

↓

Domain system activates published version

↓

Domain system confirms activation (RELEASE_CONFIRMED)

↓

028 records release confirmed

**Frozen principle:**

028 orchestrates release. Domain systems activate content.

**8.6 Retirement Workflow**

Retirement decision made (author, clinical reviewer, or flagged by
automated system)

↓

Retirement reason recorded

↓

Automated system flags for review (cannot directly retire clinical
content)

↓

Authorised human action required for retirement

↓

Retirement request submitted
(editorial_release_records.retirement_request = true)

↓

Domain system processes retirement

↓

Domain system confirms retirement

↓

028 records retirement confirmed

**Frozen principle:**

028 orchestrates retirement. Domain systems decide how to handle retired
content. Automated systems cannot directly retire clinical content.

**8.7 Emergency Withdrawal Workflow**

Safety concern identified (SAFETY_CONCERN, CLINICAL_HARM,
SERIOUSLY_OUTDATED)

↓

Content flagged for urgent review (editorial_issues, severity =
CRITICAL)

↓

Urgent clinical review triggered

↓

Temporary withdrawal requested
(editorial_release_records.withdrawal_request = true)

↓

Domain system temporarily withdraws content from runtime use

↓

Clinical decision made: RESTORE or RETIRE

↓

If RETIRE: normal retirement workflow

↓

If RESTORE: content restored with corrections

**Frozen principle:**

028 orchestrates emergency withdrawal. Domain systems temporarily
withdraw content from runtime use.

**8.8 Supersession Workflow**

New editorial revision created

↓

New revision approved and released

↓

Domain system activates new version

↓

Domain system confirms activation

↓

Previous version marked SUPERSEDED (editorial_release_records)

↓

supersedes_domain_version_id set

↓

Historical candidate records retain exact domain_content_version_id
(immutable)

**Frozen principle:**

028 orchestrates supersession. Domain systems migrate to new versions.
Historical candidate records are immutable.

**9. GMC/MLA Map Change Handling**

003 owns canonical GMC/MLA mapping and emits map change events. 028
receives these events and performs editorial impact
analysis.\[[ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws](https://ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws.com/web/direct-files/attachments/140542714/2a57c912-dd24-400d-b34c-28ef2ec8ff5c/UKMLA-IMPROVEMENT-PROJECT.docx)\]

**9.1 Map Change Event Flow**

003 releases new MLA content map version

↓

003 emits map_version_created / map_version_activated event

↓

028 receives event (028 does not independently monitor GMC)

↓

gmc_map_impact_records created

↓

Affected content identified (gmc_map_affected_content)

↓

Impact assessment performed

↓

Review triggered for affected content

**Frozen principle:**

003 owns canonical GMC/MLA mapping and emits map change events. 028
tracks content affected by map changes.

**9.2 Impact Assessment**

For each affected content item:

↓

Determine impact type:

\- MAPPING_CHANGED (canonical target changed)

\- TARGET_ADDED (new target relevant to content)

\- TARGET_RENAMED (target terminology changed)

\- TARGET_MOVED (target hierarchy changed)

\- TARGET_RETIRED (target removed)

\- TARGET_RELATIONSHIP_CHANGED (target relationships changed)

\- CONTENT_NO_LONGER_ALIGNED (content no longer aligned with map)

\- CONTENT_REQUIRES_REVIEW (review recommended)

\- CLINICAL_GUIDANCE_CHANGED (underlying clinical guidance updated)

\- GUIDELINE_CHANGED (guideline reference updated)

\- SAFETY_CONCERN (safety issue identified)

↓

Set review_required flag

↓

Assign reviewer

↓

Review completed: gmc_map_affected_content.review_status = COMPLETED

**Frozen principle:**

028 tracks impact. 003 owns canonical mapping.

**9.3 Content Revision Trigger**

Review identifies required changes

↓

New editorial revision created

↓

Clinical review performed

↓

Editorial QA performed

↓

Approval granted

↓

Release authorised

↓

Domain system activates new version

↓

Previous version superseded

**Frozen principle:**

028 manages revision workflow. Domain systems activate revised content.

**10. Guideline Change Handling**

028 supports external clinical-reference update events (future:
automated ingestion, v1: manual flagging).

External guideline updated (NICE, BNF, resuscitation guidance, national
safety guidance)

↓

Editorial team flags affected content (manual v1)

↓

editorial_issues created (issue_type = OUTDATED or REFERENCE)

↓

Editorial review triggered

↓

Revision workflow proceeds

**Frozen principle:**

028 does not independently monitor external guidelines in v1. Editorial
team flags guideline changes manually.

**11. Separation of Duties**

028 enforces separation of duties for clinical content:

Author ≠ Clinical Reviewer

Author ≠ Approver

Clinical Reviewer ≠ Approver (configurable for high-risk content)

**Frozen principle:**

Separation of duties is mandatory for clinical content. Automated
enforcement in 028.

**12. Content-Family-Specific Review**

028 supports content-family-specific review checklists:

**AKT Question Clinical Review**

Factual accuracy

Answer correctness

Distractor plausibility

Guideline alignment

Ambiguity

Clinical safety

**CPSA Station Clinical Review**

Scenario realism

Task clarity

Actor instructions

Safety-critical criteria

Acceptable performance variants

Scoring/rubric coherence

**Learning Content Clinical Review**

Factual accuracy

Current guidance

Clinical completeness

References

Outdated terminology

**Reasoning Scenario Clinical Review**

Starting facts

Expected reasoning

Acceptable alternative reasoning

Safety-critical reasoning

Misconception model

Clinical references

**Frozen principle:**

Common workflow with content-family-specific validation and review
checklists.

**13. AI-Assisted Authoring Safeguards**

028 may use AI to assist authoring, but with strict safeguards:

**13.1 AI Provenance (Architectural v1)**

ai_assistance_used (boolean)

ai_provider (string)

ai_model (string)

ai_model_version (string)

ai_workflow_version (string)

ai_generation_id (string)

ai_generated_at (timestamp)

human_review_required (boolean, default true)

**Frozen principle:**

AI provenance is architectural v1, even if AI generation is initially
disabled.

**13.2 AI-Assisted, Not AI-Authored**

AI may draft content

Clinical experts must review and approve

Human authorship recorded

**13.3 AI Cannot Approve or Release**

AI cannot approve content

AI cannot release content

AI cannot retire content

AI cannot withdraw content

AI cannot supersede content

**Frozen principle:**

AI is an authoring assistant. Clinical governance remains
human-controlled.

**14. Schema Validation (Core v1)**

028 validates content against domain-specific schemas before release:

**AKT Question Schema**

Stem (required)

Options (required, 4-5 options)

Answer (required)

Rationale (required)

Teaching points (optional)

Difficulty (enum)

Clinical references (required)

Content map IDs (required, validated against 003)

**CPSA Station Schema**

Instructions (required)

Scenario (required)

Actor brief (required)

Examiner material (required)

Expected actions (required)

Rubric (required)

Safety-critical criteria (required)

Acceptable variants (required)

Clinical references (required)

Content map IDs (required, validated against 003)

**Learning Content Schema**

Title (required)

Learning objectives (required)

Sections (required)

Resources (optional)

Clinical references (required)

Content map IDs (required, validated against 003)

**Reasoning Scenario Schema**

Clinical context (required)

Candidate starting information (required)

Reasoning objective (required)

Expected reasoning steps (required)

Acceptable reasoning variants (required)

Common misconceptions (optional)

Clinical references (required)

Content map IDs (required, validated against 003)

**Frozen principle:**

Schema validation is core v1. Domain-specific schema validators
(AKTQuestionValidator, CPSAStationValidator, LearningContentValidator,
ReasoningScenarioValidator).

**15. Duplicate Detection (Core v1)**

028 performs basic duplicate detection before release:

Exact duplicate (identical content)

Near-identical stem (AKT questions)

Identical scenario title (CPSA stations, reasoning scenarios)

Same domain + high textual similarity

Same content target + highly similar content

**Frozen principle:**

Basic duplicate detection is core v1. Advanced semantic similarity can
come later.

**16. Completeness Check (Core v1)**

028 checks for editorial completeness before release:

All required fields present

Clinical references provided

Mapping provided (003)

Teaching points provided (for AKT questions)

Safety criteria provided (for CPSA stations)

**Frozen principle:**

Completeness check is core v1.

**17. Mapping Validation (Core v1)**

028 validates mapping against 003:

Canonical content_map_ids exist in 003

Mapping is appropriate for content type

Mapping version is recorded

**Frozen principle:**

003 owns canonical mapping. 028 validates mapping references.

**18. Permissions and Roles**

028 requires structured permissions:

**18.1 Author**

Create editorial work items

Edit drafts

Submit for review

Revise based on feedback

**18.2 Clinical Reviewer**

Access content under review

Submit clinical review

Check guidelines

Identify safety concerns

Recommend changes

**18.3 Editorial QA Reviewer**

Access content under QA

Run QA checklist

Check duplicates

Validate schema

Validate mapping

Check accessibility (for learning content)

**18.4 Approver**

Access approved content

Review clinical review record

Review QA record

Grant approval

Verify separation of duties

**18.5 Publisher**

Access approved content

Request release

Confirm release

Request retirement (authorised human action required)

Request withdrawal (authorised human action required)

**18.6 Admin**

All permissions

Manage users

Manage workflows

Manage GMC/MLA map impact

**19. Audit Trail**

028 maintains comprehensive audit trail:

All editorial work item changes logged

All editorial revision changes logged

All review actions logged

All approval actions logged

All release actions logged

All retirement actions logged

All withdrawal actions logged

All supersession actions logged

All GMC/MLA map impact actions logged

All editorial issue actions logged

All editorial dependency actions logged

**Frozen principle:**

Audit trail is immutable. Administrative access required for audit log
access.

**20. Content Provenance**

028 captures full content provenance:

Author identity

Clinical reviewer identity

QA reviewer identity

Approver identity

Publisher identity

Creation date

Review dates

Approval date

Release authorised date

Release confirmed date

GMC/MLA map version at each stage

Guideline references at publication

Change history

AI assistance provenance (if used)

**Frozen principle:**

Provenance is captured in 028. Domain systems may use provenance for
their own purposes.

**21. Historical Immutability**

**Frozen principle:**

Content retirement, withdrawal or supersession must never mutate
historical candidate records that reference an earlier
domain_content_version_id.

Historical records retain:

domain_content_id

domain_content_version_id (immutable)

Examples:

005 question attempts

020 mock results

023 station results

026 tutor sessions

025 content consumption

021 analytics

**22. 028 vs 003 --- Editorial vs Mapping**

**Critical boundary clarification:**

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Aspect**     **003 (Canonical Mapping)**          **028 (Editorial
                                                      Workflow)**
  -------------- ------------------------------------ ---------------------------
  **Owns**       GMC/MLA canonical content taxonomy,  Editorial workflow with
                 map change events                    mapping references

  **Scope**      \"Heart failure is mapped to X.Y.Z\" \"This editorial work item
                                                      references X.Y.Z\"

  **Question**   \"How is knowledge structured?\"     \"How is content created
                                                      with mapping?\"

  **Output**     Content-map hierarchy, map change    Editorial workflow with
                 events                               mapping references
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Architecture:**

003

↓

Canonical mapping, map change events

↓

028

↓

Editorial workflow with mapping references

**028 does not create independent taxonomy. It consumes 003\'s canonical
identifiers and map change events.**

**23. 028 vs Question Content Service --- Editorial vs Question
Content**

**Critical boundary clarification:**

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Aspect**     **Question Content Service**  **028 (Editorial Workflow)**
  -------------- ----------------------------- ----------------------------------
  **Owns**       Question content definitions  Editorial workflow for question
                 and schemas                   content

  **Scope**      \"This is the question        \"This question has passed
                 content\"                     editorial governance\"

  **Question**   \"What is the question        \"How is the question produced?\"
                 content?\"                    

  **Output**     Question content definitions, Editorial workflow, release
                 versions                      orchestration
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Architecture:**

028

↓

Editorial workflow, release authorised

↓

Question Content Service

↓

Question content activated

**028 does not own question content. Question Content Service owns
question content definitions and schemas.**

**24. 028 vs 005 --- Editorial vs Outcomes**

**Critical boundary clarification:**

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**34. Acceptance Criteria --- Core**

028 is acceptable only if:

Editorial work items are owned by 028.

Editorial revisions are owned by 028.

Clinical review records are owned by 028.

Editorial QA records are owned by 028.

Approval records are owned by 028.

Editorial release records are owned by 028.

Editorial issues are owned by 028.

Editorial dependencies are owned by 028.

Change history is owned by 028.

GMC/MLA map impact records are owned by 028.

028 does not own domain content definitions (Question Content Service,
023, 025, 026 own these).

028 does not own domain content versions (domain systems own these).

028 does not own domain content bodies (domain systems own these).

028 does not own question attempts/outcomes (005 owns this).

028 does not own mock composition/scoring (020 owns this).

028 does not own clinical-performance assessment (023 owns this).

028 does not own learning content runtime (025 owns this).

028 does not own tutoring logic (026 owns this).

028 does not own canonical mapping (003 owns this).

028 does not own mastery (007 owns this).

028 does not own recommendations (012 owns this).

028 does not own review scheduling (019 owns this).

028 does not own daily plans (024 owns this).

028 does not own journey state (027 owns this).

Editorial workflow state machine is enforced.

Clinical review is mandatory where required by content type.

Editorial QA is mandatory before release.

Approval is mandatory before release.

GMC/MLA map version is recorded at each stage.

Guideline references are recorded at publication.

Change history is comprehensive and immutable.

Audit trail is comprehensive and immutable.

Content provenance is comprehensive.

AI assistance provenance is recorded (architectural v1).

AI cannot approve or release content.

Permissions are role-based and enforced.

Separation of duties is enforced (author ≠ reviewer ≠ approver for
clinical content).

Schema validation is core v1 (domain-specific validators).

Basic duplicate detection is core v1.

Completeness check is core v1.

Mapping validation is core v1 (against 003).

Editorial issues are structured and auditable.

Editorial dependencies are structured and auditable.

Emergency withdrawal is distinct from normal retirement.

Automated systems may flag content but cannot autonomously retire
clinical content.

Historical candidate records retain exact domain_content_version_id
(immutable).

Release operations are transactional and idempotent (release_reference).

003 is the source of GMC/MLA map change events (028 does not
independently monitor GMC).

028 supports four unified production pipelines (AKT, CPSA, Learning,
Reasoning).

028 is the editorial factory; domain systems remain the content
authorities.

**40. Frozen Non-Negotiables**

If 028 is approved, the following become immutable architectural
principles:

**028 owns the unified editorial production and governance workflow.**

**028 does not become the canonical owner of domain content.**

**Domain systems retain ownership of their own content definitions,
schemas, versions and runtime meaning.**

**003 remains the sole canonical GMC/MLA mapping authority and source of
map change events.**

**005 remains the sole authority for question attempts and
question-level outcomes.**

**020 remains the mock examination authority.**

**023 remains the CPSA/clinical-performance authority and station
runtime owner.**

**025 remains the standalone learning-content authority.**

**026 remains the reasoning-scenario and interactive tutoring
authority.**

**028 provides common authoring, clinical review, QA, approval, release
and audit infrastructure across those domains.**

**Published domain content remains immutable.**

**Content changes create new domain versions.**

**Historical candidate records retain the exact
domain_content_version_id used.**

**Clinical review is mandatory where required by content type.**

**Editorial QA is mandatory before release.**

**Approval is mandatory before release.**

**Separation of duties prevents authors from approving their own
clinical content.**

**028 receives GMC-map changes from 003 rather than becoming a second
mapping authority.**

**GMC-map changes generate impact assessment, not automatic content
invalidation.**

**AI may assist authoring but cannot approve or release content.**

**AI provenance is retained even when AI assistance is optional.**

**Basic schema, completeness, mapping and duplicate validation are core
v1 capabilities.**

**028 does not independently determine clinical correctness at
runtime.**

**028 does not calculate mastery, recommendations, coverage, review
schedules, performance, analytics or plans.**

**028 does not become a second CMS for each content type.**

**Release operations are transactional and idempotent.**

**Emergency withdrawal is distinct from normal retirement.**

**Automated systems may flag content but cannot autonomously retire
clinical content.**

**Editorial issues and dependencies are structured and auditable.**

**028 is the editorial factory; domain systems remain the content
authorities.**
