**8. 005 → 029 Analytics Event Contract**

**Frozen principle:**

**005 owns individual question outcomes. 005 emits outcome events to 029
via explicit analytics contract payload. 029 aggregates item-level
analytics asynchronously. 029 does not query 005 database directly.**

**8.1 Analytics Event Payload Schema**

{

\"event_id\": \"uuid\",

\"event_type\": \"QUESTION_OUTCOME\",

\"analytics_contract_version\": \"v1.0\",

\"occurred_at\": \"2026-10-08T09:00:00Z\",

\"question_content_id\": \"uuid\",

\"question_content_version_id\": \"uuid\",

\"attempt_id\": \"uuid\",

\"candidate_cohort_identifier\": \"string\",

\"attempt_number\": 1,

\"is_first_attempt\": true,

\"correctness\": true,

\"selected_option_id\": \"option_A\",

\"time_to_answer_seconds\": 45.2,

\"total_score_excluding_index_item\": 0.72,

\"assessment_session_reference_id\": \"uuid\",

\"assessment_mode\": \"AKT_PRACTICE\",

\"is_valid_attempt\": true,

\"is_voided\": false,

\"has_required_total_score_reference\": true,

\"reference_population_eligible\": true,

\"analytics_window\": \"LAST_30_DAYS\"

}

**Frozen principle:**

**005 remains the authority for these underlying candidate outcome
facts; 029 receives the contracted analytics data and calculates
aggregates.**

**8.2 Required Fields for Corrected Point-Biserial Calculation**

For 029 to calculate corrected point-biserial discrimination, the
following fields are required:

question_content_version_id --- item identity

correctness --- binary item score (0/1)

total_score_excluding_index_item --- reference performance (continuous
0--1)

is_first_attempt --- population filter

is_valid_attempt --- population filter

is_voided --- population filter

has_required_total_score_reference --- population filter

reference_population_eligible --- population filter

analytics_window --- temporal scope

candidate_cohort_identifier --- cohort grouping

attempt_number --- attempt sequencing

occurred_at --- temporal ordering

analytics_contract_version --- contract versioning

**Frozen principle:**

**005 provides the authoritative reference performance data
(total_score_excluding_index_item) required for corrected point-biserial
calculation. 029 does not invent candidate ability.**

**8.3 Required Fields for Option Analysis**

For 029 to perform option analysis, the following fields are required:

question_content_version_id --- item identity

selected_option_id --- which option was selected

correctness --- whether selected option was correct

is_valid_attempt --- population filter

is_voided --- population filter

occurred_at --- temporal ordering

**Frozen principle:**

**005 provides the authoritative selected option data. 029 flags
statistical anomalies; 028/QCS determine clinical/content ambiguity.**

**8.4 Required Fields for Time-to-Answer Aggregates**

For 029 to calculate time-to-answer aggregates, the following fields are
required:

question_content_version_id --- item identity

time_to_answer_seconds --- time spent on item

is_valid_attempt --- population filter

is_voided --- population filter

occurred_at --- temporal ordering

**Frozen principle:**

**005 provides the authoritative time-to-answer data. 029 aggregates
asynchronously.**

**9. Reference Population Definition**

**Frozen principle:**

**Phase 1 discrimination reference population is explicitly defined and
deterministic.**

**9.1 Phase 1 Reference Population Contract**

reference_population =
\"eligible_first_attempt_responses_same_question_version_analytics_window_excluding_invalid_voided_missing_total_score\"

Definition:

\- Eligible first-attempt candidate responses to the same
question_content_version_id

\- Within the defined analytics window (e.g. LAST_30_DAYS, LAST_90_DAYS,
LAST_365_DAYS, ALL_TIME)

\- Excluding invalid attempts (is_valid_attempt = false)

\- Excluding voided attempts (is_voided = true)

\- Excluding attempts lacking the required total-score reference
(has_required_total_score_reference = false)

\- Excluding attempts where reference_population_eligible = false

**Frozen principle:**

**The population definition is versioned through
analytics_method_version. Changes to the population definition require a
new analytics_method_version.**

**9.2 Example Population Filtering**

For discrimination calculation:

\- Filter attempts: is_first_attempt = true

\- Filter attempts: is_valid_attempt = true

\- Filter attempts: is_voided = false

\- Filter attempts: has_required_total_score_reference = true

\- Filter attempts: reference_population_eligible = true

\- Filter attempts: analytics_window = LAST_30_DAYS (or configured
window)

\- Group by: question_content_version_id

\- Calculate: corrected point-biserial(correlated with
total_score_excluding_index_item)

**Frozen principle:**

**Two independent engineering teams implementing 029 will calculate
identical discrimination values given the same 005 outcome events.**

**10. Analytics Status Representation**

**Frozen principle:**

**analytics_status explicitly represents SUFFICIENT_DATA,
INSUFFICIENT_DATA, NOT_AVAILABLE for each calculated metric.**

**10.1 Analytics Status ENUM**

analytics_status ENUM:

\- SUFFICIENT_DATA: metric calculated with attempt_count \>=
minimum_sample_size

\- INSUFFICIENT_DATA: metric null due to attempt_count \<
minimum_sample_size

\- NOT_AVAILABLE: metric not yet calculated, calculation failed, or
temporarily unavailable

**10.2 Application to Metrics**

observed_p_value_analytics_status --- SUFFICIENT_DATA,
INSUFFICIENT_DATA, NOT_AVAILABLE

discrimination_analytics_status --- SUFFICIENT_DATA, INSUFFICIENT_DATA,
NOT_AVAILABLE

time_to_answer_analytics_status --- SUFFICIENT_DATA, INSUFFICIENT_DATA,
NOT_AVAILABLE

**Frozen principle:**

**NULL + analytics_status = INSUFFICIENT_DATA explicitly distinguishes
from calculation failure/staleness (NOT_AVAILABLE).**

{

**11.3 Content Coverage Selection**

Request: cardiology, 20 questions

↓

029 queries question_bank_items:

\- canonical_content_map_ids IN cardiology targets

\- operational_status = ELIGIBLE

\- exposure_count \< threshold

↓

029 selects 20 questions with:

\- balanced author_difficulty

\- selection_tags distribution

\- exposure limits

\- candidate_exclusion_context (from requester)

↓

029 returns selection_id and selected_question_content_version_ids to
requester (015, 016, 020, 008--010)

**Frozen principle:**

029 generates item sets. Runtime systems consume selected questions and
own runtime sessions. **029 does not own candidate exposure history.**

**11.4 Difficulty-Calibrated Selection**

Request: intermediate difficulty, 15 questions

↓

029 queries question_bank_items:

\- author_difficulty BETWEEN 0.4 AND 0.7

\- operational_status = ELIGIBLE

\- discrimination \> 0.2 (if discrimination_analytics_status =
SUFFICIENT_DATA)

↓

029 selects 15 questions with:

\- balanced canonical_content_map_ids coverage

\- exposure limits

↓

029 returns selection to requester

**Frozen principle:**

029 uses observed_p_value and discrimination from 005 outcome events.
Question Content Service owns author_difficulty.

**11.5 Weakness-Loop Similarity Selection**

Request: similar questions for cardiology question X

↓

029 selects similar questions using:

\- canonical_content_map_ids overlap (content-map similarity)

\- question_type compatibility

\- author_difficulty band (±0.15)

\- selection_tags overlap (topic/clinical concept)

\- exclude same question_content_version_id

\- exposure constraints

\- candidate_exclusion_context (from 016)

↓

029 returns 3-5 similar questions to 016

**Frozen principle:**

029 uses defined similarity strategy (content-map, question-type,
difficulty band, topic overlap). 016 owns weakness-loop logic. **029
does not own candidate exposure history.**

**11.6 Mock Composition Item Selection**

020 requests mock item specification:

\- full canonical_content_map_ids coverage (003)

\- difficulty distribution

\- question_type balance

\- exposure limits

\- candidate_exclusion_context (from 020)

↓

029 generates item selection:

\- selected_question_content_version_ids

\- selection_metadata

↓

020 composes mock examination from selected items

**Frozen principle:**

029 generates item selections. 020 owns mock examination composition,
structure, timing, sections, scoring and lifecycle. **029 does not own
candidate exposure history.**

**12. Question Performance Analytics**

029 aggregates 005 outcome events for question performance via
authoritative analytics contract with explicit payload:

**12.1 P-Value (Item Facility)**

005 emits outcome events (analytics_contract_version = v1.0)

↓

029 aggregates asynchronously:

\- attempt_count

\- correct_count

\- observed_p_value = correct_count / attempt_count

↓

If attempt_count \< minimum_sample_size:

\- observed_p_value = null

\- observed_p_value_analytics_status = INSUFFICIENT_DATA

Else:

\- observed_p_value_analytics_status = SUFFICIENT_DATA

↓

029 updates question_bank_items.observed_p_value and
observed_p_value_analytics_status

**Frozen principle:**

005 owns individual question outcomes. 029 aggregates item-level
analytics asynchronously with freshness SLA. **analytics_status
explicitly represents SUFFICIENT_DATA, INSUFFICIENT_DATA,
NOT_AVAILABLE.**

**12.2 Discrimination Index (Corrected Point-Biserial)**

005 emits outcome events with total_score_excluding_index_item

↓

029 filters attempts per reference_population contract:

\- is_first_attempt = true

\- is_valid_attempt = true

\- is_voided = false

\- has_required_total_score_reference = true

\- reference_population_eligible = true

\- analytics_window = configured window

↓

029 calculates discrimination:

\- corrected point-biserial correlation

\- correlation between correctness (0/1) and
total_score_excluding_index_item (continuous 0--1)

\- reference-performance contract explicitly defined:
\"total_score_excluding_index_item\"

\- reference_population:
\"eligible_first_attempt_responses_same_question_version_analytics_window_excluding_invalid_voided_missing_total_score\"

\- discrimination \> 0.3 → good (configurable)

\- discrimination 0.2-0.3 → acceptable (configurable)

\- discrimination \< 0.2 → poor (flag for review, if attempt_count \>=
minimum_sample_size)

↓

If attempt_count \< minimum_sample_size:

\- discrimination = null

\- discrimination_analytics_status = INSUFFICIENT_DATA

Else:

\- discrimination_analytics_status = SUFFICIENT_DATA

**Frozen principle:**

Discrimination uses explicitly defined methodology: corrected
point-biserial, reference-performance contract = total score excluding
index item, reference_population = eligible first-attempt responses
within analytics window excluding invalid/voided/missing total-score.
029 does not invent candidate ability.

**12.3 Option Analysis**

005 emits outcome events with selected_option_id

↓

029 analyses option selection:

\- correct option selection rate

\- distractor effectiveness per option

\- flags statistical anomalies (e.g. distractor selected \>60%, multiple
options frequently selected)

↓

029 flags questions with:

\- statistical anomalies in option_analysis_json

\- does not declare clinical/content ambiguity (028/QCS authority)

**Frozen principle:**

029 flags statistical anomalies. Editorial/content authorities (028/QCS)
determine whether item is actually ambiguous or clinically defective.

**12.4 Exposure Tracking (from QUESTION_PRESENTED Events)**

Runtime systems (015, 016, 020, 008--010) emit QUESTION_PRESENTED
events:

\- event_id (idempotency key)

\- question_content_id

\- question_content_version_id

\- session_reference_id

\- consumer_system

\- occurred_at

↓

029 ingests events asynchronously:

\- exposure_count++

\- exposure_last_presented_at = occurred_at

↓

029 updates question_bank_items.exposure_count and
exposure_last_presented_at

**Frozen principle:**

Exposure means actual presentation (QUESTION_PRESENTED event), not
merely selection. Runtime systems emit exposure events.

**12.5 Time-to-Answer Aggregates**

005 emits outcome events with time_to_answer_seconds

↓

029 aggregates asynchronously:

\- time_to_answer_avg_seconds

\- time_to_answer_std_seconds

↓

If attempt_count \< minimum_sample_size:

\- aggregates = null

\- time_to_answer_analytics_status = INSUFFICIENT_DATA

Else:

\- time_to_answer_analytics_status = SUFFICIENT_DATA

**Frozen principle:**

005 owns individual time-to-answer. 029 aggregates item-level analytics
asynchronously. **analytics_status explicitly represents
SUFFICIENT_DATA, INSUFFICIENT_DATA, NOT_AVAILABLE.**

**13. Item-Quality Recommendation Workflow**

029 generates item-quality recommendations; 028 executes editorial
actions:

**13.1 Automatic Flagging**

029 detects (with minimum sample checks):

\- discrimination \< 0.2 (configurable, if
discrimination_analytics_status = SUFFICIENT_DATA)

\- observed_p_value \> 0.95 or \< 0.2 (configurable, if
observed_p_value_analytics_status = SUFFICIENT_DATA)

\- exposure_count \> threshold (configurable)

\- content outdated (from 028 editorial review)

\- option_analysis_json flags statistical anomalies

↓

029 creates item_quality_recommendations (item-quality recommendation,
not candidate recommendation)

↓

029 refers to 028 editorial workflow (external UUID reference)

**Frozen principle:**

029 generates item-quality recommendations. 028 executes editorial
actions through editorial workflow. **Quality flags never automatically
change operational_status; 029 recommends action, 028/QCS determine
authoritative lifecycle change.**

**13.2 Editorial Review (028)**

028 receives item-quality recommendation

↓

028 creates editorial work item

↓

028 clinical review triggered

↓

028 editorial QA triggered

↓

028 approval workflow

↓

028 release orchestration (retirement/revision)

↓

Question Content Service updates question content state

↓

029 receives authoritative RELEASE_CONFIRMED/retirement event (with
supersedes_question_content_version_id if applicable)

↓

029 updates question_bank_items.operational_status
(ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE/RETIRED) per authoritative event

**Frozen principle:**

028 owns editorial retirement. Question Content Service owns content
retirement. 029 updates eligibility projection after receiving
authoritative event. **Quality flags never automatically change
operational_status.**

**14. Operational Status Transition Rules**

**Frozen principle:**

**Quality flags (low_performance_flag, high_exposure_flag,
review_required_flag) never automatically change operational_status
(ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE/RETIRED). 029 recommends action via item-quality
recommendations; 028/QCS determine authoritative lifecycle change.**

**14.1 ELIGIBLE → INELIGIBLE**

Triggered by authoritative event (e.g. 028 editorial workflow, Question
Content Service)

Reasons: under investigation, insufficient calibration data, temporary
clinical review

Reversible (INELIGIBLE → ELIGIBLE per authoritative event)

**14.2 ELIGIBLE → RETIRED**

Triggered by authoritative event (e.g. 028 editorial workflow, Question
Content Service)

Reasons: permanently withdrawn version, superseded by new version

Irreversible (RETIRED is permanent)

If supersedes_question_content_version_id is present, update
superseded_by_question_content_version_id = new version

**14.3 INELIGIBLE → ELIGIBLE**

Triggered by authoritative event (e.g. 028 editorial workflow, Question
Content Service)

Reasons: investigation complete, calibration data sufficient, clinical
review complete

Reversible

**14.4 Version Supersession**

Q123 v1 → ELIGIBLE

↓ revision

Q123 v2 → RELEASE_CONFIRMED (supersedes_question_content_version_id =
v1)

↓

Q123 v1 → RETIRED (superseded_by_question_content_version_id = v2)

Q123 v2 → ELIGIBLE

**Frozen principle:**

**Version supersession is explicit
(supersedes_question_content_version_id,
superseded_by_question_content_version_id). 029 updates previous version
status deterministically per authoritative event.**

**26. Security**

Required:

Authenticated access

Role-based permissions

Question bank metadata encrypted at rest

API validation

Rate limiting

Audit logs

Tenant/service authorization boundaries

Least-privilege service identities

Immutable audit events for selection decisions

Protection against question-bank enumeration

Prevention of unauthorised bulk extraction

Separation between candidate-facing and editorial/admin APIs

**27. Privacy**

Question bank metadata is not necessarily personal data. The sensitive
area is where 029 receives candidate-associated exposure/outcome data.

Requirements:

Authenticated access

Role-based access controls

Encrypted transport

Controlled storage

Defined retention

Deletion/retention policy

Minimise candidate-identifiable data (QUESTION_PRESENTED events use
session_reference_id, not candidate_id)

Distinguish question-bank metadata from candidate-linked usage data

**candidate_exclusion_context.candidate_exposure_history provided by
requester system (015/016/020/008--010), 029 does not store candidate
exposure history**

**005 → 029 analytics events contain cohort identifiers, not direct
candidate identifiers**

**28. Accessibility**

029 must support:

Keyboard operation

Screen readers

Clear instructions

Accessible controls

Non-colour-only indicators

**29. Internationalisation**

029 supports:

Locale as a selection dimension

Version references

Locale availability indexes

**Frozen principle:**

029 indexes and selects locale-specific content versions; it does not
own translation or locale content. Question Content Service owns
translated content versions.

**30. Performance Targets**

Initial targets:

**Runtime selection**: p95 \<1 second

**Ingestion (RELEASE_CONFIRMED, QUESTION_PRESENTED, 005 outcome
events)**: p95 \<500 ms acknowledgement

**Analytics calculation**: Asynchronous/event-driven with freshness SLA
(e.g. \"Standard item analytics updated within X minutes of sufficient
new outcome data\")

No blocking 005 outcome dependencies (candidate can receive questions
even if analytics are temporarily delayed)

**31. Acceptance Criteria --- Core**

029 is acceptable only if:

Question bank inventory and eligibility metadata are owned by 029.

Question selection rules are owned by 029.

Question selections (item sets) are owned by 029.

Question selection items (first-class relational model) are owned by
029.

Question performance analytics (item-level) are owned by 029.

Item-quality recommendations (editorial action) are owned by 029.

Question exposure events (QUESTION_PRESENTED) are owned by 029.

Selection audit trail is owned by 029.

029 does not own question content (Question Content Service owns this).

029 does not own question attempts/outcomes (005 owns this).

029 does not own AKT practice sessions (015 owns this).

029 does not own weakness-loop sessions (016 owns this).

029 does not own mock examinations (020 owns this).

029 does not own editorial governance (028 owns this).

029 does not own mastery (007 owns this).

029 does not own candidate recommendations (012 owns this).

029 does not own curriculum coverage (014 owns this).

029 does not own longitudinal candidate analytics (021 owns this).

029 does not own daily plans (024 owns this).

029 does not own journey state (027 owns this).

Question bank references Question Content Service via external UUIDs (no
cross-service FKs).

Item-quality recommendations refer to 028 editorial workflow (external
UUIDs).

Question performance analytics aggregate 005 outcome events via
authoritative analytics contract with explicit payload (005 owns
individual attempts).

Question selection algorithms are configurable and versioned.

Observed p-value uses 005 outcome events.

Discrimination uses explicitly defined methodology: corrected
point-biserial, reference-performance contract = total score excluding
index item, reference_population = eligible first-attempt responses
within analytics window excluding invalid/voided/missing total-score.

Exposure tracking uses QUESTION_PRESENTED events (actual presentation,
not selection).

Option analysis flags statistical anomalies (028/QCS determine
clinical/content ambiguity).

Item-quality recommendations use terminology \"item-quality
recommendation\" or \"editorial action recommendation\" (not candidate
recommendations).

Bank inventory gaps are identified (item availability, not curriculum
coverage).

Item-level psychometric analytics are owned (not longitudinal candidate
analytics).

Question bank ingestion from 028 is event-driven (RELEASE_CONFIRMED
events, idempotent, with supersedes_question_content_version_id for
version transition).

Question bank analytics are auditable (analytics_method_version,
calculated_at, sample_size, population_definition).

Question bank is searchable by canonical_content_map_ids,
selection_tags, question_type, locale.

Operational eligibility (ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE/RETIRED) is separate from
quality/exposure flags (low_performance_flag, high_exposure_flag,
review_required_flag).

Minimum sample size safeguards are enforced (INSUFFICIENT_DATA for small
samples).

Psychometric thresholds are configurable (not immutable rules).

Analytics are asynchronous with freshness SLA (not synchronous request
latency).

Selection contracts are explicit (request/response, algorithm_version,
rule_set_version, selection_seed, candidate_exclusion_context).

Selection audit trail is immutable (reproducibility).

created_by_id is external UUID reference to 000 identity authority (no
cross-service FKs).

Locale/version handling is clear (029 indexes locale-specific versions,
does not own translation).

029 calculates item-level psychometric analytics (p-value,
discrimination, option analysis, exposure, time-to-answer aggregates).

029 does not calculate candidate mastery, candidate recommendations,
curriculum coverage, longitudinal candidate analytics, mock scoring.

QUESTION_PRESENTED event contract is explicit (event_id,
question_content_id, question_content_version_id, session_reference_id,
consumer_system, occurred_at).

Exposure means actual presentation (QUESTION_PRESENTED event), not
merely selection.

Item eligibility model is explicit (ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE/RETIRED, with
explicit transition rules).

Exclusion rules are explicit (exclude previously seen, recently seen,
same content family, retired version, locale unavailable, flagged item,
already in current set).

Selection auditability includes algorithm/rule versioning
(reproducibility).

Analytics versioning is explicit (analytics_method_version,
calculated_at, sample_size, population_definition).

Version supersession is explicit
(supersedes_question_content_version_id,
superseded_by_question_content_version_id).

Quality flags never automatically change operational_status.

candidate_exclusion_context.candidate_exposure_history is provided by
requester system (015/016/020/008--010), 029 does not own candidate
exposure history.

Consuming systems must persist selection_id when instantiating/using the
selected set.

calibrated_difficulty is reserved for future version (nullable in Phase
1, not populated by Phase 1 analytics pipeline).

**005 → 029 analytics event contract has explicit payload (event_id,
question_content_id, question_content_version_id, attempt_id,
candidate_cohort_identifier, attempt_number, is_first_attempt,
correctness, selected_option_id, time_to_answer_seconds,
total_score_excluding_index_item, assessment_session_reference_id,
assessment_mode, is_valid_attempt, is_voided,
has_required_total_score_reference, reference_population_eligible,
analytics_window, occurred_at, analytics_contract_version).**

**reference_population is deterministically defined (eligible
first-attempt responses to same question_content_version_id within
analytics window, excluding invalid/voided/missing total-score).**

**analytics_status explicitly represents SUFFICIENT_DATA,
INSUFFICIENT_DATA, NOT_AVAILABLE for each calculated metric.**

**33. Implementation Phases**

Recommended engineering sequence:

**Phase 1A --- Bank Foundation**

Build:

Question bank inventory and indexing

Question ingestion from 028 (RELEASE_CONFIRMED events, idempotent, with
supersedes_question_content_version_id)

Operational eligibility (ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE/RETIRED, explicit
transition rules)

Question version references (external UUIDs,
superseded_by_question_content_version_id)

Basic selection algorithms (explicit contracts, versioned,
candidate_exclusion_context)

QUESTION_PRESENTED exposure events (ingestion)

Selection audit trail (immutable)

APIs (selection request/response contracts, candidate_exclusion_context)

Security (tenant/service authorization, least-privilege, bulk extraction
protection)

**Phase 1B --- Item Analytics**

Add:

Observed p-value calculation (from 005 outcome events, asynchronous)

Basic item statistics (attempt_count, correct_count, time-to-answer
aggregates)

Discrimination calculation (corrected point-biserial,
reference-performance contract = total score excluding index item,
asynchronous)

Analytics pipeline (asynchronous, freshness SLA)

Minimum sample size safeguards (INSUFFICIENT_DATA)

Analytics versioning (analytics_method_version, calculated_at,
sample_size, population_definition)

**analytics_status explicit representation (SUFFICIENT_DATA,
INSUFFICIENT_DATA, NOT_AVAILABLE)**

**005 → 029 analytics event contract implementation (explicit payload)**

**reference_population deterministic filtering**

**calibrated_difficulty reserved (nullable, not populated)**

**Phase 2 --- Advanced Item Intelligence**

Add:

Option analysis (statistical anomaly flagging)

Similarity strategy (content-map, question-type, difficulty band, topic
overlap)

Bank inventory gap analysis (item availability, not curriculum coverage)

Item-quality recommendations (editorial action, to 028)

Editorial integration (028 editorial workflow, external UUID references)

Exclusion rules (previously seen, recently seen, same content family,
etc.)

Advanced selection algorithms (configurable, versioned)

calibrated_difficulty methodology (future version, e.g.
Rasch/1PL/2PL/IRT)

This staged approach reduces implementation risk.

**34. Architectural Anti-Patterns**

Do not implement:

❌ 029 as a question content authority (Question Content Service owns
this)

❌ 029 as a question outcomes authority (005 owns this)

❌ 029 as an AKT practice authority (015 owns this)

❌ 029 as a weakness-loop authority (016 owns this)

❌ 029 as a mock composition authority (020 owns this)

❌ 029 as an editorial authority (028 owns this)

❌ 029 as a mastery authority (007 owns this)

❌ 029 as a candidate recommendation authority (012 owns this)

❌ 029 as a curriculum coverage authority (014 owns this)

❌ 029 as a longitudinal candidate analytics authority (021 owns this)

❌ 029 without question bank inventory and eligibility metadata

❌ 029 without question selection algorithms (explicit contracts,
versioned)

❌ 029 without question selection items (first-class relational model,
not JSON array)

❌ 029 without question performance analytics (item-level, asynchronous,
freshness SLA)

❌ 029 without observed p-value calculation (from 005 outcome events)

❌ 029 without discrimination calculation (corrected point-biserial,
reference-performance contract = total score excluding index item)

❌ 029 without exposure tracking (QUESTION_PRESENTED events, actual
presentation)

❌ 029 without item-quality recommendations (editorial action, to 028)

❌ 029 with cross-service database FKs (external UUIDs only)

❌ 029 directly retiring questions (028 executes retirement via
editorial workflow)

❌ 029 querying 005 database directly (authoritative analytics contract
only)

❌ 029 inventing candidate ability (discrimination requires
reference-performance contract)

❌ 029 declaring clinical/content ambiguity (028/QCS authority)

❌ 029 creating competing canonical mapping definitions (003 owns
canonical mapping)

❌ 029 owning translation or locale content (Question Content Service
owns this)

❌ 029 calculating candidate mastery, candidate recommendations,
curriculum coverage, longitudinal candidate analytics, mock scoring

❌ 029 with synchronous analytics calculation (asynchronous, freshness
SLA)

**36. Frozen Non-Negotiables**

If 029 is approved, the following become immutable architectural
principles:

**029 owns the question bank inventory, eligibility, selection and
item-level analytics layer.**

**029 does not become the canonical owner of question content.**

**Question Content Service retains ownership of question content
definitions, schemas, versions and runtime meaning.**

**005 remains the sole authority for question attempts and
question-level outcomes (including analytics event contract payload).**

**015 remains the AKT practice authority.**

**016 remains the weakness-loop authority.**

**020 remains the mock examination authority.**

**028 remains the editorial authority.**

**021 remains the longitudinal candidate analytics authority.**

**014 remains the curriculum coverage authority.**

**029 provides question bank inventory, eligibility, selection, item set

infrastructure.**

**Question changes create new question versions.**

**Historical candidate records retain the exact
question_content_version_id used.**

**Observed p-value is calculated from 005 outcome events (asynchronous,
freshness SLA).**

**Discrimination is calculated using corrected point-biserial
methodology, reference-performance contract = total score excluding
index item, reference_population = eligible first-attempt responses
within analytics window excluding invalid/voided/missing total-score
(asynchronous, freshness SLA).**

**Exposure is tracked from QUESTION_PRESENTED events (actual
presentation, not selection).**

**028 executes question retirement/revision through editorial

**Question bank references question content via external UUIDs (no

authoritative analytics contract with explicit payload (005 owns
individual attempts).**

**Question selection algorithms are configurable and versioned (explicit
contracts).**

**Question sets use first-class relational model
(question_selection_items, not JSON array).**

**Selection audit trail is immutable (algorithm/rule versioning,
reproducibility).**

**Analytics versioning is explicit (analytics_method_version,
calculated_at, sample_size, population_definition).**

**QUESTION_PRESENTED event contract is explicit (exposure means actual
presentation).**

**Operational eligibility (ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE/RETIRED) is separate from
quality/exposure flags (explicit transition rules).**

**Minimum sample size safeguards are enforced (INSUFFICIENT_DATA for
small samples).**

**Psychometric thresholds are configurable (not immutable rules).**

**Analytics are asynchronous with freshness SLA (not synchronous request
latency).**

**Locale/version handling is clear (029 indexes locale-specific
versions, does not own translation).**

**029 calculates item-level psychometric analytics (p-value,
discrimination, option analysis, exposure, time-to-answer aggregates).**

**029 does not calculate candidate mastery, candidate recommendations,
curriculum coverage, longitudinal candidate analytics, mock scoring.**

**029 identifies bank inventory gaps (item availability, not curriculum
coverage).**

**029 generates item sets; consuming systems own runtime assessment
composition.**

**029 does not independently determine clinical correctness at
runtime.**

**029 does not become a second CMS for question content.**

**created_by_id is external UUID reference to 000 identity authority (no
cross-service FKs).**

**canonical_content_map_ids, question_type, locale, author_difficulty
are denormalised/indexed projections from authoritative content
(Question Content Service).**

**selection_tags are 029-owned operational/indexing metadata (not
canonical taxonomy).**

**Discrimination uses explicitly defined methodology: corrected
point-biserial, reference-performance contract = total score excluding
index item, reference_population = eligible first-attempt responses
within analytics window excluding invalid/voided/missing total-score.**

**Option analysis flags statistical anomalies (028/QCS determine
clinical/content ambiguity).**

**Exclusion rules are explicit (previously seen, recently seen, same
content family, retired version, locale unavailable, flagged item,
already in current set).**

**Similarity strategy is defined (content-map, question-type, difficulty
band, topic overlap, exclude same item/version, exposure constraints).**

**Ingestion is idempotent (RELEASE_CONFIRMED, QUESTION_PRESENTED, 005
outcome events).**

**029 does not query 005 database directly (authoritative analytics
contract only).**

**029 does not create competing canonical mapping definitions (003 owns
canonical mapping).**

**029 does not own translation or locale content (Question Content
Service owns this).**

**029 protects against bulk extraction and question-bank enumeration.**

**029 minimises candidate-identifiable data (QUESTION_PRESENTED events
use session_reference_id, not candidate_id).**

**Version supersession is explicit
(supersedes_question_content_version_id,
superseded_by_question_content_version_id).**

**Quality flags never automatically change operational_status.**

**candidate_exclusion_context.candidate_exposure_history is provided by
requester system (015/016/020/008--010), 029 does not own candidate
exposure history.**

**Consuming systems must persist selection_id when instantiating/using
the selected set.**

**calibrated_difficulty is reserved for future version (nullable in
Phase 1, not populated by Phase 1 analytics pipeline).**

**005 → 029 analytics event contract has explicit payload (event_id,
question_content_id, question_content_version_id, attempt_id,
candidate_cohort_identifier, attempt_number, is_first_attempt,
correctness, selected_option_id, time_to_answer_seconds,
total_score_excluding_index_item, assessment_session_reference_id,
assessment_mode, is_valid_attempt, is_voided,
has_required_total_score_reference, reference_population_eligible,
analytics_window, occurred_at, analytics_contract_version).**

**reference_population is deterministically defined (eligible
first-attempt responses to same question_content_version_id within
analytics window, excluding invalid/voided/missing total-score).**

**analytics_status explicitly represents SUFFICIENT_DATA,
INSUFFICIENT_DATA, NOT_AVAILABLE for each calculated metric.**

I have re-checked the **entire UKMLA-029 specification**, not just the
five amendments. The major architectural problems are now resolved, and
**000--028 do not need reopening**.

However, I would **not yet freeze 029 exactly as written**. There are a
few remaining engineering-contract ambiguities that are worth fixing
now, because after freezing they become expensive to correct.

**UKMLA-029 --- FINAL REVIEW**

**Overall decision: AMEND BEFORE FREEZE**

The architecture is fundamentally correct. I found **5 remaining
amendments**.

**1. AMEND --- Define the authoritative source/event for eligibility
changes**

You now correctly say:

029 owns bank eligibility projection; QCS/editorial lifecycle owns
canonical content lifecycle.

But there is still a small contradiction in the event flow.

You say:

028 executes retirement through editorial workflow

then:

Question Content Service updates question content state

then:

029 receives authoritative RELEASE_CONFIRMED/retirement event.

The specification needs to say **who is authoritative for the event that
changes the bank projection**.

The cleanest architecture is:

028

Editorial decision / approval

↓

Question Content Service

Authoritative content lifecycle transition

↓

Authoritative lifecycle event

↓

029

Bank eligibility projection

Therefore explicitly define:

**QCS is the authoritative publisher of canonical content lifecycle
events consumed by 029. 028 may initiate/approve the editorial action,
but 029 must consume the authoritative lifecycle event rather than
treating a 028 workflow event as the canonical lifecycle state.**

This prevents 028 and QCS from becoming competing authorities.

**Decision: AMEND.**

**2. AMEND --- Define selection shortfall behaviour**

This is the most important remaining selection-contract omission.

Your request can say:

requested_count = 20

But there may only be 14 eligible questions satisfying all constraints.

The response currently gives:

selection_id

selected_question_content_version_ids

selection_metadata

It doesn\'t explicitly say what happens when:

requested_count ≠ selected_count.

You need a deterministic contract.

I recommend:

{

\"selection_id\": \"uuid\",

\"requested_count\": 20,

\"selected_count\": 14,

\"selection_status\": \"PARTIAL\",

\"shortfall_reason\": \"INSUFFICIENT_ELIGIBLE_ITEMS\",

\"selected_question_content_version_ids\": \[\...\]

}

with:

COMPLETE

PARTIAL

NO_ELIGIBLE_ITEMS

For example:

COMPLETE = requested count satisfied

PARTIAL = some eligible items found but requested count cannot be
satisfied

NO_ELIGIBLE_ITEMS = zero items satisfy constraints

Critically, **029 should not silently relax constraints** unless the
request explicitly permits fallback behaviour.

Otherwise 015/016/020 cannot reliably know whether they received the
requested assessment set.

**Decision: AMEND.**

**3. AMEND --- Make the exclusion-rule contract match the actual request
contract**

Acceptance criterion 48 says:

exclusion rules are explicit (exclude previously seen, recently seen,
same content family, retired version, locale unavailable, flagged item,
already in current set).

But the actual request contract explicitly provides:

previously seen

recently seen

candidate exposure history

It does **not explicitly define**:

same content family

already in current set

flagged-item exclusion semantics

Some of these are naturally internal 029 rules, which is fine, but the
architecture should distinguish:

**Requester-provided candidate exclusions**

candidate_exposure_history

exclude_previously_seen

exclude_recently_seen_days

**029-owned selection exclusions**

retired/ineligible

locale unavailable

already selected in current set

configured quality exclusions

same-content-family exclusion, where configured

That makes the ownership boundary much cleaner.

Also define what \"same content family\" actually means --- preferably
via the canonical content mapping/content-family identifier rather than
an undefined concept.

**Decision: AMEND.**

**4. AMEND --- Define CUSTOM analysis-window representation**

You correctly removed analytics_window from the 005 event.

Good.

But question_performance_analytics contains:

analysis_window =

ALL_TIME

LAST_30_DAYS

LAST_90_DAYS

LAST_365_DAYS

CUSTOM

If CUSTOM is permitted, engineering needs to know the actual interval.

Otherwise two implementations could have:

CUSTOM

but different date ranges.

Add something like:

analysis_window_type

analysis_window_start

analysis_window_end

or a single immutable window specification.

For example:

analysis_window_type = CUSTOM

analysis_window_start = 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z

analysis_window_end = 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z

The window must be reproducible from the stored analytics record.

**Decision: AMEND.**

**5. AMEND --- Define candidate_cohort_identifier precisely**

The privacy architecture is good, but this field needs one final
definition.

You currently have:

candidate_cohort_identifier

and say it is not a direct candidate identifier.

That is directionally correct, but engineering needs to know what it
actually represents.

Define it as something like:

A non-person-identifying identifier representing the analytics
cohort/population to which the outcome belongs. It must not be a
candidate identity key, account identifier, session identifier, or
reversible surrogate for candidate identity.

And ideally state:

029 must not use candidate_cohort_identifier to reconstruct individual
candidate histories.

This matters because otherwise someone could eventually turn the field
into a pseudonymous candidate ID and undermine the stated privacy
boundary.

**Decision: AMEND.**

**Everything else: CORRECT**

RETIRED

**UKMLA-029 --- Question Bank / Item Banking**

**Version:** v1.0 FINAL --- FROZEN / ENGINEERING READY\
**Date:** Thursday, October 08, 2026\
**Phase:** D\
**Priority:** VERY HIGH\
**Status:** APPROVED

**Executive Decision**

UKMLA-029 is the next major AMaC capability.

Its purpose is to provide the **authoritative service for question-bank
inventory, eligibility metadata, selection, set-generation, exposure
tracking and item-level psychometric analytics**.

The core product question is:

**\"How does AMaC manage, select and analyse its question bank for
optimal learning and assessment?\"**

**Critical architectural principles:**

**029 owns question bank inventory, eligibility projection, selection
and item-level analytics.**

**029 does not own question content (Question Content Service owns
this).**

**029 does not own question attempts/outcomes (005 owns this).**

**029 does not own runtime assessment sessions (015, 016, 020, 008--010
own these).**

**029 does not own editorial governance (028 owns this).**

**029 does not own candidate mastery (007 owns this).**

**029 does not own recommendations (012 owns this).**

**029 does not own curriculum coverage (014 owns this).**

**029 does not own longitudinal candidate analytics (021 owns this).**

**029 generates item sets; consuming systems own runtime assessment
composition.**

This is fundamentally different from existing systems:

**Question Content Service**: owns question content definitions and
schemas

**005**: owns canonical question attempts and question-level outcomes

**015**: owns AKT learning/exam modes (consumes question bank)

**016**: owns immediate weakness-loop practice (consumes question bank)

**020**: owns mock examination lifecycle and scoring (composes from
question bank)

**028**: owns editorial workflow and governance (publishes questions)

**029 is the question bank manager, not the question content owner or
runtime assessment engine.**

**1. Core Product Question**

**Question Content Service asks:**

\"What is the canonical question content?\"

**005 asks:**

\"What were the question attempts and outcomes?\"

**015 asks:**

\"How does the candidate practise or take AKT exams?\"

**016 asks:**

\"What similar questions should the candidate practise after an
incorrect answer?\"

**020 asks:**

\"How did the candidate perform on the mock examination?\"

**028 asks:**

\"How is the question produced and governed?\"

**029 asks:**

**\"How is the question bank managed, selected, analysed and made
eligible for use?\"**

This is a **question bank management** capability, not a content
authoring, runtime assessment or editorial system.

**2. Strategic Objective**

029 should transform AMaC from a system that has questions into a system
that **intelligently manages, selects and analyses questions for optimal
learning and assessment**.

The intended workflow:

028 publishes questions (RELEASE_CONFIRMED event)

↓

029 ingests published questions into question bank (event-driven,
idempotent)

↓

029 manages question bank:

\- inventory indexing

\- eligibility metadata (ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE/RETIRED)

\- version supersession (supersedes_question_content_version_id)

\- content-map references (003)

\- selection tags

\- difficulty indexing

\- exposure tracking

↓

029 receives QUESTION_PRESENTED events from runtime systems (015, 016,
020, 008--010)

↓

029 aggregates exposure metrics

↓

029 receives 005 outcome events (authoritative analytics contract with
explicit payload)

↓

029 calculates item-level analytics:

\- p-value (item facility)

\- discrimination (corrected point-biserial, reference-performance
contract defined)

\- option analysis

\- time-to-answer aggregates

↓

029 flags underperforming questions (item-quality recommendations to
028)

↓

028 executes retirement through editorial workflow

↓

Question Content Service publishes authoritative lifecycle event

↓

029 updates eligibility projection (ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE/RETIRED) per
authoritative event

The key differentiator is therefore not simply:

\"AMaC has questions.\"

It is:

**\"AMaC intelligently manages question inventory, eligibility
projection, selection and item-level psychometric analytics.\"**

**3. Critical Ownership Principle**

**029 owns question bank inventory, eligibility projection, selection
and item-level analytics.**

It does **not** own question content, runtime assessment, editorial
governance, mastery calculation, recommendations, curriculum coverage,
longitudinal candidate analytics, or candidate exposure history.

The frozen ownership model is:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **System**     **Authority**
  -------------- --------------------------------------------------------
  000            Authentication / identity

  003            GMC/MLA canonical content mapping

  **Question     **Question content definitions and schemas, canonical
  Content        content lifecycle, authoritative lifecycle events**
  Service**      

  **005**        **Canonical question attempts and question-level
                 outcomes (including 005 → 029 analytics event
                 contract)**

  007            Knowledge mastery

  008--010       Diagnostic lifecycle

  011            Dashboard presentation

  012            Recommendations

  013            Manual override for recommendations

  **014**        **Content-map coverage (curriculum coverage)**

  015            AKT learning/exam modes (consumes question bank,
                 provides candidate exclusion context)

  016            Immediate weakness-loop practice (consumes question
                 bank, provides candidate exclusion context)

  017            Homepage / conversion

  018            Commercial entitlement

  019            Knowledge review scheduling

  **020**        **Mock examination lifecycle and scoring (composes from
                 question bank, provides candidate exclusion context)**

  **021**        **Longitudinal analytics (candidate performance)**

  022            Communication

  023            CPSA/clinical-performance assessment

  024            Daily study plan / command centre

  025            Standalone clinical learning content

  026            Interactive clinical reasoning tutor

  027            Unified UKMLA/PLAB readiness journey

  **028**        **Content authoring, editorial workflow & quality
                 assurance (publishes questions, initiates editorial
                 actions)**

  **029**        **Question bank / item banking (inventory, eligibility
                 projection, selection, item analytics)**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**4. Non-Negotiable Boundary**

**029 is the question bank management layer. It may manage inventory,
eligibility projection, selection and item-level analytics, but it may
not own the question content (Question Content Service), runtime
assessment (015, 016, 020, 008--010), question outcomes (005), editorial
governance (028), mastery calculation (007), recommendations (012),
curriculum coverage (014), longitudinal candidate analytics (021), or
candidate exposure history.**

**Critical boundary clarification:**

**029 owns the question bank\'s eligibility projection and selection
eligibility state; it does not own the authoritative canonical content
lifecycle. Question Content Service is the authoritative publisher of
canonical content lifecycle events consumed by 029. 028 may
initiate/approve editorial actions, but 029 consumes authoritative
lifecycle events from QCS.**

029 produces:

Question bank inventory and indexing

Eligibility metadata (ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE/RETIRED) --- **bank
eligibility projection**

Selection algorithms and rules

Item set generation (selected question_content_version_ids)

Exposure tracking (from QUESTION_PRESENTED events)

Item-level psychometric analytics (p-value, discrimination, option
analysis)

Item-quality recommendations (to 028 editorial workflow)

Bank inventory gap analysis (item availability, not curriculum coverage)

029 does **not** produce:

Question content definitions (Question Content Service owns these)

Question content versions (Question Content Service owns these)

Canonical content lifecycle decisions (Question Content Service owns
these)

Authoritative lifecycle events (Question Content Service publishes
these)

Question attempts or outcomes (005 owns this)

AKT practice sessions (015 owns this)

Weakness-loop sessions (016 owns this)

Mock examinations (020 owns this)

Editorial governance (028 owns this)

Mastery state (007 owns this)

Recommendations (012 owns this)

Curriculum coverage (014 owns this)

Longitudinal candidate analytics (021 owns this)

Mock scoring (020 owns this)

Candidate exposure history (runtime systems own this, provide exclusion
context)

**5. 029 Is Not a Question Content Authority**

This is a central design rule.

**029 decides:**

\"This question is ELIGIBLE for cardiology practice.\"

**Question Content Service decides:**

\"This is the question content.\"

**029 decides:**

\"This question has p-value 0.65 and discrimination 0.28.\"

**005 decides:**

\"This is how candidates performed on this question.\"

**029 decides:**

\"This question should be flagged for editorial review due to low
discrimination.\"

**028 decides:**

\"This question should enter editorial workflow.\"

**Question Content Service decides:**

\"This question content lifecycle state is now RETIRED.\"

029 must not independently calculate:

Question content (Question Content Service owns this)

Question attempts or outcomes (005 owns this)

AKT practice sessions (015 owns this)

Weakness-loop sessions (016 owns this)

Mock examinations (020 owns this)

Editorial governance (028 owns this)

Mastery state (007 owns this)

Recommendations (012 owns this)

Curriculum coverage (014 owns this)

Longitudinal candidate analytics (021 owns this)

Candidate exposure history (runtime systems own this)

Canonical content lifecycle (Question Content Service owns this)

Authoritative lifecycle events (Question Content Service publishes
these)

**6. Question Bank Architecture**

029 manages questions through a unified question bank:

**6.1 Question Ingestion (from 028 via Question Content Service)**

028 RELEASE_CONFIRMED event (question published)

↓

Event contains:

\- question_content_id

\- question_content_version_id

\- supersedes_question_content_version_id (nullable, for version
transition)

\- release_revision

\- occurred_at

\- source

\- content_map_version/reference (where authoritative)

\- question_type (denormalised from QCS)

\- locale (denormalised from QCS)

↓

029 ingests event (idempotent)

↓

If supersedes_question_content_version_id is present:

\- Update previous version: operational_status = RETIRED

\- Set superseded_by_question_content_version_id = new version

↓

029 indexes question bank item:

\- question_content_id (external UUID reference)

\- question_content_version_id (external UUID reference)

\- canonical_content_map_ids (references to 003)

\- selection_tags (029-owned operational metadata)

\- author_difficulty (denormalised from QCS)

\- question_type (denormalised from QCS)

\- locale (denormalised from QCS)

\- operational_status = ELIGIBLE (default for newly published)

\- superseded_by_question_content_version_id (nullable, external UUID
reference)

↓

029 makes question available for selection

**Frozen principle:**

028 publishes questions via RELEASE_CONFIRMED events with explicit
version-transition contract (supersedes_question_content_version_id).
029 ingests events idempotently and updates previous version status
deterministically. Question Content Service owns question content and
canonical content lifecycle.

**6.2 Authoritative Lifecycle Event Flow**

028 editorial workflow

↓

Editorial decision / approval (e.g. retire question)

↓

Question Content Service

↓

Authoritative content lifecycle transition (e.g. RETIRED)

↓

Authoritative lifecycle event published by QCS

↓

029 consumes authoritative lifecycle event

↓

029 updates bank eligibility projection (operational_status)

**Frozen principle:**

**Question Content Service is the authoritative publisher of canonical
content lifecycle events consumed by 029. 028 may initiate/approve
editorial actions, but 029 must consume the authoritative lifecycle
event from QCS rather than treating a 028 workflow event as the
canonical lifecycle state.**

**6.3 Question Selection**

029 selects questions based on:

Content coverage (canonical_content_map_ids, references to 003)

Author difficulty and observed p-value

Selection tags (029-owned operational metadata)

Question type (denormalised from QCS)

Exposure tracking (from QUESTION_PRESENTED events)

Performance metrics (p-value, discrimination --- with minimum sample
safeguards)

Learning objectives (via content-map references)

**Candidate exclusion context (provided by requester system, e.g.
015/016/020/008--010)**

**029-owned selection exclusions (retired/ineligible, locale
unavailable, already selected in current set, configured quality
exclusions, same-content-family exclusion where configured)**

**Frozen principle:**

029 selects questions. Runtime systems (015, 016, 020, 008--010) consume
selected questions and own runtime sessions. **029 does not own
candidate exposure history; candidate exclusion constraints are provided
by requester systems. 029 owns selection exclusion rules.**

**6.4 Item Set Generation with Selection Shortfall Handling**

029 generates item sets for:

AKT practice sessions (015 requests, provides candidate exclusion
context)

Weakness loops (016 requests, provides candidate exclusion context)

Mock examinations (020 requests, provides candidate exclusion context)

Diagnostic assessments (008--010 requests, provides candidate exclusion
context)

**Frozen principle:**

029 generates item sets (selected question_content_version_ids).
Consuming systems retain ownership of the runtime assessment/session
that uses those selections. **Consuming systems must persist the
returned selection_id when instantiating/using the selected set.
Selection shortfall behaviour is explicit (COMPLETE, PARTIAL,
NO_ELIGIBLE_ITEMS).**

**6.5 Question Performance Analytics**

029 analyses question performance from 005 outcome events (authoritative
analytics contract with explicit payload):

**p-value** (item facility: proportion correct, with minimum sample
safeguards)

**Discrimination** (corrected point-biserial correlation with total
score excluding index item, with minimum sample safeguards,
reference-performance contract explicitly defined)

**Option analysis** (distractor effectiveness, flags statistical
anomalies)

**Exposure rate** (from QUESTION_PRESENTED events)

**Time to answer** (aggregates from 005 outcome events)

**Content coverage gaps** (bank inventory gaps, not curriculum coverage)

**Frozen principle:**

005 owns individual question outcomes. 029 aggregates item-level
analytics via authoritative analytics contract with explicit payload.
029 does not query 005 database directly. **calibrated_difficulty is
reserved for future version (nullable in Phase 1).**

**6.6 Item-Quality Recommendations (to 028)**

029 flags underperforming questions via item-quality recommendations
(not candidate recommendations):

Low discrimination (\< configurable threshold, with minimum sample
check)

Too easy (p-value \> configurable threshold) or too hard (p-value \<
configurable threshold)

High exposure (from QUESTION_PRESENTED events)

Content outdated (from 028 editorial review)

Technical issues (ambiguous options flagged via option analysis)

**Frozen principle:**

029 generates item-quality recommendations (editorial action
recommendations). 028 executes retirement/revision through editorial
workflow. **Quality flags never automatically change operational_status;
029 recommends action, 028/QCS determine authoritative lifecycle change.
QCS publishes authoritative lifecycle events.**

**7. Data Model**

**7.1 Question Bank Items**

question_bank_items

**Frozen principle:**

question_bank_items is 029\'s index of published questions. It
references Question Content Service via external UUIDs; it does not own
question content. **No cross-service database FKs.**

Fields:

id (PK, UUID)

question_content_id (UUID --- reference to Question Content Service,
**external reference, not database FK**)

question_content_version_id (UUID --- reference to Question Content
Service, **external reference, not database FK**)

operational_status (enum: ELIGIBLE, INELIGIBLE, RETIRED) --- **lifecycle
eligibility (bank eligibility projection)**

**ELIGIBLE**: currently selectable

**INELIGIBLE**: temporarily not selectable due to authoritative
eligibility decision (e.g. under investigation, temporary clinical
review, technical issue, locale/content availability issue, or other
explicitly configured bank eligibility rule)

**RETIRED**: permanently withdrawn version

superseded_by_question_content_version_id (UUID --- reference to
superseding version, **external reference, not database FK**, nullable)

supersedes_question_content_version_id (UUID --- reference to superseded
version, **external reference, not database FK**, nullable)

low_performance_flag (boolean --- quality flag, separate from lifecycle)

high_exposure_flag (boolean --- quality flag, separate from lifecycle)

review_required_flag (boolean --- quality flag, separate from lifecycle)

canonical_content_map_ids (JSON --- array of 003 canonical identifier
references)

selection_tags (JSON --- array of 029-owned operational/indexing tags)

author_difficulty (decimal --- author-defined difficulty denormalised
from QCS)

observed_p_value (decimal --- item facility from 005 outcomes, nullable)

observed_p_value_analytics_status (enum: SUFFICIENT_DATA,
INSUFFICIENT_DATA, NOT_AVAILABLE)

calibrated_difficulty (decimal --- **reserved for future version,
nullable in Phase 1, not populated by Phase 1 analytics pipeline**)

discrimination (decimal --- corrected point-biserial from 005 outcomes,
nullable)

discrimination_analytics_status (enum: SUFFICIENT_DATA,
INSUFFICIENT_DATA, NOT_AVAILABLE)

discrimination_method (string --- \"corrected_point_biserial\")

reference_performance_contract (string ---
\"total_score_excluding_index_item\")

reference_population (string ---
\"eligible_first_attempt_responses_same_question_version_analytics_window_excluding_invalid_voided_missing_total_score\")

reference_population_definition_version (string ---
analytics_method_version reference)

exposure_count (integer --- from QUESTION_PRESENTED events)

exposure_last_presented_at (timestamp, nullable --- from
QUESTION_PRESENTED events)

question_type (string --- denormalised from QCS, e.g.
\"single_best_answer\")

locale (string --- denormalised from QCS, e.g. \"en-GB\")

minimum_sample_size (integer --- configurable threshold for psychometric
calculations)

analytics_method_version (string --- version of analytics calculation
methodology)

created_at (timestamp)

updated_at (timestamp)

**Constraint:**

INDEX(canonical_content_map_ids)

INDEX(selection_tags)

INDEX(operational_status)

INDEX(question_content_version_id)

**Frozen principle:**

029 owns question bank inventory and eligibility metadata (bank
eligibility projection). Question Content Service owns question content
and canonical content lifecycle. question_content_id and
question_content_version_id are external UUID references. **Version
supersession is explicit (supersedes_question_content_version_id,
superseded_by_question_content_version_id). Quality flags never
automatically change operational_status. analytics_status explicitly
represents SUFFICIENT_DATA, INSUFFICIENT_DATA, NOT_AVAILABLE with
metric-specific validity checks. QCS publishes authoritative lifecycle
events.**
